.. Those words were embarrassing?!

 Phainon felt himself instinctually moving his hands to cover his chest against his shirt, bristling at the man who now was looking at him with owl wide eyes. 

“You looked?!”

“Of course,” Mydeimos mumbled after a few moments of staring at Phainon, and Phainon almost could swear he could see the smallest little smile on the necromancer’s lips over Phainon’s horror,  “I had to undress you to make the townsfolk less terrified as I carried you away. I put some clothes over your head, at least.”

.. Undress him.

Undress him?

Mydeimos had to..?

“You.. What do you mean by undress? Surely just m-”

“All of it.” Mydeimos told him as he closed his eyes and waved his hand to the side.

Those words.. Phainon was pretty sure his face would be feeling so very hot with his shame and blood rising to his face if his heart still beat within his chest. 

“H.. How did you carry me?” Phainon asked, feeling the way his chest was tightening in an odd way when he considered Mydeimos carrying him after undressing him.

But Mydeimos only raised a brow over that - shaking his head a little lazily as he waved his hand again before crossing it over his chest. Every movement that necromancer made was one Phainon watched keenly, still on edge as if he would be attacked, even if Mydeimos didn’t appear to be in the mood for such a thing currently..

“Strange line of questioning and worries, but on my back.” Mydeimos told him in a flat tone, already moving to sit back on the floor and open that book yet again. Brows furrowed a little in thought and Phainon really had no idea what that man had thought of so abruptly that he needed to study it right now..

.. Not when Phainon still had so many questions as he dropped his hands away from his chest - breathing out a heavy sigh as he thought about it more.

Mydeimos had allegedly rescued him from being a mindless servant of the undead, and if he believed that.. 

“How long was I unconscious after you saved me?” Phainon asked, recalling the way he had awakened in that foreign bed and been so stunned - his eyes staring off into that doorway and he could only take note of how it seemed as if that was the only bed around here. His eyes searched a little for a second one, and found nothing.

Surely they were not.. Sharing a bed, were they?

Mydeimos didn’t even look away from his book at that, appearing more and more focused on it if anything; “A week or so, but you weren’t growling at me like a wolf with rabies - so I figured it was a good sign of your treatment.”

“What did I do while controlled by him?”

That was enough to make Mydeimos look up from that book again - enough to make him have an odd look on his face that seemed almost in pain as he tried to think of what to say. And that.. That was not a good thing, not something you wanted to see expressed on someone when they were a necromancer. It wasn’t the reaction you wanted to see when the townsfolk had been so terrified of you.

And it was more than enough to make Phainon feel a nauseating wave of nervousness wash over him as he waited for an answer with baited breath. 

“.. Some things are better unknown, Mr Knight.” Was the reply he got however, making his jaw twitch and his hands clench a little as he shook his head slowly.

“My name is Phainon,” Phainon informed him, realizing a bit late that this man probably had never once learned his name or had even been informed of his name. Phainon had just been that to him; a knight that kept showing up. 

Mydeimos only blinked his eyes over that; “Right, some things are better unknown, Phainon.”

Phainon had to stare at the necromancer over that - trying to ignore the way his name was rather.. Cute in a way in Mydeimos’s accent, a rough and grainy feeling to it with Mydeimos’s voice. But soothing in the most bizarre way that he for sure felt as if his cheeks would be heating up if they still had the ability. 

Regardless of whatever that emotion was towards his name being said by the prince, he sighed heavily. 

“Mydeimos, I need to know,” Phainon grumbled out, feeling himself resisting the urge to grit his teeth as he spoke.

Only for Mydeimos to tilt his head to the side innocently. 

“Mydei.”

Mydei.

Something about calling a royal man by a nickname felt as if Phainon should rot away a little, and yet he had to sigh over it. 

“Mydei, I need to know,” Phainon restated, feeling a creeping emotion of dread clawing into him to weigh in belly - hot and curling, cruel in its wake as he tried to watch the way Mydei’s face still seemed to contort over that.

As if even if he did not want to explain this. As if Phainon was asking such a horrible thing that he didn’t even want to be the one to break the news to him, all while Mydei had once been his enemy earlier in life. 

“Are you sure?” Was the simple question Mydei asked, one that he thought he knew the answer to but.. The way that necromancer was acting was making him second guess himself. 

.. But he had to know, the people in his kingdom feared him - and he had to know why, even if it was agony for him to uncover and be informed. He wanted to know why he was a traitor for being loyal to his king, and what the king had done to him if it was not Mydeimos. He had to know, for the sake of the people in town, and himself in the long run. 

“Yes.”

Mydei studied him for a moment all before giving up on that book once more - clearly deeming Phainon the more important subject of his time now as his lips were pulled into a thin line. Unamused, and looking highly unhappy over the topic. 

“You were crowned the ‘King’s Executioner’ formally, and most of the time walked the streets merely cutting down whoever you saw fit that day,” Phainon knew his breath had stopped, a habit he still had been doing regardless of if he even needed to. But those words were enough to make his entire body go numb, standing there and unable to look away from that necromancer as he spoke, “No rhyme or reason, just.. A person a day would be killed by your hands.”

Phainon wasn’t even sure how he was supposed to take that as he found himself only standing in that awful home Mydei lived in - hands trembling just the slightest bit at his side as he tried to steady himself. 

He would never.

He couldn’t even imagine himself killing the people who lived in the kingdom he loved like this; it was unfathomable. 

And yet, those very same people had feared him today - spat insults at him and scurried off as if he were plagued and sowing rot within their homes and hearts. Called the lapdog of the king, and hated as soon as they even caught sight of his existence.

“The streets became unsafe, people started fearing walking the town, most left their homes,” Mydei continued on, explaining in his rather deadpan tone all while sounding a bit quieter - probably because he knew this topic was a bit.. Rough for Phainon to swallow, “Some tried to stand up to you, but it’s rather hard to fight an abomination that feels no pain. No offense.”

Phainon still didn’t reply - not even as Mydei seemed to snap his mouth closed and choose silence between them. 

“What.. Were you doing?” Phainon eventually asked in that lull, desperate to hear that man speak regardless to distract himself from the boiling feeling of unending dread spiraling inside of  him. Something that made him feel as if he could go insane from that alone.

“Most of my time was spent in town trying to research how to stop your onslaught, all while fending off your daily attacks,” Mydei replied without missing a beat - as if he was fully ready to be asked that question as he moved slightly. Enough to look like he was getting more comfortable for the conversation ahead of them - at least, that was what Phainon had been imagining before standing up once more. Stretching a little, all before looking at Phainon again.

“I.. Did that?” Was all Phainon could manage, feeling all of his thoughts spiraling back to that again and again. Fully understanding now that if these words from Mydei were true, he couldn’t even blame the people of the kingdom he loved and cherished so very much hating him more than anything or anyone else.

His eyes instead drooped to his hands, holding them in front of himself to inspect them. Staring at the way they were shaking so horribly, ghostly and as pale as milk - and had been used to murder without a single care in the world.

“No. The man controlling you like a puppet did that I would argue,” Mydei mumbled after a few seconds, but Phainon didn’t dare look away from his hands as he stared at how bloodied they must be for everyone else.

“But they still.. The townsfolk looked at me with such fear,” Phainon countered easily, not willing to look at that necromancer who he had once found at the root of all of his problems. At least, that was what he had assumed. And now he was supposedly a monster who had done even worse things than that fallen prince..?

“.. Your body did slaughter them, but not your heart or mind. Come with me,” Mydei muttered, and Phainon found himself obeying.

He had nothing more to say as he dropped his hands and followed that necromancer in the dim lighting - straining his eyes to focus on that man who seemed to have such a strong stride. Confident in himself and proud, and Phainon was sure he didn’t match that presence at all - not anymore as he followed behind that man silently. 

Right back into that small little space that Phainon had woken up in - blinking as Mydei seemed to snap his fingers to light a candle in an eerie green flame. Something he may have commented on before, but the brightness of it was rather welcomed and he still couldn’t find the words on his  tongue to say anything much.

His mind only returned again and again to those villagers who held so much disdain for him. 

Disgusting lapdog.. Was that all his reputation was now? A monster’s lapdog who barked and played tricks for the man who caused them all endless suffering..?

Phainon’s eyes only watched that necromancer move to that familiar nightstand - the one that Phainon had grabbed onto for dear life upon waking up and retrieving something. 

Only to leave Phainon feeling more and more baffled as he saw that necromancer turn towards him with a bundle of clothes in hand and a shortsword seemingly wrapped in cloth atop of the solid black clothing. A sight that made Phainon feel more and more confused as he tried to digest why he was being handed the items. 

Phainon accepted them with still shaken hands - trying his best to swallow down his unbridled dread as he looked up hollowly from the fabrics to that necromancer, “What is this?”

“Your attire, and a blade.” Mydei explained as if that made much sense, immediately crossing his arms over his chest as he stood just a foot away from Phainon. Clearly not caring how confused those words only made Phainon feel as he waited for a reply, golden eyes searching into blue ones in that flickering light.

Phainon found his mouth opening and closing a few times - resisting the urge to babble in his strange state of mind before sighing loudly. Eyes dropping to those clothes in his hands and staring at that small sword, “Attire..? You’re enforcing a uniform on me?”

“.. It’s enchanted to hide your face when the hood is up, you fool.” Mydei growled out, but Phainon still couldn’t take his eyes away from the weapon that was bundled up on top of those fabrics - one that was foreign to him and so much shorter than what he would prefer. One that seemed hastily given, unplanned, and unaccounted for, “It’s so the town isn’t terrified to see you exist.”

“Where.. Is my sword?” Phainon asked as he darted his eyes upwards to that necromancer, staring him down hard before Mydei only slowly shrugged at him. 

“I don’t know.”

“What do you mean?” Phainon hissed, feeling his teeth grit together as he tried to get every ounce of information from the fallen prince who barely seemed phased by that. A brow raise, but nothing more. 

“You never had it while a zombie lurking the streets,” Mydei offered in a rather quiet tone, “So I don’t know.”

His sword.

The last thing he had left of Cyrene was.. Gone?

Phainon could accept losing his life, but he absolutely couldn’t accept the way he dreaded the fact that a man walking around under the guise of Kephale was using his sword now if he was assuming correctly. Remembering a bit painfully how he had commented on how well of a craft it was as a taunt, something about that made Phainon feel disgusted.

To compliment his sister’s sword, all before using it to kill Phainon.. 

“I need to find it,” Phainon growled out, not even caring much as he moved past Mydei to tear off his own clothes - that were probably also Mydei’s - before putting on the new ones. A tight black shirt with rather loose fitting pants, and a hood that apparently hid his identity. A thing he did in fact check on as he glanced a look into the mirror of that room as he pulled the cowl up - feeling his fingers pause on the edges of it as he stared at the way there was nothing.

Pure abyss looked back at him, black as the night sky with not even a trace of himself. 

“You’re leaving?” Mydei asked finally as Phainon moved past him - not even sparing a second thought for the way Mydei had just been silently standing there watching him. Well, for some reason Phainon had to assume that man had the decency to look away while Phainon was undressing.

Or, at least he hoped so as his feet stopped while passing that man by - hesitating just a shoulders width away as his eyes flickered to meet Mydei’s. Teeth gnashing together uncomfortably in his mouth as he tried to think of what to say.

This man probably didn’t care about his sap story for why he wanted his sword back - even if a part of him debated the idea that Mydei possibly could understand a material possession meaning a lot to him with those gone now. 

“It’s.. Important to me.” Was all Phainon managed to say regardless of if Mydei found his emotions relatable - moving to continue on his walk to leave that cave once more and begin his search of the town hopelessly. A piece of him knowing fully well the answer was in the castle, somewhere, held by some false king that had taken everything from him now. 

Only, Phainon heard steps behind him - those same heavy ones that were precise and steady, enough to make Phainon blink and look at the owner of those footsteps. 

He couldn’t even stop himself from tilting his head to the side - staring at that man rather dumbfoundedly, “What are you doing?” 

“Coming with you. I assume you’re going into town and I need to check on people there,” Mydei replied without fail, looking as if he was bored by that line of questioning, or had just expected it. Either way, Phainon had to sigh over it - he wasn’t exactly sure if he wanted the company of this man, but the people in town had spoken as if they trusted Mydeimos.

.. He had little choice but to assume it was better for himself to make sure that man did in fact come with him. 

“I.. Okay.” Phainon had to give in, shaking his head and looking away from that man as he approached that door he had left through not too long ago - only to pause over Mydei speaking up once more.

“Borrow some of my shoes, please.” 

Phainon froze over that, cocking his head to throw a glare at that man who only seemed genuine in his words. Too genuine, so painfully earnest in his attempt to give Phainon good advice that it only made Phainon sigh and glance at the pairs of shoes he had off to the side awaiting Phainon.

He probably would have growled over it or refused out of spite, if not for the way his feet were so pale.. So sickeningly white and eye-catching that he knew fully well it was another red flag to the living that he was.. Well, not living like them. 

He sighed over that, kicking on those boots he picked out all while feeling those golden eyes burning into his skin. And a piece of him was thankful that he could look right back at the man without him knowing, staring at his face to try to study his mood. To read deeper on the emotions Mydei may show, almost yearning for the looks of annoyance he used to show during their duels.

Yet he found nothing of the sort - sighing instead as he gave up and headed for the exit. 

“Why have you stopped wearing your own outfit to conceal your identity?” He asked as he pushed that shoddy door open, trying his best to start some small talk with that fallen prince.

.. He had a sinking feeling that he would be spending much of his time while dead around this man, at least, if Mydei hadn’t been lying to him.

“The people who live in town stopped fearing me, so who do I have to hide from?” Mydei asked from behind him, and Phainon found himself scoffing over that to instead mess with that rather loose fitting belt on his pants - doing his best to tighten it comfortably around himself. But he couldn’t quite stop his thoughts of thinking this outfit was most likely a hand-me-down from Mydei himself.

Especially with how baggy his pants were, but his shirt was tight around his breasts.. Whatever it was, he had to focus on making that shortsword comfortable on his hip - sighing a little as he did so. 

“The false king?” Phainon offered as they walked, feeling his skin burn over the fact Mydei was behind him. He should feel threatened, make the man walk in front of him for his own safety - but if anything..

He was the one who was already dead, wasn’t he? Mydei was trying to be cautious currently and avoid himself being stabbed through his back like Phainon had been. 

They didn’t need to both have their lives cut short in the same way- not if Mydei was innocent in all of this. Thus, Phainon couldn’t even blame the man for the distrust as he led the way back to Aedes Elysiae with slow steps. 

“He barely even acknowledges I exist, or he merely enjoys my attempts to save those he has doomed,” Mydei explained with a heavy exhale leaving his lips - a dramatic thing considering Phainon could hear it through the cracking of leaves beneath his feet as they walked, “By lessening their suffering I also..”

Mydei trailed off - letting the silence hang heavy in the air and Phainon could only feel the pricks of annoyance working into his mind over that. He needed answers, not for this man to suddenly go quiet with what he knew. 

“Go on,” Phainon prodded, looking over his shoulder with a glare before feeling a little stupid for even doing that - reminding himself that Mydei couldn’t even see his face. He was just glaring to glare and it made no impact on Mydei’s mood or anything else of the sort.

Thus, he snapped his head forward with a heavy sigh that matched Mydei’s previous one in volume.

“I increase the time he gets to toy with their lives and health to feed into himself, assuredly,” Mydei told him in a tired tone - one that made Phainon knit his brows together as he walked through the forest brush. Leading the both of them to that familiar dirt road as he tried to think about those words.

Feeding their health into himself, was that the game the master necromancer was playing with his kingdom? Feeding off them like some kind of fiend of the night? 

“But you cannot just let them suffer?” Phainon offered into the silence after Mydei’s words, doing his best to try to believe that man meant the best for the living. Praying that he truly meant his words and were helping the people of the kingdom, all while he had to bite his tongue and act normal around him.

Maybe it was for the best that they were entering the city together, at least, that way Phainon could try to keep an eye on the necromancer in case he was doing anything too shady and noticeable. 

“Of course not,” Mydei agreed with a scoff from behind Phainon, “I do my best, but it’s a war on two fronts.”

A war on two fronts - Phainon could understand that much as he tutted his tongue a little. Glancing his eyes upwards at the sky above them with a heavy sigh leaving his chest as they walked now. 

“They.. Hide when I come into town.” Phainon confessed, thinking of how they all had said such venomous things about him, full of hatred and despair towards his entire existence when that was.. Nothing he had ever wanted. He had always wanted to help them, and now all he could do was glance a little behind him at that fallen prince behind him.

A red linen shirt, black pants, and a sword on his hip - eyes looking as fiery as ever even if they were off to the side and looking at other things. His posture was as formal as ever, confident and strong, something Phainon almost felt jealous of currently as he looked away from him once more. 

“Naturally, your mindless corpse was hunting them; that’s why I enchanted that cloak for you.”

Phainon wanted to hide away, and those words certainly were not helping his mindset - but he couldn’t blame Mydei. Not really, not when he knew how correct the man was as he led them into town. Besides.. He couldn’t hide away.

He had to face this, their hatred and distrust towards him, their rage and fire, their life that still burnt brightly - Phainon wanted to take in all of it while it was still alive.

“Right..” Was all he could say instead, shaking his head a little at how Mydei had thought that out for him - a step ahead and still.. He let Phainon go to the town and find out the truth himself when he first awoke. He had no idea if that was out of kindness, or just the pure knowledge that Phainon would absolutely be back after just a bit of time when he found out the harsh truth.. And those thoughts made Phainon unsure whether he wanted to laugh or cry. 

Either way, the conversation between them both died out and fizzled into silence as Phainon was left to stew in his thoughts. Dread was the main feeling creeping into him, he still wasn’t sure if this man was being honest - or if he was about to see something horrific and have his own body disobey him as Mydei revealed he held all control over it.

Dread was also there due to the townspeople. He didn’t want them to realize who he was and feel fear, he didn’t want their lives to be harder than it already seemed to have become. Every inch of their journey into the kingdom he had loved all of his life felt as though he was walking into his own damnation. 

Those feelings only worsened as they approached those familiar walls - Phainon’s eyes gazed upon that castle in all of its majesty before lowering again. Focusing instead on the way it had all crumbled so quickly.

Six months.

That felt like too soon for all of this to happen, for the town to be left in disrepair, but.. What did he know? If he had truly been hunting people down daily just to slaughter them, he was sure things had gone wrong in other ways - ways that Mydei just hadn’t informed him of yet. 

And that was haunting as his eyes fell more and more, staring at the floor as he practically waited for Mydei to say he was leaving - or for something to happen to give Phainon some sort of direction.

Nothing made him feel better as he even dared to look around - only fully grasping how dire it seemed to be with the amount of houses that were in ruin already. Windows broken, spider webs creeping into all of the spaces, every single one looked as if it was in an awful state. 

“Mydei!” That happy tone was enough for Phainon’s feet to stop dead in their tracks - eyes only able to stare as a young girl immediately ran up to Mydei with a bubbly laugh leaving her throat as she seemed to circle him like a vulture. 

Phainon looked from her and to where she had appeared from and bolted out of - some sort of back alley and a piece of him was curious if the people moved out of the main street due to him. It would make sense, but he dared not ask such a young child as he instead kept his lips sealed. Merely stopping and waiting for whatever he could glean from their conversation..

“Hello,” Was that necromancer’s stellar response, one that made Phainon feel himself frown heavily over how even to children he was as stoic as ever. 

Not that she seemed to mind as she beamed over that greeting - immediately grabbing onto Mydei’s hand and yanking him along without a care in the world. An action that Phainon merely watched as Mydei seemed to allow himself to be led away by the child who couldn’t possibly be above the age of eight. A sight that made Phainon bite back a chuckle, only before feeling somewhat wistful.

It hadn’t been too long ago that this was his life, engaging with the children who were fond of him being a knight and messing with his armor - only now the child was dragging a prince along as if he were a muzzled pet cat.

“Will you play with us today?” The girl asked, not even caring about whatever reply Mydei had up his sleeves as she continued yanking him away - apparently towards a house in specific that Phainon was unfamiliar with. Saying no words as he followed behind the two of them, feeling less than any desire to speak up currently. 

“Apologies, no. I’m looking for your aunt, how is she doing?” Mydei answered in that same tone, and Phainon had to keep himself from clicking his tongue over how stiff the man seemed - though.. A part of him almost thought it was due to Phainon being there. Golden eyes kept flicking to him almost nervously, as if something about Phainon watching had him on edge or anxious.

That seemed shady in itself, but Phainon didn’t dare to comment on it as he instead silently followed behind - eyes narrowed over how happy the girl seemed regardless of Mydei’s stiffness in the situation.

“Still in bed! Who is this?” The girl asked, all while throwing a look over her shoulder while her hands remained holding onto Mydei - making Phainon give her a warm smile. One that after a moment of no reaction, made him remember she certainly couldn’t see it. 

.. Nor did she want to, and that bitter knowledge was enough to make Phainon’s smile fade immediately as she jerked her head back to the front. 

“A friend,” Mydei mumbled, but Phainon found himself unconvinced of that sort of description from Mydei - luckily, the child didn’t seem to pick up the flicker of disdain in Mydei’s word as he explained that. 

“He looks so spooky with that hood on! It’s just pure black!” The girl said with a quiet little giggle, sounding as if it was almost a bother for her - but humorous in some sort of way that Phainon couldn’t quite make any sense of. 

“Sorry,” Phainon choked out, doing his best to sound as friendly as possible as his fingers twitched at his side. Wishing he could take it off to make her happier, but fully knowing the sight of himself would only terrify her.

.. Sickening. This level of uselessness made him feel sick to his core.

“It’s okay!” She chirped out, but she didn’t even look at Phainon - no, those words were spoken to Mydei as if it were to comfort him of all people. And Phainon couldn’t wrap his mind around the situation as he moved closer to Mydei - taking on the other side of the man with a heavy scoff leaving his chest. 

“We’re just following a child?” Phainon growled out, ignoring the way she seemed so happy over this situation - her small hands holding onto Mydei’s large hand without a care in the world. 

Mydei gave him an odd look at that - one that looked almost perturbed as if he couldn’t understand why on earth Phainon found this scenario to be odd; “.. Yes? She obviously knows me, what’s the issue?”

.. What was the issue?

Where was Phainon to start? From the fact that this girl was just openly holding the hand of a necromancer, or the fact that she was more comfortable holding his hand than she ever would with Phainon who was supposed to be a knight protecting her.

.. Phainon didn’t know up from down anymore, closing his eyes and letting himself fall a step behind as he ignored the sharp gaze of that fallen prince. 

“I.. I don’t know.” Phainon murmured as he did so, doing his best to tell himself that was it.

This man was a prince at his core, even if he had allegedly done such horrible things, there was no way to wash the blood away that ran through his veins. A prince through and through, and to any child, a prince was a marvel in themself.

.. Let alone one that was as pretty as Mydeimos, but that was neither this nor that currently. 

He silently followed after them - all before they neared a house that looked.. Significantly less in disrepair than those on the main road, off and in a corner but there was something different about this area. A hum of life that seemed to resonate beneath it - voices around there, distant, but voices meant people which meant hope wasn’t completely lost.

Not yet. 

“Pardon the intrusion,” Mydei said as he followed after that girl into the house - and Phainon didn’t have to wait long to find out why he heard that as he slowly moved to the entryway as well. Pausing a little before a new voice sounded much too excited. 

“Mydeimos! You’re never intruding, come in, come in!” That happy voice sounded off - audible to Phainon even as he timidly found himself waiting outside, slowly entering to let his eyes adjust to the dim lighting - glancing around the small house.

Homey - warm and inviting, the disparity between the inside of it and the outside surroundings felt like a confusing night and day between them. 

“How are you doing today?” Mydei asked, pausing in that small kitchen and doorway to barely give Phainon any room - and Phainon had half of his mind to ask where the child had run off to, but he felt it better he remain a wallflower for now. 

“I’ve been well! Your medicine has done wonders for my aches in my joints!” The woman answered as she moved around that small kitchen - immediately digging through her cabinets for a rather large parchment paper, “I’ve also acquired those blueprints you requested.”

Those words made Phainon grit his teeth - unsure of what ‘blueprints’ a necromancer could possibly ever need..

“Are these the correct ones? They were practically ancient, but it’s the floor plan of the castle alright.” The woman explained as she began to unfurl that piece of paper and lay it down on the table - words that instantly drew Phainon’s attention, and a map that made him raise a brow as he moved a little bit closer.

Only, she seemed to have finally realized he was there when he became more curious over that; “Who is this?”

Mydei was silent for a moment at that - his own eyes staring at the yellowed and fraying parchment that had been laid out on the woman’s rickety kitchen table before his eyes slid slowly. Looking straight at Phainon before shaking his head a little. 

“A helper with the necromancer issue,” Mydei explained, all before his eyes moved back to that map to study the layout of it - a layout that Phainon felt like he should know more than that man as his own eyes tried to take it in.

Old, this layout was very old - probably even ancient with some of the rooms and their uses being outdated, but it wasn’t wrong. The floorplan was arguably the same - even if just a bit jumbled up. 

“Oh!” The woman explained, nodding just a few times before she slowly made her way closer to Mydei - voice dropping a little,  “Is he.. You know..?”

Phainon found himself looking away from those drawings, blinking at the woman who had no idea he was staring at her - all before Mydei huffed out  a quiet little laugh. 

“Dead? Yes,” Mydei replied, as flat as ever and that.. That made Phainon cock his head to the side as he stared over how open he was being currently. 

“They.. Know you’re a necromancer?”

Mydei’s eyes moved to him with those words - jaw looking a bit tight as if the question was a bother, all before the woman spoke first. 

“We didn’t originally! Just a man investigating our town in the shadows! But as time went on and the king became more and more deranged with his new orders and laws it became obvious something was wrong,” She explained with a little sigh, her hand moving upwards to tuck white locks of hair behind her ear slowly,  “Days were terrifying, yet Mydeimos showed up time and time again to try to aid us all while hiding away from us.”

Phainon had to blink at that, for once idly wondering how old this woman was if her hair was already graying - she seemed to be in decent shape but.. It was worrying, were only old folks left behind? Surely not, that child earlier was so young..?

“.. Please excuse me while I see to your sister,” Mydei spoke after a moment, excusing himself to immediately duck into a different room and Phainon found himself staring after that man - straining his ears to hear him stepping up to a second floor. 

At least, if Phainon’s ears were hearing it correctly as he blinked and looked at that woman who was smiling so warmly at him - not at all appearing bothered by the fact she now was aware Phainon was merely a living husk in her home.

.. Was their trust in Mydeimos truly so high that even his armies of the undead were welcomed guests in their lives?

“Anyway, It felt a bit silly to not invite him in,” She continued on, putting a hand on her hip as she kept that smile on her lips, “Only to later learn he’s a necromancer, what a scary thing to learn!”

Phainon found himself unable to understand those words - instead merely staring at her as he puzzled over it; “.. You still trusted him regardless?”

“Why not? By then the king was surrounding himself with zombies of his own,” The woman countered with a little laugh, shaking her head as she instead began to flatten that mess of blueprints all over again. An action that Phainon found himself nervously watching - curious if it was all truly for that fallen prince. 

He shouldn’t allow this information to be spread around - the documents of their kingdom and its layout were private, something that you didn’t want to be out and in the air.

And yet..

He could only sigh. 

“What if.. The king is controlled by Mydeimos?” Phainon asked, looking at her for the answers and desperately wanting to know what she truly felt about that idea since.. Phainon had been dreading it.

“Hmm,” She nodded at him, as if she completely understood his angle of asking,  “Using us as test subjects? He’s talked a bit about his home kingdom, but they said the fall of that kingdom happened in a span of a mere few days, I’m not sure he even has the heart for it.”

Phainon found himself biting into his lips over that - he wasn’t even sure if she was being truthful with him, or was merely lying due to assuming he would run to Mydei and tell him of his treachery. Whatever the case may be, Phainon had to fight the way his face was twitching over that reply he was given; “He has the heart to raise the dead.. But you don’t question if he would torture you all?”

“I don’t know,”  She admitted immediately, and that felt as though Phainon had been punched as his jaw went slack - watching the way she seemed to hum and go about her business, all before throwing Phainon such a kind smile; “You’re the first zombie I’ve seen around him and you seem rather polite.”

“That’s.. A lot of trust to put in him..” Phainon said as he trailed off, not even fully sure if he himself could have such confidence in that man. He couldn’t even fully say if the way he had acted before was under the control of Mydei, forced to slaughter his precious people who lived in the kingdom, or if it was truly under the control of the king.

“Maybe,” She admitted once more, making him jerk his eyes to her confusedly - feeling baffled over the way he was merely agreeing to such a thing,  “But we’re hopeless otherwise.”

Hopeless.

That was a driving force behind them trusting him so easily? What else did that have to lose mentality?

.. Phainon didn’t like that at all, feeling that wave of sickness wash over him that he was utterly powerless to dispel as he looked at her, keenly watching her as she seemed to have more to say on the topic.

“What chance do we have when the healthy have long since left and most of the young left when their families began to get sick as well? That and the traitorous lapdog of a knight who hunted us down for fun,” The woman gave a brittle laugh over that - vibrant green eyes flicking upwards to look at Phainon’s own, at least, where she assumed his were, “I’ll take my chances with the man who has been trying to heal us, even if in the end he was a liar. The betrayal would hurt less than the plagues have.”

Ah.

Phainon found himself unable to conjure a reply to that - instead remaining silent as he watched her only seem to suffer around and organize those papers for Mydeimos even more. Almost nervously, as if she was eager for him to have them and..

Phainon couldn’t blame her; if he was trying to use these to end the crimes of that false king, it made sense that everyone in the kingdom would be standing behind Mydei and doing their best to support the fallen prince.

“Who else do we have to turn to, anymore?”

Phainon wished he could say himself - wished that he could be something more, wished that he could protect them, wished that he could be a beam of light and hope in their life.

.. But that was already Mydei, wasn’t it? And all he could do was the same thing they were doing; try to support that man that was once his enemy foolishly. 

Phainon found himself sighing, letting his shoulders sink a little as his eyes only returned to those parchments languidly to roam over them once again; “.. I see, I’m sorry.”

“Bah.. Like I need the dead to apologize to me!” The woman laughed out - waving her hand dismissively but..

Phainon had to choke a little over that, over how he had caused more deaths by his own hands - and now he was being told he had nothing to apologize for. That wasn’t true. 

“That’s s-”

“Hello,” Mydei interrupted as he walked back into that small kitchen, making Phainon’s mouth snap shut instead of uttering the words he was going to dare say. Instead looking at him and watching the way the woman practically flickered back to life - looking so excited over seeing Mydei that Phainon.. Couldn’t possibly interrupt it.

All he could do was remain quiet, and fall into his role of holding these secrets close to his chest - huh?

“Welcome back Mydeimos!” The woman happily stated, looking much too happy and Mydei..

Mydei only immediately moved to that table again - between Phainon and the older looking woman to stare at those blueprints laid out there. 

“I need to leave now, do you mind if I take this with me?” Mydei swiftly said, eyes dipping from those papers and to the woman - obviously ignoring Phainon but Phainon.. Didn’t mind that much.

A piece of him was rather used to staying silent in scenarios like this - allowing royalty to do their dealings and important meetings all while he stayed off to the side. Watching, protecting, keenly aware of everything as his eyes only watched that man speak with this unknown woman.

The smallest of smiles on his lips as he looked at her - warm and inviting, one that would reassure anyone given how strong Mydei was outside of that. Hands that seemed much too gentle as they moved, calloused and well practiced, yet having a bit of tenderness that was bizarre to Phainon’s mind as he watched him touch those ancient papers. 

“Go ahead, I found them for you anyway.” The woman replied with a wave of her hand, and Phainon only remained watching as Mydei quickly obeyed and picked up those papers - stuffing them into his shirt with a swiftness that Phainon found almost alarming. 

“Thank you,” Mydei nodded, all before cutting Phainon a little look - one that didn’t say much, yet Phainon found his mind puzzling over it, “Come on.”

“Have a good day, you two!” The woman called after as Mydei strode past Phainon and out the door, making Phainon’s thoughts struggle even more as he moved to follow after him. Just.. Before pausing to give her a small little wave to her happily. 

“You as well!”

And with that he followed the oddly grumpy seeming prince suddenly - a piece of him wanted to question the man as he hurried to catch up to him. Only to be caught off guard as Mydei gave him a look as he fell in line behind Mydei - a glance over his shoulder that seemed expectant. 

“I assume you wanted to find your sword, yes?”

His sword.

Phainon’s eyes dipped down to his own hip, looking at the sword that had taken the spot of his true sword - the one he cherished so dearly and it now was missing.

.. But did such a material thing matter more than the issues of these people? He didn’t think so, currently he wanted to know more and more behind their trust and faith in Mydei. 

“.. Originally, yes, but..” Phainon had to think about his words, feeling a bit choked when he remembered how earnest she was - how much hope and faith she obviously had in this man as he followed after Mydei leisurely, “Their trust in you..”

Phainon looked at that man over that - watching the way Mydei seemed to study him for a moment before flicking his eyes forward. Something about it made Phainon feel like he had expected to be asked about this - or maybe he had just heard their talk while upstairs.

Whatever it was, Mydei shrugged his shoulders a bit lazily as he continued moving. 

“It’s easy to trust an outsider when your king has cut off all contact with the outside world and the other kingdoms,” Mydei explained with a quiet hum leaving his throat,  “And.. The plagues and such.”

“They look at you like you are their savior,” Phainon choked out, feeling more and more insane as he remembered how soft and kind the woman was - how entranced she almost seemed by Mydei being there for even the briefest of moments.

As if he were her hero. 

Mydei paused at that; his steps failing as he instead turned a little on heel to look at Phainon, tilting his head to the side as he moved to cross his arms over his chest with a deep exhale sounding in the silence as Phainon stopped as well. 

“I’m merely doing what I could not for my own people,” Mydei explained, his eyes boring into Phainon’s soul as if he couldn’t even understand the way this was being brought up to him, “Would you not do the same if you were in my shoes?”

Ah..

He would.

Even if it was Kremnos or another kingdom, if Aedes Elysiae was all destroyed with not a soul left like Mydei’s home.. He would have chased that man down to the ends of the earth just like Mydei, aided whoever he could, all while doing his best to get revenge. 

And as Phainon stood in that empty town that was once bustling with life and joy, a hum of sanctuary and home - he knew that it was still the path that called to him. 

“As for your sword, I suspect it’s still in the castle som-”

“I don’t need it right now,” Phainon interrupted, studying the way Mydei seemed caught off guard by that - jaw snapping shut as he instead looked at Phainon, a brow raising to his hairline as he stood there. All before golden eyes dipped away, looking around at the broken houses that surrounded them - but Phainon didn’t copy.

His eyes stayed fixed on that fallen prince who suddenly seemed a little bit antsy as he looked back at Phainon finally. 

Mydei gave him an odd look at that - head tilting even more to the side as he tried to make sense of what was being said to him; “.. You said it was important to you.”

It was - No, it is.. Phainon treasured that sword so very much, and yet.. He could only clench and unclench his hands into fists - breathing out a heavy sigh as he copied the man. Opting to look away from him in favor of looking at his poor home and what had become of it. The distant rumbles of people talking were there, but there was no laughter.

No joy and life of the merchants haggling in the streets, no children running through the very same streets and causing a ruckus, nothing but the quiet murmurs now. A raging fire of life that had died out to mere embers, and somehow - Phainon had aided in snuffing out the lives he cherished so painfully much.

That was enough to make him believe he didn’t need his sword back - not yet. 

“The.. The people will only fear me if they recognize that sword, and it won’t look good for you to be befriending the knight that killed their friends.” Phainon explained instead, blinking a worried look to the man in front of him even though he knew fully well that Mydei couldn’t see it at all. Not through the cowl he himself had enchanted for Phainon’s anonymity. 

“Oh? The knight is caring for my wellbeing? How sweet,” Mydei laughed out a bit softly, all before rolling his eyes over it - as if he was teasing as well. 

.. That made sense, considering Phainon the entire time had been doubting Mydei in more than one way. 

Phainon had to sigh over it, watching the way Mydei straightened himself out and dropped his hands from his chest - as if giving up on studying Phainon very much.

All to which Phainon felt nervousness prick at his skin - a tiny bit anxious as he tried to gauge Mydei’s mood as he looked at that man, “I’m.. Sorry, I think.”

“‘You think’?” Mydei echoed, appearing more confused than Phainon had expected him to be, which made Phainon shuffle his weight between his feet with a little sigh escaping him.

“Well, I just mean..” Phainon trailed off - not even sure how he was supposed to apologize for the weeks of throwing insults to Mydei, only to be horribly wrong about him. He felt unwell every single time he thought of those insults and how now, they fit him better than they ever had fit Mydei.

He was the one who had been slaughtering his loved ones - ending their lives coldly with his own hands. And Mydei.. Had never hurt his family or kingdom, he had never done anything that had been accused of him, at least, that was what Phainon had to believe now with how the people still here thought so highly of Mydeimos. 

He had been such a fool; and now he wasn’t even sure how to apologize proficiently over it. 

“It’s fine, I don’t hold a grudge towards nippy dogs.” Mydei told him anyways, not seeming like he particularly minded as he shook his head with a heavy sigh. One that made Phainon feel beyond insane as his mouth fell agape - floundering a little before he tilted his head to the side. 

“Huh?”

“They call you the lapdog of the king, and you truly always were that,” Mydei explained as he turned on heel with a lazy hand wave - seeming as though it was the most logical thing in the world that he was now explaining, “Loyal and trusting, even if it was to the very man who killed you in the end of it all.”

Phainon couldn’t even stop the way his feet began moving on their own after that man, following him as if he was made to do that without question. Biting into his own gums between his lips over how at home he felt doing such a thing, as well, to follow behind a prince was.. Somehow, his calling. 

“Don’t apologize to me, you already died a shameful death and were abused in the afterlife. Just focus on atoning with the people you actually harmed,” Mydei grumbled out, sounding less than amused as he told Phainon to do such a thing - yet Phainon’s mind was still lagging behind. Struggling to even understand that simple advice. 

Phainon had to grit his teeth, doing his best to resist the urge to comb his fingers through his hair a bit nervously, “Is.. It possible to repent for such crimes?”

Mydei didn’t even stop at that, only giving a quiet little sighing noise over the question - as if he had somehow expected to be asked that, “No, but you have to figure out some way to rest easily with how you died, and what was cursed upon you in undeath, or you may be here forever.”

Expected the question, or he himself was always wondering about Phainon’s fate as well - one way or another, Phainon felt his stomach drop with those words being said to him so casually. 

“Is that.. How this curse works?” Phainon asked as he only continued slowly following that man, unable to stop the way he felt as though his throat was closing in on itself nervously - and he almost thought his heartbeat would be pounding out of his chest if it still functioned. 

“Not sure,” Mydei admitted, pausing a little to look at Phainon again - his feet halting once more to turn to Phainon just a little, “But it’s a start, isn’t it?”

“Where are you going now?” Phainon asked, unable to stop himself from finally asking all while his mind was puzzling over how he had so earnestly replied with ‘not sure’.

What hope was there for Phainon if even the necromancer himself had no idea how to help him rest peacefully?

.. Phainon found himself sinking into dread, only looking at Mydei for answers to it, or a helping hand that the fallen prince himself seemed to lack. 

“.. To the garden,” Mydei replied after a few moments of silence, all before he flicked an egregious gaze towards Phainon - studying him all before raising a brow, “You don’t have to follow me, you know?”

Of course he knew that - his hands were restless for answers however, and on the other side.. 

“I.. I wouldn’t know where to go otherwise,” Phainon admitted as he followed after that necromancer who had begun to walk away again - staring at the back of Mydei’s head as he swiftly followed after him like a lost dog.

A place and destination in mind, and Phainon found himself feeling jealous over even that as he now felt as though.. He had neither of those types of things to speak of anymore. He didn’t know where his feet would lead him in the end, nor was he even sure of his destination; and the only clue he had was this man now who he was chasing after hopelessly. 

“I see,” Mydei replied, all before he made an odd humming noise - as if thinking over those words a little, “No family to check on?”

Family.

What an ironic thing for Mydei to be wondering about, considering Phainon felt as though he had no right to talk about family with this man. 

“No, they died years ago.” Was what Phainon replied coldly, dipping his eyes away to instead blink at cracked marble beneath his feet instead. Teeth gnashing into his lips nervously as he tried to bite back the bile that was stirring in his chest in regret of how he had treated this man. 

All feelings he had never expected to feel in regards to the ‘Kremnoan’s Last Prince’.

“Sorry,” Mydei immediately apologized, and that was enough to make Phainon’s mind pause over those words - remembering throughout all the times they had met and fought, all the times he had yelled venom at the necromancer.

.. The fact Mydei’s own family had died so recently and horribly, completely slaughtered and Phainon had assumed it was at the hands of Mydei himself.

“Don’t.. Apologize to me, Mydei,” Phainon found himself choking out - doing his best to try to shake his thoughts of how cruel he had truly been to Mydei in the long run of it all. 

With how much these people loved and trusted Mydei, the fact he had mocked him in the form of being angry that Kremnos fell to his hands.. There were words he could never take back, and yet, he wished he could. 

“About your family?” Mydei innocently inquired further about that, clearly not understanding why Phainon suddenly would refuse apologies from the man he had once blamed for so very much.

“In general.. Didn’t you know? Royalty shouldn’t grovel before their knights,” Phainon chuckled as he uttered those words - a joke, and yet.. Phainon somewhat knew deep down he meant it, his own head felt dizzied, confused, and dazed over the fact his king had betrayed him to such an extent - and now he was following this prince around who had all the traits of being a good king.

Gentle and understanding with the common people to the point of Phainon feeling like he already was his knight. 

Or maybe Phainon just didn’t see any other purpose in his life outside of being a knight.. Or in his undeath. 

“Kremnoans never took royal knights,” Mydei however spoke, easily making him blink his thoughts away and focus on that man who seemed less than amused over the idea of it, “Too many chances for betrayal when you’re most vulnerable, thus I-”

“I’m loyal and trusting, I hear,” Phainon cut in with a small smile, watching the way Mydei’s eyes immediately jerked to him - staring at him with the slightest quirk in his lips before he shook his head rather deliberately. 

“.. Right, and willing to interrupt royalty it seems.” Mydei snarkily said, rolling his eyes a little. 

“I’m not your knight, thus I can be rude in the presence of royalty if I want,” Phainon waved it off, shrugging his shoulders with a smile on his lips. 

Something about teasing this man felt more at home, not as cruel and harsh as before when they were enemies - but something lighter. More friendly, more welcoming, something that felt oddly more at home in Phainon’s soul when he considered it more. 

“Years of training for being a polite knight gone in an instant, huh?”

Mydei’s voice was teasing - light and soft in a way that was almost foreign for Phainon to hear as he was much too used to this man growling at him while trying to parry his attacks.

Something about it made Phainon’s chest burn, a curling sensation in the depths of his own emotions as he tried to figure it out, but all he could do was manage a scoff - knitting his brows together over those words after a few moments. 

“Well! When you get a blade shoved and twisted in your back by the king you swore to serve, you kind of don’t have fond feelings for royalty anymore!”

Mydei stared at him with those words, all before that smile faded from his mouth and he looked back to watch where he was walking instead; “.. I see.”

Solemn.

That was the odd emotion Mydei gave off now as he spoke those words and appeared to avoid Phainon’s eye contact - and Phainon couldn’t tell if it was for Phainon’s death, or the fact he was one of the ‘royalty’ in question.

.. Phainon had to assume the former, considering they had never exactly been friends, anyway.

“You sound sad now,” Phainon teased with a quiet chuckle, still watching the way Mydei seemed to be avoiding looking at him, “Did you want m-”

“I don’t care, I’ve no kingdom nor people of my own. I’m no actual prince, not anymore,” Mydei interrupted, but something about that seemed a little.. Off. Disheartening, in a way that Phainon couldn’t put into words as his feet slowed the tiniest of bits to fall behind Mydei’s strut. 

Phainon wasn’t sure what to make of that, nor did he know exactly why he felt.. Bad, for that either. He truly meant those words, at least.. He thought he did, but as he blinked at the back of that man’s fiery golden hair - he found his thoughts a bit more jumbled in regards to him being a prince.

That was something Phainon had mocked and hissed over before, getting jabs in over the prince killing his entire kingdom, but as it stood Phainon wasn’t sure if Mydei was guilty anymore. A thing he once thought was as obvious as night as day, was now a blurry and confusing topic to think of when he remembered his own sword in his back and ‘Kephale’ informing him Kephale was dead.

“You know, I’m actually looking for a new j-”

“Good evening, Mydeimos!” 

Phainon’s jaw snapped shut at that, instead watching the way Mydei’s steps halted as an old lady seemed to be approaching them at a languid pace. Phainon could only move a bit from behind Mydei, doing his best to blink at her in mute wonder - he had never met many of the elders of town. 

They didn’t used to go out and mingle, naturally, so seeing one leaving her home just with the intentions of speaking to Mydei made him feel a bit baffled. 

“Hello,” Mydei used that same blunt greeting again to the old woman - whose eyes only looked back and forth between the duo. Appearing not at all bothered by Phainon’s hooded visage at all, and he had to assume that was due to how Mydei had concealed himself originally around them as well..

“And you’ve brought a friend.. How delightful,” She nodded as she waved a hand, clearly motioning for the two of them to follow after her. 

“You can ignore him, “ Mydei immediately hissed out, making Phainon just a bit aware he may have said something a bit wrong a few moments before - all while Mydei carried on, “I’m just here to check on my weeds.”

“.. Weeds?” Phainon quoted out, but Mydei didn’t even acknowledge his existence as he still continued to walk after that old woman. And Phainon could only exhale deeply as he followed after them.

He had half of his mind to go to that castle and search yet..

His eyes moved to the side - looking up at the majestic marble buildings that spiraled to the heavens, a testament to how far their small farming kingdom had once come. Now the rest of the city was crumbling, decaying as if a war had been fought here and it was only aided with his own hands. A feeling that made him stand there and blink at the sight, eyes narrowing as he tried to think it through.

He couldn’t just march in there - not as he remembered how odd those guards had been, how all of them had lost their personalities and never spoke to him anymore.

.. Had he been the only last human alive in that castle, kept there as a toy for that necromancer to laugh at and mock? How many of the dead were now lurking those halls to protect the man sapping the kingdom of its strength and lifeforce? 

He didn’t even pay attention as the woman eventually left them - no longer talking to Mydei as they walked and allowed the both of them their privacy together.

.. For some reason.

And Phainon’s eyes found their way to watch as Mydei took a knee - something that made him catch his breath over how a prince should never be doing that. How it was improper of him, and yet, the blond haired man didn’t even bat an eye over it. Instead fully settling into the mud to mess with some flowers.

Beautiful, as crimson as Mydei’s markings on his skin - all while bleeding into a hue of lavender. Regrettably, Phainon had zero knowledge involving what flowers were and their meanings and uses. The most he had ever learned were what mushrooms he could eat while away from home to make do in life - and even still he had eaten the wrong ones a few times and had.. Eventful nights. 

Not that he would ever tell anyone about the time he got naked and slept in the farmer’s hay, of course, that was between him and the cow that woke him up in the morning. 

“What are these?” Phainon asked as he hunched down a little - just enough to blink at the flowers and wait for a reply. 

“They’re poisonous,” Mydei answered flippantly, still focusing wholly on his work in favor of looking at Phainon - probably due to the fact that gardening required precision that Phainon knew nothing about.

What he did know about, however, was the fact there were children here - making his jaw go rigid as he made a shocked and baffled noise, “And you planted them by the-”

“They’ve been fine so far,” Mydei cut in, borderline hissing as his amber eyes shot a glare to Phainon - sharp enough to make him snap his mouth shut, but not enough to easily dispel his worries. 

Phainon had to give him a strange worried look over that, feeling his face knit together as he tried to get answers from Mydei, “What if you hurt someone?”

“.. They will be fine, I promise.” Mydei told him in a tired tone, already standing and walking away from Phainon and those plants - a movement that made Phainon nervously look at those plants..

.. All before trusting in the man, in more ways than merely one, and deciding to walk away from them - leaving them there to instead follow after that necromancer. 

“Where are we going now?” Phainon asked as he fought back a smile over the prospect of being by the necromancer’s side - feeling himself oddly a bit too eager to be with him.

All before Mydei paused to look at him - turning on heel with a bizarre and baffled expression on his face; “‘We’?”

“Well.. Yes? I’m going to help you kill the necromancer,” Phainon explained as he tilted his head to the side - very aware of the way Mydei couldn’t see the smile on his lips as he spoke, “The false king one, to be specific.”

Mydei, however, oddly didn’t reply to that. His amber and gold flaked eyes only remained staring at Phainon, as if he was trying to read deeper into the knight's words while furrowing his brows together. Obviously, a little bit stunned over how easily Phainon was giving into this situation and offering to work with Mydei and well..

That made sense, really, considering how blurry and foggy Phainon’s memories were. He really was feeling as though he shouldn’t make this decision so quickly - but what other option did he have when the townspeople respected Mydei so much?

“Don’t give me the silent treatment. The civilians really seem to trust you, meanwhile they.. Don’t feel that way towards me at all,” Phainon explained before moving to put a hand on his hip with a wave of his free hand, sighing loudly over it,  “It’s a good option for both of us.”

“Is it?” Mydei immediately asked - making Phainon’s eyes dart to him to study him now. 

His tone of voice was bordering annoyed, but there was something more beneath it - a flicker of anxiousness in a way that Phainon couldn’t quite comprehend. As if Mydei was dreading Phainon snooping around more, or finding something out.

.. But that was all the more reason for Phainon to stay close to him; to figure out all of his secrets and make sure the necromancer was doing just as he said, and nothing more. To keep him on a tight leash and make sure he truly had no hand in the foul play happening in either of their kingdoms.

Phainon could accomplish at least that much. 

“You seem lonely, Mr. Prince,” Phainon teased, doing his best to lean forward a little as he grinned at that man.

Only for Mydei’s brows to harshen, lowering into a scowl as he seemed to process those words in real time between the two of them. 

“It’s best not to assume things, Mr. Knight,” Mydei growled out - appearing less and less happy with every word he uttered on this topic,  “And I told you before, I’m no prince.”

“Mm,” Phainon straightened himself out at that, doing his best to study the mood change that had abruptly happened in Mydei but.. He didn’t know the man well enough to be able to say why that was, not yet, at least, “But you’re not necromancer-y at all, you still fit into that prince title easily.”

Phainon couldn’t help himself but moved his free hand to tap at his chin slowly - looking at the way Mydei still seemed to not desire to comment on this. But that was fine, Phainon was more than a little used to not getting replies or having to earn them from his line of work in life. 

“Correct posture while walking, incredibly formal and blunt to the townsfolk, the attempts at stoicness, and the familiar feeling of being impressed when seeing you,” Phainon began to list out the easy things - noticeable by eyes alone, “Not very necromancer-y.”

Not to mention Mydei’s personality.

Something about it was much too welcoming, willing to be upfront and honest - nothing about that gave the impression of a necromancer, but it had all the tellings of his past as royalty and doing his best for his people while at meetings. A mark that he couldn’t quite wipe away, much like those crimson tattoos that told anyone the truth of where he came from - royalty or not, Kremnos had left its mark on him. 

“.. You talk a lot for a knight,” Was all Mydei grumbled after a few moments of his expression flickering between his moods, as if he couldn’t quite make up his mind if he was truly allowed by this all or not. 

Either way, he shuffled his feet slightly - enough to be noticeable as his eyes dipped away for the briefest of moments. A look that made Phainon wonder if the prince was feeling.. Shy?

Was that it? Embarrassed and shy? 

“Yes. Anyway, can’t help but notice you haven’t accepted or declined my aid yet,” Phainon instead opted to change the topic - not exactly desiring that prince to worm his way away from this topic.

And it seemed to work as those eyes found their way back to throwing a piercing and haunting stare at Phainon - as if he hadn’t expected that to be brought up. Especially when Mydei’s jaw twitched a little, tightening and moving just a tad as he tried to figure out what to say to that and Phainon.. Almost felt nervous as he waited for that reply.

He had no clue where to start, otherwise, if this man declined his company. 

“Your aid would be appreciated,” Mydei flatly told him, giving nothing more away about any deeper feelings on the matter - and Phainon didn’t even know why he was hoping for more from the man.

What answer had he hoped for outside of him agreeing? Why had he almost hoped that Mydei would be more energetic about it instead of staring at him egregiously and speaking in that same stoic and respect-demanding tone that he seemed so settled into every moment of his life?

.. Why was Phainon hoping for more from Mydei..?

Phainon had to laugh over that - trying his best not to think about those feelings inside of himself for too long instead, “Wow.. So honest.”

“You know that castle better than I ever could by just studying the design of it through this scroll,” Mydei explained flippantly - making Phainon bite into his lips just a little. 

He understood that, they were both just means to an end, so why did he oddly feel a bit.. Saddened over that? As if that logical explanation of how useful Phainon would be for Mydei had  wounded him in some sort of way, all while he knew he should merely be happy that he was at least deemed useful to the fallen prince..?

Was it truly just his soul being too used to working under royalty like Mydeimos, or was there something more irksome creeping into Phainon more and more with every single second he stayed around Mydei?

“What’s your plan?” Phainon asked with a choked tone itching into his throat - burning him a little as he did his best to move on from that topic and his own thoughts. 

He didn’t know his own plans, or how to get to where he wanted to go - he wasn’t even sure how to actually handle being dead now that he seemed trapped in this new situation.

Only, Mydei didn’t appear to know either; “Eventually to kill him. How I get to that result has been the inquiry for months.”

Right.. 

Phainon had to shrug over that anyway - it’s not like he himself knew exactly how to get to that destination either, not when it was once his job to.. Well.. Do the opposite of just that. His life was dedicated to protecting his king, and now in death he had to kill him?

“I’m growing fond of that plan,” Phainon huffed out as his eyes moved back to the decaying city around them - hesitating just a little as he took note of those red stains on the tiles and the lack of life as they were now almost on the main street again.

A lack of life that was Phainon’s fault, in his own mind or not, they would always assume it was his own hands that had chosen to do that to them. And nothing he did now could undo that, right?

“Can you even do it?”

Phainon found his mind stalling at that - moving his eyes back to that prince who was only staring right back at him.

There was no amusement, no teasing, no hints of this being some kind of jest in any form - Mydei sounded as if he was in utter disbelief. As if he was actually holding distrust, and the fact that distrust was towards Phainon made him feel just a little insane. 

Phainon was the one that should be feeling that towards Mydei, not the other way around, right..?

Phainon had to open his mouth at that, all before closing it as he relaxed his posture, instead tilting his head to the side confusedly; “..Pardon?”

“If you had to raise your sword against the man who you swore your life to, could you do it?” Mydei asked without missing a single beat - copying Phainon even as he tilted his head to the side a little and sending blond locks of hair across his own face messily. 

A sight that Phainon would have almost found endearing, if not for the way his mind was still stuck wondering about that question.

Could he raise his sword against the man he had served every single day of his life? The man that he had trusted so very much, only to find himself at the end of his own sword and having his life stolen from him by presumably that man? 

.. Phainon didn’t actually know, but he did know one thing as he laughed a little over the question. 

“I.. Well, I’m not exactly alive anymore to have a life to give him, now am I?” 

It was a fair point, he had sworn his life to that man while living - that was true, but now he had no life to give. He was dead and decaying, cursed to walk the earth once more by a man as some sort of mockery - and all he could do was try to make amends now.

Though, Mydei’s lip seemed to quirk a little over that - an unreadable emotion as he straightened his posture back out before crossing his arms over his chest with a heavy sigh. 

“No, I suppose you are not.”

Phainon couldn’t help himself - his words spilling from his lips before he even had a chance to rethink them; “Well! I swore one king my loyalty in life, what if this fallen knight swore to a fallen prince as well?”

And the silence that followed after was enough to make Phainon shuffle his feet a little - fighting the urge to cough into his hands as he sweated under that rigid gaze that was peering daggers into his skin uncomfortably.

Even if Mydei couldn’t see under his hood, it certainly felt like he was at the very least looking into his soul.

.. All before Phainon had to blink at that sight, doing his best to truly understand what emotion Mydei was displaying because it was there. 

The slight hue of red in Mydei’s checks, the tiniest amount of flusterness on display before he closed his eyes and gave a shuddering sigh. 

“.. Do not be foolish, we are only both working to the same means to an end,” Mydei grumbled out, all before opening his eyes and looking away immediately - scoffing a little as if he was doing his best to try to remove the redness from his skin.

Only, Phainon found himself moving a little bit closer at that.

“Ah,” Phainon started in such a sweet tone, feeling a smile dancing on his lips as he blinked at Mydei and took in the rather odd sight of the prince currently, “Saying that while you’re getting red in the face, are you one who is prone to embarrassment, my prince?”

“I am not your prince,” Mydei told him, yet again, “I am no one’s prince.”

Phainon wasn’t sure if he really agreed with that - sure, the man technically had no kingdom but there was still something very royal about him. Perhaps the mere air around him that made Phainon feel as if he was still in the presence of a sovereign, but whatever it was - Phainon felt a bit regretful now that he had once agreed with the man and insulted him over it.

Mydei turned on heel at that - not even giving Phainon another look at his cute expression with the smallest amount of pink in those cheeks - just enough to make those red markings under his eye truly pop.

And Phainon tilted his head to watch that man, staring at the bounce of golden flaming hair as he watched that man go. 

“My dearest prince! Don’t run off in such a hurry without me!” Phainon found himself chuckling as he moved to follow that man - still idly thinking of the way Mydei’s ears had turned the softest color of red. As if he was so very honest with his emotions, in just that one instance.

.. And Phainon didn’t want to linger on why he could feel his nonexistent heartbeat speeding up over the memory of that sight.

chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

i am horrible at fight scene writing but the fighting was not the focus ok . just look away ill try harder nice time i just needed gay yearning

“Mydeimos,” Phainon started with a heavy exhale leaving his throat as he side stepped one of the shambling men there - dodging them as they merely swayed back and forth and waited almost earnestly for Mydei to say a command,  “What is.. This?”

Mydei’s head jerked up a little at that - merely to blink at Phainon as their gazes met before his eyes dipped away and back into his tome once more. Not appearing bothered at all as he remained on that fallen log and his legs spread as far as they could be while he read.

“Practice.” Was the reply Mydei offered as his own eyes looked at the crowd of undead a bit boredly, not even seeming to care about telling Phainon how exactly it was practice as they all just continued to stand there and watch Mydei read in the small forest clearing. 

“Right, right.. The horde of the undead just creeping around you practice, may I ask what for, exactly?” Phainon pressed forward as he leaned a little to look at the book Mydei seemed so very focused on - eyes trying their best to read the words of it, only to be floundering as he immediately realized he had no idea what letters they were.

Something about them didn’t look human, either, he was pretty sure he could at least tell when something was Kremnoan, but.. That was absolutely not Kremnoan, every word looked drenched in hot green wax and was practically burning off of the pages - not that Mydei appeared to mind. 

“Practicing how long I can keep them active,” Mydei replied in a rather bored sounding tone - as if he had long since been expecting that question all while he flicked over to the next patch with a few oddly green and wicked embers flying off the page with the movement.

Phainon had half his mind to question whatever in Kephale’s taint he was reading, but he had to bite his tongue over that. Instead moving his gaze away and to the crowds of undead surrounding the necromancer - shambling and creaking as they stood nearby. Body and joints cracking every inch they moved and swayed in the breeze. 

“.. And how is that going?”

Phainon’s eyes never left those creatures as he stared at them, studying the way they seemed so much.. More despondent in comparison to him. To where he almost had to question just what all that mark on his neck was truly doing to his mind, or was it the false king Kephale’s ‘blessing’ to him?

“Swell. They last a few hours,” Mydei answered him, making him slowly look at that book again with a quiet huff leaving his chest. 

He had been sleeping more lately, sleeping as if he were truly dead and unable to be roused by Mydei who had one spoke about trying to wake him a few days ago for Phainon to not even move. 

It was odd to know that about himself, and yet, he woke up every time and was doomed to continue his undead life.

“Right.. And what are you reading?” Phainon asked as he placed a hand on Mydei’s shoulder a bit testingly - always amused over how that fallen prince had slowly begun to allow things like that.

A touch here or there, gentle and fleeting - originally a thing that made Mydei duck away from him and bristle like as if he were a grumpy little feline. Only, now he allowed it - jumping just a tad under Phainon’s touch before relaxing again with a sigh.

Golden eyes flicked away at that, glancing over his shoulder and to Phainon who was beaming a smile at him - doing his best to seem friendly as that prince only raised a brow curiously towards him; “Oh? The perfect knight wants to learn about necromancy?”

“I’m far from perfect now, and if my prince is a necromancer shouldn’t I know a little to better protect him?” Phainon fired back as a soft little tease, feeling a glimmering smile creeping wider onto his lips as he spoke.  

“Your prince?” Mydei scoffed out - darting a glaring look to Phainon that normally would have shut Phainon up, at least, if he still actually was still a knight, “I told yo-”

“I know, I know. You’re no one’s prince anymore.” Phainon moved away from that man at that, waving his hand lazily as he sighed over those words that had been repeated to him so many times now. 

Everything kept repeating in his mind, making him relive their fights and duels and all the harsh words he had said to Mydei, his own death that became more clear with every passing day, and the way he still couldn’t fight back his regrets that were decaying in his heart.

Mydei sighed over that - shaking his head a little, “.. I should tell them to attack you for mocking my tone like that.”

“Is that so?” Phainon asked teasingly, already moving to one of those corpses that were shambling about. Standing there with dead fish eyes that seemed to not even acknowledge Phainon, making him tilt his head to the side with mute fascination. 

This was him a bit ago before Mydei put that sun marking on his neck, huh? Mindless and obeying the same man that had killed him..?

.. That was enough to haunt him easily as he blinked away from that soulless husk, instead focusing his gaze on the pretty necromancer that stood out like a sore thumb in the clearing with zombies lurking about. 

“Yes.”

“Ah, but you never did that while I was alive!” Phainon chirped out as he swayed his hips to the side - moving immediately to give a beaming grin at that man who was now shutting his own book with a heavy sigh. 

“Hmph.”

Well, that was never a good sign! And Phainon found himself chuckling a little bit nervously as Mydei stood rather quickly and walked away. Not from Phainon, no, Phainon was following hot on his heels after him instantly - but away from those zombies he was leaving there and Phainon had half his mind to comment on it.

Instead, he only gave a soft little smile as he listened to the creaking and odd bursting noises of the dead decaying behind him and Mydei - walking after that necromancer who was quickly moving.

Though, Mydei seemed very aware of the way Phainon was behind him - leaving the door open for him all while Mydei went about his business. Leaving Phainon to idly watch him settle his book down, before moving into their shared bedroom. 

He was gone there a few moments, all before returning with a rather normal attire for himself - though, this time, Mydei as well had a hood on. A familiar thing that made Phainon raise a brow as he studied that man, always a little baffled by the heavy golden gauntlets he seemed to wear when he went out - but he supposed the prince couldn’t let go of all of his ties to Kremnos. 

“Where are you going?” Phainon decided to ask as that man seemed keen on tucking his locks of hair into his own hood - all before throwing Phainon a little look. One that seemed borderline amused, mixed with brief annoyance. 

“It appears reading it out of the question, so I’m going shopping,” Mydei told him curtly, in a tone of voice that made Phainon lean against the wall and watch that man put on more dark colors. He really did think Mydei would look pretty in other colors, but he seemed quite fond of crimson and black.. 

“.. Shopping? In Aedes Elysiae?” Phainon asked, but he fully knew that it was the wrong answer - of course it wasn't Aedes Elysiae.. Mydeimos wouldn’t be trying to hide his tattoos if that was the case, not anymore at least. 

“No.”

“Are you not going to say where instead, then?”

“No.”

“You..” Phainon sighed over that, shaking his head as he watched Mydei move towards him and that entry way - giving Phainon yet another odd little look from beneath his own hood. 

“It doesn’t matter where I’m going, considering you seem to just decide you’re coming along.” Mydei grumbled out, and Phainon couldn’t help but laugh over that - especially as he knew himself and how true those words actually were for himself. 

“That’s true! I’m just eager to know your plans.” Phainon beamed out, feeling as happy as possible over the way that necromancer seemed to have learned his personality so quickly and easily.

Really, it made working together a lot simpler. 

Mydei however, only seemed to twitch a little at that - cocking his head to the side over Phainon’s words; “Is that all?”

“Yep!”

“Hmph.”

──────────────

“Do I have to wear this cowl even into this city?” Phainon asked in a whiny tone, hands already grasping at the soft sides of it and rubbing it with his thumbs as he let his head fall dejectedly a tiny amount.
