He wasn’t really that upset by it - not with how his face and skin seemed to burn in the sunlight, feeling much too hot and almost made Phainon feel as if he were melting. 

.. Probably due to being a corpse, yet Mydei didn’t seem to care. Even as Phainon had made some.. Slight adjustments to this attire Mydei had enchanted for him. A few more belts here and there with some decent gloves, more things to make him appear less like a lost and decaying wizard and more like an adventurer who was merely hiding his identity.

Sure, sure, he was still wearing a lot of black - but it felt more freeing to have some accessories as well, outside of Mydei’s clothes of choice for him. 

“Yes.”

Phainon hummed over that - tugging his hood a little bit forward as he stared at the back of Mydei’s head, all before moving to join him at his side instead. Allowing their shoulders to bump together just the tiniest amounts as he leaned forward to look Mydei in the eyes. Endlessly amused by how that almost stoic looking man raised a brow over that inquisitively - waiting to hear out whatever nonsense Phainon would say to him next.

And it was only fair that Phainon obeyed, moving to pull on his sleeve a little to show off the skin of his wrist with a quiet hum as he flipped it between both sides, “Is it because I’m as pale as the moon?”

“Yes.”

Phainon hummed so painfully innocently over that; “Should I try staying out in the sun more?”

That hit its mark.

This time, Mydei stopped walking - instead halting to give Phainon an odd little look of disbelief as he cocked his head to the side, staring Phainon down and Phainon was once more thankful for him. Thankful that he had enchanted Phainon’s cowl to make it to where even he himself couldn’t see the playful smile on Phainon’s lips as Mydei’s eyes lowered into a glare.

“.. Is this a joke?”

“Surely even a dead man can tan a little..” Phainon offered with a shrug, still grinning even if that man couldn’t see that it was for him. 

Mydei seemed to pause at that - taking a moment as if he was reflecting on those words, pondering them rather deeply before his eyes slid to Phainon. A hand moving to touch his arm a little, his wrist, so gently that Phainon found himself a little baffled over how sweet the touch was. Tender, too tender for it to be wasted on the dead.

And yet, Mydei only stood there pondering those words - assuredly thinking over the rather useless information regarding if Phainon actually could or not before humming quietly while dropping Phainon’s hand once more. 

“Not in the same way a living body would tan, no. A change in your skin that could resemble tanning may occur but it wears off quickly,” Mydei explained as his thumb rolled over Phainon’s skin on his hand, as if he was truly inspecting the possibility and Phainon.. Felt a bit silly for the way he felt embarrassed by this.

Unable to bite back the feelings of nervousness as that man only continued to seemingly hold his hand as softly as possible - too gentle and kind of an action to be directed at a man who was already dead. 

Phainon moved his own free hand to pat at Mydei’s gently - almost doing his best to be soothing towards that prince, even if the only effect it actually had was making Mydei release his hand with a quiet little huff.

As if he had been zoning out and barely even realizing he was holding and inspecting Phainon’s hand so sweetly.

But that was fine, Phainon couldn’t help but chuckle a little over that reaction; “Wow, I’m becoming so very educated in things I never once thought about before in my entire life.”

Mydei moved to cross his arms over his chest at that - sighing heavily as he threw a rather narrow stare Phainon’s way, “.. Is this some sort of enrichment for you?”

Enrichment for Phainon?

If anything, he thought this was more for Mydei’s sake than anything - the way that man seemed to light up just a little when he had to actually ponder things of this nature. Digging through his own thoughts and ideas before finding an answer to give to Phainon’s arguably stupid questions.. The way Mydei seemed so earnestly trying to help him and solve things..  

Something about it all brought a smile to Phainon’s face easily, all while Mydei seemed eager to do so as well; and a lurking part of Phainon had to assume this man enjoyed being depended on. Maybe even sought it out, enjoying helping people and doing what he could in every scenario he found himself in.

It was only morally correct for Phainon to give Mydei reasons to aid Phainon then, right? 

“Certainly, I like how your face scrunches up a little in thought!” Phainon chirped out with a little laugh regardless of his own thoughts - watching the way that fallen prince closed his eyes a bit lazily as if he were truly digesting those words before turning on heel. 

“.. Let’s carry on.”

‘Let’s’.

That had become a thing with the both of them, where they were now a duo and Mydei seemed to fully expect him to come along with him even if he growled over it and acted somewhat annoyed. Which really only aided fuel to the fire that was Phainon’s assumptions of Mydei liking having his company around, but that was fine.

Phainon could bask in those emotions without bringing them up and ruining it! 

Though, as he moved to catch up to that prince, he had more things on his mind as he hummed and bumped their shoulders together once again; “It’s kind of endearing, did you have many suitors when you were a fulltime prince?”

That earned him an egregious stare from Mydei - a lazy one as he seemed more focused on walking, but still one that said more than a thousand words ever could as he appeared borderline confused; “.. Fulltime?”

“Mhm.. Were you popular with the princesses?” Phainon asked as he moved his eyes to look at the dirt path they were on - feeling a smile on his lips but.. It quivered a little for some reason.

The idea of this man being with a princess, married and in love.. Why did it make him feel almost.. Jealous?

Phainon had never been the type of person to seek out love, especially due to being a knight for his king and swearing the entire idea off, but now.. Did he really actually want to marry a princess so badly that he was jealous of Mydei’s past life?

After all, he had always thought the princesses were stunning! His eyes had been glued to them and watched them dance all the time when he was on duty, so it wasn’t that odd that he would think of Mydei marrying one of them and feeling jealous!

Though, he had to wonder if Mydei himself knew how to dance? Surely he did, Phainon couldn’t quite remember seeing Kremnoan royalties basking in the festivities of balls and dances very often - but what kind of prince didn’t know the most basic of dances? Phainon could probably teach him if he didn’t, however.. 

“No.” Mydei replied coldly, and that was enough to make Phainon blink at his own thoughts - head tilting upwards as he stared at that harsh sun above them as he tried to even think about that.

“Wow.. Shocking,” Phainon murmured, because it truly did feel a bit odd that Mydeimos had no suitors after his hand and no princesses grasping for the throne of Kremnos..

“Mocking me gets you nowhere.”

Those hissed out words were enough to make Phainon toss his head to the slightly shorter man walking at his side - mouth falling agape as he tried to even work out how that man thought Phainon was making fun of him. 

“I’m not mocking you! I’m genuinely curious about the pretty Kremnoan prince’s love life before all of this!” Phainon knew he sounded whiny as he gasped out those words, but he was genuinely stunned over the fact Mydei had such little trust in him. 

“There was no love life. I did my duties, that’s all that mattered,” Mydei grumbled after a few moments of silence - making Phainon snap his jaw shut over how for some odd reason, that made him feel better.

.. Probably because he was super jealous of that guy having a love life where he had none! The idea of a necromancer actually having more people in love with him than Phainon had ever had in his life was driving him insane! Especially as he thought about what kind of wedding ceremony Mydei would even have, let alone how he would dress..

Phainon could assuredly treat a royal lover better than this man, after all, he was taught for most of his life how to take care of them and pamper them! Mydei certainly was not and was comparatively out of his depth! 

“Not even a little? Not a couple hundred people vying for your attention?” Phainon was now teasing a little, sniffling back a small laugh,  “Kremnos was a kingdom of war and triumph, honor and glory - surely someone wanted you as their husband.”

“No.”

Phainon had to glance at that man at his side - brow raised over the way Mydei seemed so annoyed by this topic. Maybe it was a sore spot like his mother, or maybe there was something more to it all. Either way, Phainon had to let out a rather sharp whistle through his teeth over it. 

“Wow.. So flat and deadpan sounding, are you that sure of it?”

“Yes.”

“Hmm,” Phainon found himself smiling over it all still, unable to hold himself back as he gave that man a wide grin - very aware of the way Mydei couldn’t see it, even if those golden feline eyes were glaring him down, “You wouldn’t accept a knight to protect you, but would you allow them to take your hand in marriage?”

Mydei was silent at that, seeming a little bit caught off guard as he grit his  teeth quite obviously - his lips moving but not opening, only massaging his words before speaking them it seemed, “.. Would any kingdom allow such a thing?”

Phainon had to hum over that - moving his eyes to focus on the road ahead as he tried to think of why he was even asking this. It was all so foolish and stupid to wonder, and yet.. He found himself laughing a little, throwing a smile towards that dirt road before them. 

“I once heard that Kremnos is not quite like other kingdoms, one that values strength above most other things,” Phainon explained, thinking on all of the stories he had been told throughout the years of Castrum Kremnos and its glory, “I’ve even heard of a ritual where the suitor battles for their love’s hand in marriage.”

That was a gamble.

A playful one at that as he darted his eyes to the man at his side, watching the way Mydei’s jaw seemed to tighten and slack after a few moments of thinking over Phainon’s words. Clearly heavily debating the right dialogue choice in this type of situation between them both. 

“.. Why are you asking such things?” Mydei asked after a few heavy and rather deliberate moments between the words Phainon had just said and his own. 

“Curiosity.”

“Stop asking.” Mydei snapped as his eyes jerked back to the road he was now more than a little focused on, so blatantly attempting his best to ignore Phainon at his side. But even that made Phainon feel more and more curious on this topic. Almost skipping as he moved to be more in front of Mydei as he turned to awkwardly walk and stare at Mydei, drinking in the way that fallen prince was refusing to look at him.

Phainon had to chuckle over it as he skillfully kept pace with Mydei all while staring him down, “You won’t even confirm that knights could fight for the royalty’s hands in marriage if they wanted to?”

Phainon knew the answer.

Kremnoan royalty allowed it, to fight their royal bloodline for a chance at their hand and being wed to each other - but no one ever dared attempt it. Too often did those attempting such a thing lose their lives, or became a public mockery for trying to best those Kremnoans. And Phainon could understand why as his eyes trailed to Mydei’s arms - taking note of the muscle there that he had seen on display so many times before when they were enemies. 

.. Phainon didn’t even know what Mydei thought of them both now, either, whether they were enemies or companions - whatever the case, Phainon had to acknowledge Mydei was strong both physically and mentally. 

A duel for his hand in marriage would not be easily won.

“It’s much too rare for knights to rival someone from the royal bloodline in strength,” Mydei replied with a heavy exhale seeming to run through him as his eyes still refused to look at Phainon - as if the road before them was the most interesting thing in the world to him for some reason, “It’s why we do not take knights, after all.”

“Mm..” Phainon hummed as his eyes remained fixed on Mydei - studying the brief flickers of emotions on his face, watching the way he was obviously appearing a little nervous over this conversation. Antsy, even, as if the topic of love and marriage was something he wasn’t accustomed to.

But that felt outrageous, he was a prince, after all. 

“So it’s rare, but not impossible.” Phainon spoke while nodding, watching the way Mydei cut him a harsh little glare;  “Interesting.”

“.. It’s not interesting.” 

Mydei’s eyes were back on the road ahead of them now - but Phainon couldn’t bite back the smile on his lips over this conversation even as he copied. Blinking at the castle walls that were now coming into view and Phainon… Phainon had heard of this kingdom, but he had never been here himself.

Styxia.

A place that was a bit more darker than Phainon preferred - and he didn’t mean that in the lighting sense, instead.. He meant the way the kingdom worked. If anything, this was one of the rare far and few kingdoms that were rather open about practicing magic and the sorts - a thing that made Phainon bite at his lips a little.

Though, maybe he should lighten up.. He wasn’t exactly alive anymore to be super serious and up tight about magic, when his entire existence now depended on magic. 

“Keep your head down,” Mydei jarred him out of his thoughts regardless, making him blink and look at that man who was scowling beneath his own hood,  “A hood that's just a pitch black void is daunting.”

Phainon almost wanted to question why Mydei’s hood wasn’t enchanted like Phainon’s - but he supposed it didn’t matter what the reasoning was as he focused on the front again. Instead walking as his eyes moved around to blink at those eerie blue flowers, taking in the sights and the way the land seemed to darken with every step that they got closer. 

“Less than if I had it down to show off my face?” Phainon asked in a slight tease, merely wanting to fill the air as the world became more eerie. Every step into that land made his bones shake - and he almost felt the urge to double check if his flesh was still there or if it had begun to rot when he was looking away. 

Regardless, Mydei didn’t seem bothered by the question; “Yes.”

“.. Are you trying to be mean to me, or?”

“Kephale isn’t exactly liked, anymore. And neither is his beautiful white haired and blowing blue eyed knight.” Mydei explained with a rather heavy and deep felt sigh - a thing that made Phainon chuckle a little. 

He understood what the man was saying, and yet, he couldn’t help himself but to grin at that man - watching the way those golden eyes flicker to him beneath his own cowl even with most his face hidden away. 

“You think I’m beautiful?”

Mydei gave him a rather bizarre look at that, appearing more than a little flabbergasted as he sighed loudly once more, “.. That’s what you focused on?”

“Well,” Phainon hummed out, straightening himself out and staring at the kingdom walls that were getting ever closer - a sense of dread clawing into Phainon’s throat every time he thought of it,  “If I focus on the fact Kephale’s reputation is completely shattered due to a maniac necromancer using his dead body or his appearance like a puppet, I start feeling very unwell.”

Phainon explained with a lazy wave of his hand - very aware of those feline-kin eyes watching his every move. 

“Everything in my life was for naught, and I failed the person I swore to protect.” Phainon mumbled with a little less heart, feeling a laugh bubble up out of his chest that was threatening to choke him when he thought on it for too long. 

“So, I do my best not to, and try to aim for the revenge angle!”

Mydei remained silent at that, instead only continuing to walk in the new strange quietness between them both. One that made Phainon almost regret the words he had jokingly said, all before Mydei said one single thrilling word. 

“.. Okay.”

Okay..

Well, Phainon would take what he could get as his eyes only studied the way the sky had turned almost to night in an instant, as if the steps they were taking were breaking beyond the barrier of life and death. Every step felt as if he was being pulled into a direction that he just couldn’t quite place, all to where his body felt sluggish.

.. That was fine though, he just needed to remember to stay by Mydeimos’s side and it would be fine. 

“This place is kind of..” Phainon began speaking, swallowing a little over the way he couldn’t bite down his feelings of dread that were sinking into him,  “Strange feeling.”

“Castorice,” Mydei replied flippantly, and Phainon had to blink at that - it was a name he had heard before, he knew that much. But not one he actually could place to anything, thus, all he could do was look at that necromancer with confusion settling deep in his mind. 

“Pardon?”

“Princess Castorice has an enchantment on her entire kingdom that her family works to upkeep, her sister’s life depends on it,” Mydei explained as he slowed his steps, crossing his arms as he peered upwards at that vast castle - a marvel that Phainon took the chance to look at as well, copying Mydei a little,  “At least, that’s what I know of it.”

That was bizarre to Phainon; enchanting their entire kingdom for some sort of end goal, but not allowing anyone to be privy of it? 

For what purpose?

.. Did Phainon even have any right to ask? 

“Enchantment.. For what?” He asked anyway, unsure of the answer, but well.. He wasn’t even a knight anymore, that role was gone from him, and now if anything, he was just a nosy passerby. 

Hell, even worse, he was a nosy dead passerby, and it wasn’t as if the dead could tell tales… Or however the saying went, it probably didn’t apply to Phainon anyway considering he most certainly could yap about whatever he wanted to. 

“I don’t know,” Mydei admitted with a slight shake of his head - a movement that Phainon watched from the corner of his eyes as he instead blinked upwards, “I’m not even supposed to be divulging this information to you but..”

His eyes only watched as blue little snow flakes seemed to fall from the sky - glowing, light and beautiful, all before vanishing without a trace and Phainon couldn’t even resist the urge to reach out and grab one. Well, attempted to grab one - instead it disappeared immediately against his gloved hand, becoming nothingness as if it had never existed in the first place. 

“That’s why the air feels more odd and heavy, suffocating, almost. What you’re privy to is the heavy layer of magic coating the town,” Mydei explained with a lazy shake of his head, his own eyes looking upwards as well, “A thing you probably wouldn’t have noticed when you were alive due to your lack of mana.”

“Er..” Phainon tried to begin, still looking at his empty hand before raising a brow and looking to Mydei curiously, “So, it feels super depressing and kind of scary here due to them wanting it to be that way?”

Mydei took a moment at that before lowering his gaze and looking to Phainon, just before motioning to the side of him freely; “.. Yes, Everything here is imbued with magic, even the willow trees around us.”

Phainon’s eyes moved the trees lining the entry way at that - taking a moment to look at the deep purple hues of them that cascaded into such a deep blue all before the ends of the leaves seemed to glow with life. A flickering white hue that shined so brightly, yet somehow Phainon found himself ignoring it in trade of focusing on the falling odd snow around them. 

Phainon’s eyes only blinked as he looked up those trees a little, staring at the silver chains that hung down with white glowing baubles at the ends of them for lights - all while those flakes still snowed down. His mind reeling a little over the way the canopy of the leaves almost looked as though they were dazzling stars above his eyes.

.. Gorgeous, was a word he would call it - all while feeling his mouth left agape as he tried to take it in fully. Everything about it felt more mystical than he had ever imagined his eyes would see as the everlasting beams of moonlight of this place seemed to creep through the branches above.

“Come on, little knight,” Mydei’s voice snapped him out of it, making him look downwards and find a rather coy looking Mydei peering back at him, “There’s a lot of pretty sights in this world like this, if you just go out looking.”

Phainon found himself unable to reply to that, not sure if he should comment on how he spent his life only following his king - and for once. Just this once, he had a tiny bit of regret as he watched that necromancer turn his back to him and begin to walk into that kingdom. A movement that Phainon found himself following after without a second thought. 

Passing through that grand entry way only made Phainon feel even more baffled by the beauty that had immediately entranced him as he blinked at the rows of bushes. Bushes that rose up so wonderfully high, all while having spirals of lanterns wrapping around them artistically - lighting up the streets just enough to be beautiful, and useful.

Though, that didn’t seem to matter as Mydei instead took a rather sharp turn - veering off and heading down a corridor that Phainon had barely even noticed. At least it seemed as though Mydei certainly knew where they both were going - and Phainon found himself swallowing a little as he chased after him into this now much more.. Densely packed area of the kingdom. 

Every step into that more crowded area had Phainon huffing a little, doing his best to stay next to his companion as he narrowed his eyes - sniffling a little as the way opened up more. Only to reveal much too many people, swarms of them, really.. And Phainon never would have guessed this kingdom would be so alive. 

“What specifically are you here to buy, Mydei?” Phainon asked as he felt his arm knocked together into Mydei’s by someone passing him by - an action that only made him creep closer to that fallen prince. 

A part of him debated grabbing the man’s arm to make sure he stayed close, but Mydei would assuredly growl over that and chastise how foolish he was. 

“Does it matter?” Mydei asked, and Phainon continued to move his eyes to peer at the braziers of blue fire - eerie, yet gorgeous as more of those odd vivid snowflakes fluttered out of them.

“Well,” Phainon mumbled out as his eyes continued to look up and down at the area around them - feeling a little baffled over the way things seemed so.. Glowy,  “This doesn’t seem like a particularly safe area..”

Every step that he took on brought him a tiny bit closer to Mydei, staring at the cobblestone path before them while darting his eyes around this small back alley market street they seemed to be on. Every house appeared to have a little open area where people were peddling wares, some looking happy - others, not so much.

Whatever it was, Phainon could barely keep his eyes away from marveling over the plants here, blue and magical - even from the pots that seemed to house the roots, only for the actual leaves and stems of the plant to not be touching the pot at all, instead hovering above it.

“Just keep your nose down.” 

Phainon had to look at that man with those words - blinking at the way Mydei appeared so serious currently, focused wholly on moving through the crowds and making their way to a specific place. 

“Mhm..” Phainon hummed as he looked at the man who still had a heartbeat in his chest; and the man who had made Phainon feel more alive than he ever had when he was.. Actually alive, “But I’m worried about you more than myself, you know..”

Mydei didn’t reply immediately to that - making Phainon scoff a little as his eyes only trailed to the side more, looking at the glowing blue lanterns that seemed to hover in place all before looking back to Mydei.

“Someone pulling a knife on me will be significantly less painful than if someone stabs you.” Phainon continued to explain as he moved to bump his shoulder into Mydei’s own a bit playfully, doing his best to ignore the way Mydei seemed a bit miffed over it. A piece of him wanted to ask why the prince was so high-strung currently, but..

With this many people walking around and chattering amongst themselves, it probably wasn’t the right time and place to ask that.

“I’ve dealt with worse pains.” Mydei rather flippantly replied, not even batting his eyes as he instead took a turn down a path that made Phainon pause a little - blinking at how much darker that area was. Gone were the magical and whimsical lights floating about, the snowflakes of glimmering wonder, and instead it was.. Eerie and dark.

And yet, Phainon found himself following after that man without much of a second thought, “.. Mydei, that doesn’t mean you deserve to feel those pains again if it can be helped.”

“And it cannot be helped, I need to be here,” Mydei growled back, looking a little over his shoulder and making Phainon instinctually smile at him - only for Mydei to jerk his head to the front again and continue walking. 

This area was much more beaten down, quieter, all with eyes watching the both of them as they walked and that.. That made Phainon feel as if they were somewhere that a prince like Mydei never should be in his entire life. 

Phainon found himself staring at the back of Mydei’s head over those thoughts; “Why don’t you just send me to buy things for you when it’s in such.. Shady locations?”

Mydei made a loud huffing noise at that, once that Phainon was doing his best in imagining was a laugh as that hood shook a little from side to side. A glance happened once more over Mydei’s shoulder as he gave Phainon an expression that could only be explained as amused in the dim lighting; “.. You wouldn’t have any idea what you’re here to buy, you fool.”

“That’s true! But I’m not afraid to ask!” Phainon chirped out, happily stating those words as he continued after that man and walking just a bit faster. Eager to walk side by side with that man. 

“And what? Have what you are found out and burnt to ash in the townsquare?” Mydei argued back without missing a single beat, bickering just as they always had, and something about it made Phainon feel as if he were at home with Mydei.

As if he had always wanted to be with this man and at his side like this, somewhere deep within his soul. 

“Mydeimos, it is so sweet when you care about me!” Phainon laughed out as he bumped his shoulder into Mydei again, doing his best to ignore the odd silence around them as he did so. 

Though, that seemed to have done a number to Mydei’s mood for some reason; “.. Keep your voice down.”

“But I tru-”

“Quite the unique name you have there!” 

Phainon found himself snapping his mouth shut over that as Mydei’s footsteps faltered and seemed to pause completely - making Phainon copy and tilt his head towards the new speaker. 

Well, speakers, really, as his eyes took in quite a few angry looking people - perturbed and bothered. 

“I would hope the full name isn’t ‘Mydeimos Kremnos’, or you would have a rather bad time today,” A man began, making Phainon look to the new speaker as he blankly tried to take in what was happening with this situation, “Though, with those red markings all over your body.. It’s obvious you’re Kremnoan.”

One of the strange burly men laughed at that, taking a moment to whistle so painfully loudly - loud enough to make a scene and draw even more eyes to both Phainon and Mydei. A situation that had Phainon feeling.. A little antsy as he looked to the man at his side with a worried glance, studying the way Mydei was as stoic as he always tried to be. Only staring a burning glare into the men who were giddily chidding at him now. 

“I’ve heard word that Mydeimos was the very same prince who killed all of his own kingdom, surely that’s not you, is it?”

Ah.

Phainon had to return his eyes to those men; a piece of him had almost forgotten this was the reality of Mydei’s situation. A reality that he himself once lived, viewing that kind man at his side as an enemy, and not his companion; a crazed man who wanted all of life to decay and rot beneath his own fingertips and powers..

.. And not at all the sweet man who seemed to have the patience of a saint when he was speaking with Phainon. 

“The rumors say Mydeimos used necromancy to kill all of his people, just to enslave them eternally,” One of the men only continued, nodding to the other as Phainon found himself tilting his head over that, “If you’re here to try to repeat history, you have some nerve.”

Even that was incorrect, really, Phainon knew that much even before becoming Mydei’s ally. That man never used an undead army like he had expected, let alone the enslaved souls of Kremnoans to fuel his power. 

“.. I would never do such a thing.” Mydei grumbled out from Phainon’s side, making Phainon’s hand twitch a little as he looked at that man - his mind idly aware of the way this.. Was some sort of sore spot for Mydei.

Naturally, his deceased kingdom would be a sore spot, but it had always been a cheap shot that Phainon himself had loved to bring up time and time again - and now these random men were bringing it up.. It felt a little unfair, considering how Phainon felt as thought at least he had met Mydei many times before to start bickering and throwing insults at him; these guys didn’t even know Mydei like that.

.. Where was his mind actually at, though? 

“Don’t feel as though you have to reply, my lord,” Phainon told Mydei as he gave a curt nod to Mydei - in reality doing his best to disperse his own thoughts that were haunting him.

Only.. Golden eyes flickered to him and seemed to look a bit baffled by that, not to mention the way Mydei cocked his head to the side a little; “.. My lord?”

“It’s rare to see people with those markings nowadays, ‘my lord’. Are we wearing that hood to hide the crimson tattoos of Kremnos on yourself?” One of the men snickered as they spoke - making Phainon blink over that, vaguely aware of the way he was being mocked now. But Phainon.. Truly hadn’t been expecting people to be so bold even in towns. Already with these few men brandishing their weapons and leering towards the both of them.

.. Were they about to fight in the streets? That felt a little illegal and forbidden, but he wasn’t exactly alive either to say something about the laws and regulations.. Especially not in a land like Styxia that was ruled by magic that was so heavy in the air that it felt almost suffocating to Phainon. 

Not so suffocating that Phainon wasn’t aware of the way Mydei himself seemed to be readying for combat a little - lowering himself into a stance that was so familiar to Phainon from the days of when they were enemies. Only now, Mydei was moving a bit closer to him, as if entrusting him fully to protect Mydei’s blindspots.

And Phainon had no desire to fail him, instead scoffing a little over the popping of knuckles he was hearing from some of the men around him as some odd sort of intimidation tactic. Phainon himself had nothing to fear; he was already dead. But he did.. Move a bit closer to Mydei, feeling an odd sense of worry for that man who still had his life to be holding onto tightly. 

Phainon knew fully well that the prince could defend himself, and yet.. He wanted to be of use to him, to defend him and stay by his side - and surely that wasn’t a crime. 

.. Was it a crime, though? Something about all of this felt just a little odd to Phainon, as if he was missing something when he actually thought about it more and more. 

If Mydei was truly known across the world as being the man who had slaughtered his entire kingdom, and Castorice was the princess who had enchanted her own land.. Wouldn’t they be a bit more on guard for Mydei? Or have some sort of system in place to defend against people like Mydei presumably was? 

Phainon had to blink at his thoughts, for once looking at those falling snowflakes of what he had to assume was pure magic before huffing a little. 

It didn’t make sense, but as he looked at the men who were rolling their heads to crack their necks and shoulders - he had to assume it didn’t quite matter right now what Mydei’s association with this kingdom was. 

“You’ll have to shop elsewhere, prince. We don’t quite like necromancers in this town.” One of the men chuckled out, making Phainon take a note of him. Large, rather muscular, but he didn’t seem particularly fit; Not in the way Mydei was.

Instead he seemed as if he had fought in a few wars, and unlike Mydei, he had probably lost them if his mess of scars were another to go by - let alone the missing eye from his face replaced with an eyepatch. 

“.. That’s news to me.” Mydei mumbled a bit quietly, in a tone that was more amused than anything and making Phainon feel like he was missing some sort of joke there.

Alas, all he could force his mind to do was focus on the duo of men who were still sneering at the both of them - angry and perturbed. 

“You’ll be slaughtered before the sun ever rises,” The other man laughed - making Phainon’s eyes look at him, yet there was something off about the situation and how no one had moved yet. Something about it made Phainon’s skin itch when he thought about it for too long, and a piece of him was unsure if he was merely unaware of how wizards do battle, or if there was something more.

Though, Mydei only continued on, “The sun never rises in Styxia. I’m hearing I have plenty of time to live my life.”

At those words, the first man had lunged at Mydei without much of a second thought - only for Phainon to butt in this time, not even hesitating as his eyes instead looked elsewhere. Only to find himself knocking into Mydei a bit roughly, on purpose, but roughly as he stared at the man behind the one whose sword was drawn. 

Blinking at the way he now was holding a bow, foregoing his own sword and dagger in trade of that - and Phainon didn’t have time to pay it any heed as he instead blocked the first man’s sword. Parrying it without much of a second thought, not even batting an eye over the way his arm had jerked - but that didn’t matter.

Instead, he used enough force to inch that man away a few feet, all before turning on heel to look at that prince who he had purposefully bumped out of the way. 

“Phainon?!” Mydei hissed out, all before barking out a rather odd laugh as Phainon moved immediately to grip onto that man’s shoulders - looking up and down to make sure he himself was unarmed. 

“Sorry!” Phainon chirped out, though he was still inspecting Mydei - a two on one attack while Phainon was there was dirty, and something he absolutely wouldn’t allow.

Sure, Mydei had the strength to fight them off, and probably would have preferred being able to fight - but Phainon couldn’t help his inner knight instincts to block everything himself. 

“Are you going mad?” Mydei asked, but he still had the oddest expression on his face - shaking his head as he instead moved to the side of Phainon, an action that left Phainon feeling almost panicked. 

“You’re asking that, but you’re the one grinning like a maniac, Mydei!” Phainon pointed that out, sure, but nothing prepared Phainon for the sight of Mydei already lashing out at the first man that had attacked him. That dazzling grin on his lips with white fangs clearly on display as Phainon found his mind reeling over it.

His eyes felt glued as he watched that man effortlessly move to attack at that man, harsh screeching sounds of metal clinking together messily all while Phainon found his breath stopping in his throat over the awe-inducing sight of that Kremnoan fighting. He had seen it time and time before, but nothing quite compared to watching him in battle, and.. Not, having his sword aiming for Phainon. 

“You have an arrow in your arm,” Mydei breathed out in between his movements, pausing to throw a glare to Phainon who had to blink at that. Now vaguely aware of the way he had just been sitting there and staring at Mydei instead of helping.

That was enough to make him huff a little, “Ow, ahhh, ohhh. Is that what you want me to say?! I can’t feel it!”

“Ridiculous.“

Phainon found himself laughing at that, already moving to grab that flimsy arrow and snap it a little - scoffing as he ripped it through his arm the rest of the way with a heavy sigh as it tore the fabric of his shirt a little, but that was fine. His eyes only moved to take in the sight of Mydei quickly - noting how he was unharmed.

As long as Mydei hadn’t taken the arrow himself, it was worth it. He would take as many as he had to in order to make sure that man truly would live to see another day. 

The more important thing now was actually handling the man who had given up on his bow, clearly annoyed that his arrow had found Phainon’s arm and barely even bothered the man (mainly because he was already dead and couldn’t exactly feel pain) who had pushed Mydei to take the shot instead. 

And Phainon found himself a bit confused as his own hands gripped at this sword as tightly as possible, only to easily parry that man away. As if he was nothing. 

.. He wasn’t as tall as Phainon, or even Mydeimos, but he had looked as bulky as possible to where his mind was reeling over it - he had barely even noticed the way he hadn’t struggled with the first assaulter, but now.. It was so painfully apparently as he slid his blade to push that man away - watching the way his feet even seemed to slide from the force of it. 

“Be careful,” Mydei hissed quietly, making Phainon perk up a little and look to the man he had barely even registered being at his side now either, “The goal isn’t to kill anyone.”

As if Phainon needed to be told that, but truthfully.. He wasn’t sure what was going on as he blinked at his hand - a bit confused over his own strength and how these men seemed to weigh nothing.

“Mydeimos,” Phainon began, only partly aware that this was not the correct time for necromancer questions - and yet, “Why do I feel so much.. Stronger?”

Mydei made an odd noise at that, making Phainon turn a little to look at that man and study him - trying his best to truly understand what was going on all while ignoring those two men and the crowd that was now forming with hushed whispers in the air.

Whispers that made Phainon feel just a little bit nervous if he thought about them for too long - mind wondering where the guards were, if the town even had any, to come and stop this street brawl that had broken out. 

Mydei himself only seemed to blink at Phainon leisurely - as if he was taking in the sight of Phainon in depth before he scoffed rather loudly, “I don’t know, I’ve never fully inspected your body.”

Phainon found his thoughts struggling at that - lowering his sword a little to instead blink at Mydei, “Inspected.. My body?”

“To see what all was done with you. I’d need to extensively look at you in the nude,” Mydei replied with that same grin on his lips - all while the man he was fighting also.. Seemed a bit stunned by those words. 

“.. H.. Huh?” Phainon found himself dumbly saying, his inflection rising with his confusion mounting - unable to really focus as Mydei moved a little, just a bit. Seeming more baffled than Phainon somehow was as he looked between Phainon and the pair of men who now seemed stunned over the topic.

“What? You asked,” Mydei answered with a quiet little scoff - a weak sounding thing to most people, but to Phainon.. It was one of the loudest huffs of laughter he had heard from Mydei. Finding himself unable to look away from how .. Energetic Mydei looked right now.

Hands still flexing beneath his gauntlets, clenching into fists and unclenching all while he was grinning with his rather white and pointed canines on display. Much longer than the average ones Phainon had seen before, and yet they fit Mydei’s personality perfectly. Phainon’s eyes only scanned Mydei a little bit more, taking note of how he was steadily breathing, his chest beneath his black clothes rising and falling in a way that entranced Phainon so easily.

.. That man was beautiful, that much was for sure - but there was something that wasn’t quite fitting in Phainon’s mind. Blood that seemed to be trickling down Mydei’s chin, and yet.. Phainon couldn’t find a wound. Was it on the other side of his face? When had Mydei even gotten a wound?

Had he truly been that stunned and dazed during combat that he hadn’t even noticed his prince being wounded? 

“Are you joking?” Phainon asked after a moment, doing his best to shake his thoughts away and not dwindle around on the fact his mind had so immediately opted to call Mydei his prince. Instead trying his best to focus on that man’s smile… And the topic at hand, of course. 

Mydei only sighed heavily over that, throwing a pointed glare at Phainon over that question, “Is this really the best time for jokes, in general?”

“You’re a worshipper of a necromancer and you’re shocked he has ruined your body with his cruel magic?” 

Those words made Phainon turn a little, looking at the two men who had just been vying for their lives and to end Mydei’s cruel acts.. Though now they also seemed to be watching, waiting, even. As if they were hoping that Phainon would wake up from his enchantment he was under by Mydei - snap out of it and become aware of how he was being controlled. 

.. But Phainon was quite sure now that he wasn’t being controlled, he had much too much freedom to do and say what he desired, if that were the case.

And something about them butting in made him click his tongue in annoyance - biting back a snarl as he looked at those men who were still assuming they knew anything about Mydei when in reality; they didn’t know a thing.

They were sheep listening to lies and rumors, not finding out a thing for themselves; they were Phainon, all before his life and world was taken from him, forced to open his eyes and accept the gentleness from a man he once hated.

.. And he had to pity them for it, truly. 

“Be quiet, this is a private conversation.” Phainon found himself hissing - all while pitying those men. 

They wouldn’t know the truth of the matter, they didn’t care enough to even try to learn it; they merely had accepted Mydei as a villain into their hearts and wouldn’t even allow him in their town.. 

Phainon’s stomach only continued to twist and writhe more and more as he thought deeper on it, slowly coming to terms that they were the sickening reflection of himself.

“.. This isn’t very private at all,” Mydei mumbled at the side of him, making Phainon chance a glance to him - looking at the way his smile was gone and replaced with something more solemn. 

“Some would say it will be the talk of town..”

Phainon found himself pausing over that - tensing up completely as it now was people around them speaking and giggling over the situation. As if this were some funny little topic of the town, and not four men fighting in the street..

“They say the slightly shorter one is Mydeimos..”

“Who is the taller one then?”

“The one who Mydeimos wants to inspect in the nude? No idea..”

“Lady Castorice will be hearing of this..”

That seemed to do numbers to Mydei in some sort of way - immediately making him take hold of Phainon’s arm and yank him practically through the crowd around them. And Phainon almost wanted to question it - yet instead he found himself a bit stunned as he watched the way the crowd seemed to giggle over it and wrap around the two other men instead now, halting their advances and Phainon..

Phainon was a little confused over it all, honestly, dumb-founded as he blinked and was dragged quickly along. 

“Do..” Phainon started as that man swiftly brought the both of them back to the main street - obviously dragging Phainon towards the exit to leave that rather magical town behind, “You know Princess Castorice?”

Those words were enough to drag a scoffing sound from Mydei, a harsh noise that made Phainon tilt his head a little as his eyes trailed down to that clawed gauntlet that seemed so tight on his arm. A tightness that was merely a dull pressure with his deceased body, and Phainon had never once in his life been so curious about how warm a person was before.

An emotion and wonder that he would never have answered.

But Mydei was wholly unaware of that, instead releasing Phainon’s arm with a quiet sigh,“.. Let’s stop talking for a bit.” 

Phainon wanted to question the man further - but he had to sigh over it, instead merely allowing Mydei to guide them both out of that small quiet kingdom once more. Though, Phainon couldn’t help but glance behind them in sheer wonder - eyes taking in the sight of all the magic in the air before following after Mydei.

“I’ll have to come back later for what I need,” Mydei growled out quietly, making Phainon blink and look at that man as they walked through those familiar rows of willow trees. A stunning view, even more so as Mydei moved to remove that hood over his own head with a heavy sigh.

Golden eyes flicking upwards and staring at them, but this seemed a bit odd as Phainon followed that man off the main path - following him to a place he didn’t dare question. Not when Mydei seemed so painfully familiar with the layout of the terrain, he almost wanted to question how many times Mydei had been here.

As if he knew exactly where he was going, and Phainon didn’t have it in himself to inquire about it - instead only dipping his eyes and looking at the rows of magical flowers. Things that still appeared as if they were from a fairy tale, and not at all things Phainon had ever expected to be able to touch with his own gloves fingers.

Yet,  Phainon could hear the way Mydei was breathing heavily as he walked - that grin during the fight hadn’t been a fake one, of course not, but even he could get a bit tired it seemed. Or maybe it was more than that as Phainon’s eyes kept latching to the prince’s face - staring at the blood that was dripping from it so freely.

All before Mydei seemed to pause and lazily sit down on a cut down tree with a huff - already moving a gauntlet covered hand to rub at his own hand. Another spot that Phainon had to take a moment from behind that man to study a little, looking at whatever Mydei was rubbing, yet he found nothing there..

Phainon found his body moving on its own to the front of Mydei with those notes - taking the wound on Mydei’s face as the only one, and he was thankful for that. Just a bit. 

“You’re bleeding, Mydei..” Phainon sighed out as he slowly took a knee, a pose he had done so many times before - but this was different as the floor gave way beneath him to mud and grime. Something that normally never would have happened - for what king or ruler would be sitting in the mud?

.. Mydei would, Phainon supposed as he moved to scrounge around in his pockets now, a bit thankful he had been keeping a spare piece of vibrant blue cloth on hand as he retrieved it slowly and turned to Mydei - eyes blinking at that gash on the side of Mydei’s face.

Not deep enough to truly leave a scar, but deep enough to be gushing out blood down the rest of his face and making his tattoo side of his face match the red of the other. 

Only, Mydei immediately moved the back of his own hand at that - rubbing at that gash on his cheek before lowering his hand again, as if that had actually wiped all the blood away so easily while more beading up at the surface of the wound instantly. 

“It will heal,” Mydei told him with a heavy sigh, eyes still watching the rippling river - and a piece of Phainon was very sure that man was just trying to avoid looking at him. Not that Phainon cared, he didn’t need to be acknowledged to know Mydei needed to at least have that wound cleaned. 

“Come here,” Phainon murmured, but he himself was already moving away to that running river - dipping that foreign cloth in a few times to make sure it was soaked before wringing it out again with a hum over how sticky his gloves were feeling now with the water in them. He probably should have taken them off first, but he felt as though even Mydei didn’t want a corpse touching his wound.

Regardless, he moved once more to that man who was still sitting on that moss covered stump - now with an elbow on his leg to prop his head up using his other cheek, golden eyes staring and watching every single move Phainon made.

And that was fine, Phainon was used to being keenly watched for acts of deception, yet now.. All he could do was move closer to Mydei with a quiet hum leaving his throat. 

“A prince’s gorgeous face is one of their greatest tools, you should strive to protect it better.” Phainon started to say with a heavy sigh escaping him - a piece of him found it almost sweet how when he neared that man he didn’t shy away at all.

Instead, he merely let that wet cloth touch his cheek without even a wince - eyes only staring down Phainon as if he were bored before he gave a quiet sigh over those words. 

“.. Phainon, my outer appearance has little to no value to me.”

Phainon hummed over it, dabbing that cloth and doing his best to wipe the blood away from Mydei’s skin without trying to hurt the man or stretch the gash anymore than it already had been. Dotting and dabbing that cloth all while moving his eyes to look into Mydei’s own, studying  him a little over that.

Something felt off about that, and Phainon had a pretty good guess over why this man no longer cared for such basic things such as looks - but he had to bite his tongue a little. If Mydei had long since given up on himself and his own future outside of slaying the man who had ruined both of their lives, it wasn’t for Phainon to judge him.

Not when his future had been robbed from him all the same, just like Mydei. If anything, a piece of him probably was clinging to Mydei due to that, even. Hoping that they could be each other’s solace, even if Phainon found himself unable to say the idea outloud to Mydei. 

“Mm,” Phainon began instead, quiet in his tone as he tried to think of what to say to that man who was seeming a bit solemn now, “You say that now, but people still treat you differently based on looks; even if they refuse it.”

Mydei didn’t reply to that - even flicking his eyes away and to the side, clearly trying his best to ignore the talk that was building up from Phainon in favor of staring into the nearby river. But Phainon didn’t mind that, after all, as he’s said before; he’s used to people ignoring him while he spoke to them. 

“A pretty prince, who they may or may not know is a prince, will always earn the trust of others easier than an ugly and scary man would..” Phainon mumbled as he moved to continue wiping away smeared blood from the tanned skin of Mydei’s cheek - doing his best to be as tender as possible as he moved his clumsy fingers across his skin.

Doing his best not to truly take in how pretty that man was - he had thought of it so many times before, but with their new distance of Phainon leaning over him to take care of him.. Those gold flakes in his eyes were catching the sun just right, making them glow and shimmer in the daylight all while appearing more and more like a hunter’s. A feline on the prowl with such a heavy jawline that Phainon found himself almost envious of it. 

Truly, a prince with his looks - even if Mydei was in denial of such a thing nowadays. 

“So you should do your best to protect your looks,” Phainon sighed out as he instead folded the cloth to a section that was less bloody - still trying his best to clean at the wound laying in Mydei’s cheek. 

“.. That would be easier done if the man following me around didn’t yell my name so loudly,” Mydei grumbled after a few moments of heavy silence and patting from Phainon, all to make Phainon shake his head with a little chuckle. 

“My apologies, my lord.” Phainon huffed out as he instead turned back to that river to rinse that cloth again, doing his best to not note how much blood had soaked into it. Mydei didn’t seem affected or bothered, but that must at least sting greatly. 

“‘My lord’, and why is that the title you’ve taken for me?” Mydei asked while Phainon had his back turned - making him turn slightly to look at Mydei as he wringed that rag once more. Blinking at the way Mydei was obviously in pain, his jaw was so very tight that he was blatantly gritting his teeth; and Phainon almost felt foolish for not noticing it before.

.. Was he truly taking in the pretty looks of Mydei so closely that he hadn’t even realized he was in agony?

“How do I say this..?” Phainon started with a shake of his head as he moved back to that man - ignoring the heavy droplets of water falling from the cloth in favor of returning to Mydei’s side quicker, “I feel most comfortable when being just a lowly lapdog to royalty, I guess.”

Mydei didn’t reply to that - not instantly, instead only staring at Phainon as he slowly decided to dab away the sweat at Mydei’s forehead this time. Softly pressing the cooled cloth against his skin to try his best to distract the man from whatever pain he was feeling in his face - all before languidly lowering his hands down Mydei’s features once more. 

Not really in a rush to get back to that gash, even as blood was beginning to bead there once more, instead taking his time to wash the other side of Mydei’s cheek as he removed it from being propped up rather obediently. 

“.. Pardon me?”

Phainon found himself chuckling over that, basking in the way those golden eyes narrowed towards him as he moved to that wound again, “I’m trusting you, Mydeimos.”

“Why? What have I done to earn such trust? For all you can prove, I am the man who slaughtered my entire kingdom and perhaps I even control the king ruining your kingdom,” Mydei growled out without missing a single beat.

And that was strange.

It was odd to Phainon how this man always seemed to want to put distrust back into Phainon’s heart, and something about it felt as though Mydei was the one hoping Phainon wouldn’t trust him. As if he didn’t think he deserved such a thing for some reason.. Phainon couldn’t place it, regretfully, instead having to sigh over it. 

“Perhaps! But I have a sneaking suspicion that you’re not.” Phainon murmured beneath his breath, it wasn’t really ‘sneaking’ at all. Not when he knew Mydei wasn’t.

Nothing added up about the man, sure, but there was one thing that did make perfect sense; he really hated that man that was walking around as ‘Kephale’, and Phainon had to agree with him there.

They both despised that man, and absolutely wanted him dead and buried - and hopefully staying dead and buried once they were done with him.

“You’re hiding something, that much is obvious. But hiding murdering me..? I don’t think so.” Phainon rambled onwards as he patted at that man’s cheek again - feeling his brows knitting together as he thought about it again.

He had thought about it so much, after all, ever since deciding to work with Mydei it was practically all he had been able to think about. 

“You were always odd in our duels, your undead were too kind and gentle; I don’t think you have it in yourself to actually be trying to genocide so many innocent people, let alone your own.” Phainon explained with a shallow laugh leaving his chest - moving his eyes to focus on Mydei’s own which seemed to be studying him so closely. Peering at him for answers.. And Phainon..

He wasn’t sure why his body moved on its own, instead taking up Mydei’s free hand gingerly into his own. 

“Maybe one day you will explain to me what you’re hiding, or maybe one day you will not,” Phainon found himself pressing a kiss to the man’s knuckles, softly and much too kind, hesitating there as he remained kneeling before that prince with a smile on his lips. One that was hidden by that hood, but he was sure Mydei could feel it on his skin. 

Phainon pulled away at that, looking upwards at Mydei who seemed more than a little baffled by the show before him as his eyes stared right back at Phainon. Shocked, baffled, and maybe even confused - those were all emotions shown so obviously on his face now.. 

“But I’m a mere loyal dog, eager to serve, and be praised for my duties when I accomplish them well enough to please you. So for now, you can use me as you wish - so long as you keep me by your side and give me direction in this life I’ve been doomed to.”

Mydei remained silent at that - his eyes as wide as they were, only before slowly returning to the man’s normalcy of stoicness. As if it was such a practiced act and Phainon had to resist the urge to wipe away at Mydei’s cheek again, unsure if it was due to the blood there now or something more.

Some odd desire to touch the man’s face and try to make it melt into something softer - yet, Mydei didn’t seem keen on that idea. Instead narrowing his eyes and looking almost.. Perturbed over those words. 

“You start a ruckus that gets me wounded, and then kneel before me begging to be allowed to stay by my side?” Mydei asked, his tone sounding high-strung and on edge, but something about it was throwing off Phainon in more ways than one as he blinked at that prince. Unable to truly fathom what he was feeling, nor what Mydei could possibly be feeling. 

“I refuse,” Mydei growled out, immediately taking his hand from Phainon’s own and making Phainon bite his lower lip the tiniest amount - probably hard enough to draw blood, but with the lack of blood in his body; he could never tell anymore, “You are a lost pup looking for his master, but that is not me.”

Phainon wasn’t breathing - he knew that much, sure, he didn’t need to breathe in the first place but those words had robbed him of all his air regardless. Leaving him to drown in a numb feeling as he stared just a tad upwards towards the man who was denying him; denying his service, and his companionship.

All while golden eyes looked right back at him - harsh and cold as he remained so fixed in this path. 

“You are not my dog, nor are you my knight. Stand on your own two feet and live for yourself for once, Phainon,” Mydei instructed him in such a foreign tone that Phainon couldn’t even truly comprehend it.

Was Phainon truly the issue here? Did Mydei merely hate the idea of his companionship that much, or was there something more?

.. Was Phainon even in the right state of mind to try to question Mydei as he let out a pained little laugh over those words; “How am I intended to live for myself, when my life ended months ago, Mydeimos?”

Phainon had to snap his mouth shut over that as he watched that prince immediately move his gaze away from him - no longer lingering on Phainon and listening to whatever he had to say and now focused back on that river. Blatantly not wanting to give him anymore attention, and that only made Phainon’s sinking panic a bit worse.

The refusal was fine, Phainon could handle being denied and shot down - what he couldn’t stand was the way that man seemed to no longer even want to give him any attention. 

“Sorry, that’s not something you have to give me an answer to,” Phainon tried to repair it, chuckling a little nervously as he instead clenched onto that cloth in his hand - moving once more to dab at Mydei’s cheek with precision and care, “I need to find my own way, right?”

Mydei still didn’t look at him with that question, his head instead returning to his position of lazing a top of his hand as he seemed to be looking to the water for answers; “.. Right.”

“Will you wait for me?”

Those words left Phainon’s mouth before he himself even had a chance to think twice about them. Words that were sputtered and hurried as his own breathing felt more erratic the longer he thought on how this man had already denied him. 

Though, those words did one decent thing as golden eyes blinked and slid back to him once more - staring him down before giving him an odd look. The briefest expression of confusion.

“Wait for you?” Mydei echoed, and Phainon couldn’t even blame him for being confused over how abrupt the question was and how.. Mydei really had no reason at all to care or wait for Phainon.

“Until I find my own answer that I can give you. Will you wait for me, Mydeimos?” Phainon asked that all while still gently wiping away blood that was now ceasing its flow - no longer dripping down Mydei’s face messily to remind Phainon of his failures.

That wound was his fault - the pain Mydei felt was his fault, and now that man was still glaring at him in such an annoyed fashion..

“You’re asking a prince to wait on a knight?” Mydei asked in an almost snarl, seeming as if he were truly reaching his limit with his rage. 

But Phainon couldn’t help himself, leaning back a little from Mydei’s face to cock his head to the side, “Oh, so now you’re a prince when it comes to declining me?” 

Mydei’s mouth snapped shut over that in a way that was almost stunning for Phainon - especially as those amber eyes dipped away from him again. No longer wanting to look at him once more, and that.. Phainon really didn’t enjoy that feeling he was becoming so familiar with, watching the way Mydei didn’t seem keen on replying to that tease. 

“I’m teasing, Mydei! Don’t give me the silent treatment! You are a prince, even if it’s just for me,” Phainon chirped out as he removed that cloth from Mydei’s face once more - giving up due to the way Mydei’s blood had ceased seeping from the wound now, “I’ll keep your secret just between us, you can be my prince.”

Phainon was doing his best to make his words alluring - to make that man look at him again and give him that odd sense of attention he felt himself craving from Mydei.

Only, Mydei didn’t. 

“No,” Mydei instead flatly replied, eyes only narrowing a bit more as he focused on that river as if it were the most interesting thing in the entire world,  “I lost myself for a moment there, you’re not incorrect.”

Lost himself for a moment.

Phainon found his mind pausing over those words, trying to figure out what they all meant while he only became more and more confused by it. Had Mydei been.. Enjoying himself and their bickering? 

“I am no one’s prince anymore, and especially not yours.” Mydei unceremoniously grumbled out, all before not missing a single beat or breath between the both of them as he immediately moved. Standing on his feet again and turning swiftly to leave that small clearing the two of them had been resting in.

“Mydeimos,” Phainon tried to get that man to stop - unsure of what he could even exactly say to do such a thing,  “Don’t leave now, you’re still bleeding!”

“I can dress my own wounds,” Mydei told him in such a stern voice that had a double meaning behind it rather blatantly. 

Mydei didn’t want to be chased right now..

And yet.. 

Phainon found himself sitting back on his haunches over that - blinking as he stared after that man’s back with an odd twisting feeling gnawing into his stomach. 

This was a bizarre sensation he kept feeling when it came to messing up with Mydei - one that screamed at him to chase after that man and beg him for forgiveness, all while being almost too nervous to do such a thing. Would Mydei think he was a fool to come whining to him, or was Mydei also hoping that Phainon followed him just like normal?

He had no idea as he moved his eyes to look at his bloodied handkerchief, staring at the red blotches there before hanging his head a little with a heavy sigh leaving him. Truthfully, he was clinging to Mydei in search of his own purpose, but the man wasn’t wrong.

Mydei himself couldn’t be the sole answer to making him happy when he already was dead and walking around the living. There had to be more to his life than just serving some man who had royal blood flowing through his veins.

.. Right?

He was trying to tell himself that, but every time he thought of what he wanted to do, there were two simple answers that came to mind.

One was the obvious, to slay ‘Kephale’ and try to fix his kingdom, to do his best for them and try to help them find their footing again. 

Yet the second, the second was convoluted to his own mind and heart; he wanted to stay by Mydei’s side. Even after that prince got his revenge and decided to permanently leave Aedes Elysiae, that thought, that knowledge that Mydei would leave and never look back - never look or meet Phainon again..

.. That much was haunting him. 

Would Mydei really leave and never speak to Phainon again? Were they still just enemies working towards a common goal and one day Mydei would grow past him..?

Phainon had to hang his head and sigh over that - instead moving to rinse that cloth out again before leaning back on his ass and staring into that river. 

He desperately needed to solve what he could possibly do with his life after they killed that monster; but every bone in his body was telling him to follow that blond haired man to the ends of the world.

.. And he really had no idea why he felt so.. Drawn to Mydei of all people. 

──────────────

Phainon’s eyes never quite got used to sights like this as he awoke - groggily still moving to rub at his eyes as he swept his view over the mess of magical candles. All flickering that eerie yet vibrant green light that assuredly gave off more sight than normal candles - but in trade they gave Phainon goosebumps when he looked at them for too long.

All before his eyes found that man in the center of it all - a mess of papers laid out around him that Phainon still couldn’t read or understand at all. If anything, these looked more like runes than letters this time around, but his mind couldn’t comprehend even those pictures. 

“What’s all of this?” Phainon asked with a yawn on his lips as he moved to stretch - eyes looking behind him for just a moment at that bed he had crawled out of. Still, a heavy sleeper, but he had trouble falling asleep usually.

.. Not for reasons you would expect, but instead due to the fact he had been sharing a bed with that fallen prince. Unable to fall asleep very quickly due to the way Mydei was always just a breath away, often that led him to staying up and staring at the ceiling while listening to the other man breathe peacefully.

A soft noise that soothed him in a way he didn’t quite understand fully, but it most likely was due to the fact he himself no longer had to breathe at all.

“Necromancy,” Mydei replied flatly, making Phainon move his eyes forward as he leaned on that doorway - a sigh on his lips over that reply as his eyes watched that man in the middle move his hand to one of those papers and peer at it particularly hard.

As if he was reading or concentrating on it, but Phainon couldn’t say.

.. Phainon was finding out he couldn’t do a lot of things in regards to this man. 

“Right, in what depth?” Phainon asked with a roll of his eyes as he moved closer - just a few steps before hunching over to look at those papers. Eyes scanning them but not really making out that red ink smeared across the pages messily, such a deep red that Phainon found himself almost.. Worried.

He had seen a lot of blood in his days, on the battlefield and off, and this.. 

“.. I hope you do not think I plan on fighting fair with that flesh walker, Mr. Knight,” Mydei spoke after a few moments, making Phainon straighten himself out and stare at the back of Mydei’s head once more.

He barely actually knew anything about this man.

He had a decent grip on the type of personality Mydeimos had beneath it all and his layers, but there were no signs of what his goals were beyond just killing that man. A piece of Phainon found himself yearning to know what Mydei was like before all of this, but..

A piece of him also feared learning it, for some odd reason. 

Thus, all he could do was sigh over ‘Mr. Knight’ being used again, “Surely you and I have moved past just our titles, haven’t we?”

“Have we?” Mydei countered, making Phainon raise his brows curiously at how annoyed Mydei was sounding currently, “You seem rather keen on reminding me that I was once a prince, I assume it is only fair I do the same for you.”

Ah.

Mydei was still bothered over that conversation at the river, then? 

Well, Phainon could easily say he was as well - no one enjoyed being denied and shoved away, but he knew he had to take that on the chin regardless due to it being Mydei’s choice. But that didn’t mean he wasn’t feeling just a tad bit bitter over it. Bitter, and sad. 

.. More sad than bitter, really. The idea of them both going their own ways could probably make Phainon slam his head into something the more he thought about it. Because who else could accept the company of the undead better than a necromancer? If anything, Phainon had to think he was made for Mydei, a prince who was a necromancer..

That was somehow right up his alley now! 

“A knight for a kingdom that wants nothing to do with me, thus we can leave ourselves at that distance as well.” Mydei only continued on, making Phainon blink and stare at that man - brows furrowing together as he tried to process what was actually being said to him right now. 

“.. What are you saying?”

Mydei sighed over that question - a heavy thing as he turned just a little bit, enough for Phainon to catch sight of those burning golden eyes that seemed to glare knives into his skin. 

“The sooner we end his rule, the faster you and I may leave each other’s company,” Mydei explained in a tone that made Phainon cock his head to the side, “It’s a win in many regards.”

A win.

Was that a victory? Phainon really didn’t think so as his brows became knitted together - fully aware of his missing hood so this man could easily see his expressions. Not that Phainon cared, if anything, he preferred that man fully knowing that Phainon was upset by the idea of them both going their own separate ways. 

“‘A kingdom that wants nothing to do with me’ he says, as if the villagers don’t fawn over you and adore you,” Phainon pointed out with a lazy wave of his hand - doing his best to hold in the heavy sigh that ran through his body over it, “What brought this sort of talk on, Mydeimos? If the prince thing really bothers you so much, I will not bring it up again.”

Mydei only continued to stare at him with the question, face changing and flickering through certain emotions that Phainon couldn’t quite put a name to. 

“You,” Mydei said in such a tired tone, sighing a little before he shook his head and narrowed his eyes towards Phainon, “You’re the thing that bothers me.”

Phainon wasn’t even sure how to react to that - jerking his head backwards just a tiny bit before he scoffed a little loudly. Arm on his hip as his jaw tightened and gave an incredulous look at that necromancer over that; “.. Excuse me?”

“We..” Mydei’s head turned at that, focusing back on whatever his current work was, “We just need to solve this matter and part ways.”

Phainon had no idea what to make of those words - feeling his brows knit together all before he felt himself settling on what exactly to think of it all.

Disbelief. 

Phainon couldn’t quite shake himself out of that feeling - instead giving a little scoff, a quiet and offended sounding thing as he shook his head rather languidly the more he thought about it, “.. You want to get rid of me that badly, Mydeimos?”

Mydei didn’t reply to that, seeming more interested in his own work yet again - and that was enough to make Phainon grit his teeth. Staring at the way he seemed to be smearing his own blood onto papers to write those runes himself - all to add to Phainon’s mounting frustration over how he couldn’t even read it.

Eyes sweeping around the mess of papers to note how much of Mydei’s own blood had been used for this to unfold.

Enough to where he found himself exhaling a bit deeply - scowling at that man; “Don’t give me the silent treatment now, not when this conversation is serious.”

Mydei let out a heavy noise - one that seemed strained and forced as his head sunk down a little bit lower, deeper and defeated. A posture that didn’t fit the man Phainon had come to know, not at all. 

“Do you not wish to split up as-”

“Are you foolish?” Phainon instantly hissed out, watching the way those words made Mydei snap his head back to the side to look at Phainon in his clear bafflement, “Asking me if it’s mutual, as if I hadn’t already tried to become your knight who would stay by your side throughout everything that may come after.”

Phainon could barely understand this line of thought - knitting his brows together before biting into his own bottom lip harshly. Enough to where he knew he would be bleeding if possible, all before clicking his tongue over those round golden eyes staring at him in sheer awe. 

“And you’re asking me if I agree or not? You’re not that dense, Mydeimos. So why?”

Mydei seemed to take a moment with those words, as if he were thinking deeply on what kind of answer he could even give to Phainon. But Phainon already knew his reply didn’t truly matter - Phainon found he would follow this man to the ends of the world if he could, and the idea of Mydei pushing people away from fear.. That was one Phainon had to assume was reality the more he thought of it.

“.. What kind of knight are you to swear yourself to a necromancer? Surely you can find a better use of your time.” Mydei grumbled out before moving one of his own bloody fingers to that parchment before him again - smoothly circling something with the drips of his own blood. A valuable thing that Phainon found himself scowling over the more he saw Mydei writing with it. 

“No,” Phainon huffed out, moving his arms to cross over his own chest as he watched Mydei merely continue his messy word, “You are more than just a necromancer, and I am now more than just a knight.”

Those words were true, and they were even more true to Phainon’s heart than merely how lightly he had uttered them. To his heart, they were a heavy weight that was pressing on his mind every single time he looked at that man.

A man who was running away from his history of being a prince due to his people already being gone and decaying behind him, all while accepting the role of a necromancer being his true title. But if that was true, if Mydei was fine with being a necromancer, why would a knight who already was dead not be his best companion?

Phainon was perfect for Mydei, just like Mydei was perfect for him - and Phainon was aware of that much now. 

“I may be loyal and desiring to serve, but that is even in death, Mydeimos. For who could I better serve than the prince of necromancers?” Phainon argued as he watched that man’s bloodied finger pause - dragging down the paper a little all before he tilted his head upwards, just enough to throw an annoyed stare at the man standing a foot behind him. 

“.. Don’t conjure up new titles for me in your head.”

New titles? Phainon wasn’t even sure if he had done that much, if anything, Mydei was working on earning it himself. Nothing more, nothing less.

And yet, Phainon smiled softly at Mydei over it; “Why not? I rather like that one!”

“You are insufferable.” Mydei mumbled out with a shake of his head and a heavy exhale leaving his chest - as if this topic was truly aging him but Phainon.. Couldn’t let go of it.

He couldn’t let go of Mydei that easily, he didn’t think he ever could, either. Not anymore.

“And you’re trying to shut me out, why is that?” Phainon asked in a soft tone, trying to be sweet as honey all while finding his own words choking and clawing at his throat,  “What could a man fear so much in other people, that he won’t even allow the dead to stay by his side?”

“That’s..” Mydei wasn’t moving as he spoke that word.

Instead, going rather rigid as he kept his head down now, as if the papers in front of him were the most interesting things in the world - and they probably would be to Phainon if he could read or understand them. But for now, Phainon found himself rolling his eyes over the way Mydei had practically shut down to try to form an argument against Phainon. 

“Come here,” Phainon hissed as he instead grabbed at Mydei’s arm, no longer willing to hear that man out while his hands were still seeping out that crimson liquid so freely. Tugging Mydei to his feet and quickly yanking him along - head shaking as he breathed out a shaky sigh. 

“What are you doing? I’m busy,” Mydei said those words, sure, but Phainon was taking note of the way he easily gave in and rose to his feet. Allowing Phainon to drag him out of that cave without much of a second though. 

And it wasn’t as if Mydei lacked the strength to yank his arm free - they both knew he could, and yet.. 

“You’re bleeding.” Phainon growled out quietly, as if that was all of the explanation Mydei needed as he instead opened the shabby door to that cave to expose them both to some much needed sunshine. Pausing his feet a little to try to gauge if he should wear his hood or not, but if he was just going to wash Mydei, it was fine.

Mydei at those two simple words, however, sighed as loudly as possible. A dramatic sound from behind Phainon as he still kept his hand curled around Mydei’s own arm - pulling him forward still and to the nearby creek with nice running water. 

“It’s a part of the ritual, you fool.” Mydei countered after a few beats of silence between the crunching of Mydei’s shoes against the forest floor and Phainon’s lack of them. 

Though, Phainon found himself scoffing over that - rolling his eyes a little. 

“Yeah, well, taking care of you is now a part of my own ritual, you fool.”

Mydei copied that scoffing noise over that - all before giving a small chuckle, a quiet and weak sounding thing compared to normal, but at least it was there.

“You bicker like a child, even when dead.”

“Be quiet.”

Mydei seemed to actually listen to that, no longer finding the need to say anything more apparently as he just allowed himself to be dragged along. And Phainon was thankful for that as he approached that familiar creek they both had been using for bathing - an area he felt a bit odd over considering he wasn’t even sure if bathing worked for him.

But Mydei claimed that it did, even if Phainon was a tad bit scared of rotting, Mydei seemed to disagree and even fought against laughing at the idea of water rotting Phainon.

.. Phainon knew he was fighting against laughing because the prince really wasn’t good at hiding it with his lips quivering and doing his best to look anywhere but at Phainon while coughing to clear his throat multiple times. 

Phainon now, however, was forcing that man to sit on the bank - sighing a little as he had a strange sense of deja vu. Moving to inspect Mydei’s hands and the mess of cuts there - only to feel himself gritting his teeth the longer he looked at them.

Calloused, battleworn, and respectable - naturally. But the deeper lines that were flared up, bumps of skin healing over previous wounds, slices carved so on purpose on his palms. Phainon almost would have worried more about the meaning behind why Mydei would do that to himself, if he wasn’t very aware this bloodletting was for those rituals of his.

All on his palms, as if he had been squeezing out the blood himself - which well, Phainon knew he had been, and yet.. 

“If you needed blood, you could have..” Phainon didn’t like how heavy the tail end of his words clung to his lips - trailing off as he knitted his brows at his own uselessness. He couldn’t even aid Mydei in this, not when he had no blood to give to that man - instead remaining kneeled down before him before sighing. Eyes flicking upwards to peer at Mydei instead,  “Why do you need blood?”
