Only, Mydei looked a little amused by it. 

“You would have let me use your own blood?” He finished Phainon’s sentence with a lick of humor in his words. 

“Well..” Phainon huffed a little, not even wasting a moment of time before moving to lean back on his feet - suddenly regretting the fact he hadn’t brought anything to actually clean Mydei’s hands with,  “I don’t.. Really have that anymore, but..”

He trailed off, unsure of what to say as he only stared at Mydei’s hands. Hands he was holding in his own and often found himself baffled with how gentle their touch was - kind-hearted and welcoming. A vast difference from what he knew of Kremnos and their wars, and still.. This man had been oddly nothing but kind to him.

If anything, the cruelest thing he had done to Phainon was refuse his company - and Phainon could do little more than stare at those hands that didn’t seem fit to be a necromancer. Not made to kill and use the undead, if anything, they seemed as if they were destined for the opposite - only for fate to be so painfully cruel. 

“Everyone around me dies.”

Those words were said so plainly that Phainon felt his entire body tense up - pausing as his eyes still raked over Mydei’s hand, doing his best to understand the words he was hearing all before tilting his head upwards a little. Glancing into those golden eyes that merely stared right back at him, no hesitation or fear behind them - only fierce and studying as he looked right back at Phainon. 

“.. Pardon?”

“I was not alone on that scouting trip my mother sent me away on, yet I was the only one to return to our kingdom alive.” Mydei replied without missing a single second - all to continue staring at Phainon in the eyes a bit eerily, “Do you know why that is?”

“I..” Phainon tried to speak, but he had no idea what to say to that - let alone what to think over randomly being told this. 

In his head, he fully knew Mydei was forcing himself to be vulnerable, to be honest and open - but right now.. Phainon wasn’t exactly sure what to say to it. 

“Poison testers for the royal family. We’re expected to wait and eat last when out on trips like that, all while our companions eat varied meals for the most safety,” Mydei explained with a shrug of his shoulders rather lazily - moving a little to close his eyes as he spoke, “And yet, everything was poisoned and they all were dead within minutes.”

Mydei blinked them open abruptly once more - focusing on the sun above them with a steady gaze. One that made Phainon wonder just what on earth that man was actually thinking about as he stared upwards - blinking a little his own eyes still looked to those cuts and scars on Mydei’s hands. 

“There was no time to grieve for them, not when even returning home only brought more solitude.”

Truth be told; Phainon had expected something along these lines, the words of a man who was a bit more guarded nowadays due to grief and loss. But Phainon.. Was the same as him, deep down. No one was left, the people of Aedes Elysiae were already lost - few remained, but even they were older and had begun speaking of leaving their homes as well.

They both had no one, no one but each other; but Phainon.. Found comfort in that.

More importantly, he found comfort in that necromancer. 

“Tell me,” “If you lost everyone in your life within a span of just a few mere hours, would you be keen on letting someone you care about in? Or would you fear they too, would begin to finally erode away?”

Someone you care about.

And those words were directed at and about Phainon, of all people, so sweetly and genuinely said that he couldn’t help but bite into his lips over it. 

“Mydei,” Phainon breathed out - knitting his brows together as he slowly moved rubbed his thumb against the back of Mydei’s hand, “I don’t know how to tell you this, but I’m already a rotting corpse. I’m not exactly going to be killed in front of you, at least, not in a way that matters.”

Mydei’s eyes lingered on him at that; taking a few heavy seconds to stare at Phainon and attempt to pry into his thoughts. An expression that made Phainon smile at him a little weakly, doing his best to comfort that man who seemed so distressed right now. All while Phainon still had one of his hands in his own hands, gently cradling the wounded part of Mydei. 

“I don’t need your answer yet, but don’t write me out of your life just yet, alright?” Phainon tried to comfort another piece of Mydei, doing his best to smile at the way Mydei’s own expression seemed much too soft and fragile,  “At least count on me a little.”

“You may.. Be the biggest fool I’ve ever met.” Mydei mumbled in such a soft little voice - taking his hands away from Phainon rather leisurely. 

“You know what they say,” Phainon spoke as he leaned back a little - cracking a smile at that necromancer who he was undoubtedly beginning to feel something more for, “The bigger the person is.. The bigger their heart?”

Mydei cocked his head to the side at that; “.. Who says that?”

“Me now, suddenly.” 

“In another life, you were probably a dog.” Mydei told him with a little laugh, and Phainon found himself shaking his head and chuckling as well - only to watch that man as he stood and seemed to mess with his hands once more. Fumbling with them just a little. 

In another life, I was probably your knight from the very beginning. 

Those were the words Phainon wanted to say, and yet nothing came out from his lips - instead, he gave Mydei a somber little smile.

“Let’s go bandage your hands, alright? I don’t need my necromancer getting sick,” Phainon mused - trying his best to ignore the way he desperately wanted to hold that man in a way he didn’t quite comprehend. Hands itching to grab at Mydei’s own once more, only fumbling and twitching at his side instead - mainly due to his desire not to hurt those already wounded hands.

.. And due to his own ebbing cowardice over how much he desired closeness with that man.

Whatever those feelings were creeping into him - he knew killing ‘Kephale’ came first, at the very least.

Chapter End Notes

Chapter Notes

i couldn't decide whether to post this today or wait a bit and instead post my new chaptered fic but uhhh tired of looking at this big ass chapter OLOLKFREDL.SGR

“A lich.”

Phainon found himself nodding to that, doing his best to act as if he knew what was going on in this conversation - sure, sure. He was focused and listening to Mydei, but that didn’t mean he understood what that pretty man was talking about. Instead, he was merely blinking and watching the way Mydei’s eyelashes fluttered softly as he scribbled on some papers.

Soft and gentle, much too kind for this world as Mydei seemed focused on his work, and yet.. 

“And.. What is that?” Phainon had to ask, feeling a little foolish for being so clueless - but he really was doing his best here, he promises! He’s just.. Out of his depth, that’s all. 

“It’s what I assume ‘Kephale’ actually is - hiding away in a phylactery somewhere in the castle.” Mydei mumbled as his eyes stayed focused on his work, dancing a little but never looking upwards at Phainon. If anything, he seemed much too focused, too intent.. 

Something about it made Phainon feel almost antsy, genuinely curious and nervous towards the one lurking thought in his mind.

Mydei had every intention of killing Kephale soon, didn’t he?

“Mhm..” Phainon hummed as he stared at Mydei writing in that language he still was not privy to, tilting his head a little, “What is a ‘phylactery’?”

Mydei sighed over that, moving to look up from his papers in the middle of that small cave area to instead look Phainon in the eyes; “.. A really fancy vase that most likely is covered with curses to keep his soul that's entombed inside of it safe.”

Phainon had to hum over that description, all before moving to place his hands on his hips with his own eyes flitting away. Just to inspect the papers Mydei was working on, and for once, finding himself relaxing when he did realize that man was not writing in red.

.. Emphasis on ‘for once’, it felt like every single day that man found a reason to use his own blood for things while driving Phainon up the wall.

“Oh, I’m rather fond of antiques.. I remember most of the ones in the castle, honestly. But, ah.. Curses?” Phainon mumbled before dragging a hand up to his chin, rubbing it a bit idly as he closed his eyes.

When he was there working up that assumed lich for months, he couldn’t quite remember seeing any new vases or the likes. If anything, he was probably the person who took the most notice of new items or treasures like that being added to their treasury halls or elsewhere.

The idea of a new antique being around and him never noticing it was low, but maybe it was truly hidden just that well - and that was.. Probably the truth. A secret locked door, or one invisible through the use of magic, the possibilities were endless, and at the end of the day.. Phainon at his core was just some guy working as a knight for a king he thought he loved, not his corpse.

Though, in his own thoughts, he didn’t even take note of the way Mydei was scrutinizing him, staring at him before dipping his eyes away as Phainon lowered his own to meet Mydei’s once more. 

“Interesting,” Mydei hummed out in a tone that Phainon couldn’t quite read - as if he was actually amused by learning that information as he instead focused on his papers again, “Traps of various sorts, I assume whoever comes closest to it will perish rather quickly.”

“What about if I went close to it? Dead and all..” Phainon offered, watching the way Mydei’s hands paused for the briefest of moments. 

All before Mydei pressed out a sigh and moved to trace his fingers over one of the tome’s letterings on the front. A gentle touch that Phainon had to blink over - staring at the way the language on the front was foreign to him. 

A common thing to happen to him, but he really did find himself a bit baffled over how many languages this man had taken up learning. Or did they all have something to do with necromancy and Phainon was merely a confused and lost puppy in that regard?

“.. I would rather not.”

Those words were spoken rather quietly, so much so that Phainon thought Mydei was almost.. Solemn sounding? Depressed, even? Or was he worried about something?

Those thoughts were enough to make Phainon hum a little, stepping forward before rounding the front of Mydei - his eyes darting to look at those mystical green lanterns before joining Mydei on the floor. 

“Oh? Why is that?” Phainon was genuinely asking, unable to stop the way this made him feel so very curious about this topic as he tilted his head to the side. Trying his best to focus on Mydei as that man seemed more intrigued by opening that book from before, immediately flipping through the pages of it as if he were in a hurry. 

“He would most likely shatter my.. Hold over you.” Mydei admitted, though, he was mumbling out every word - and Phainon found himself leaning back onto his hands with that confession. Lazily sitting there across from Mydei with his legs crossed - blinking at the way Mydei seemed so.. Distracted, today. 

He could understand it, the man seemed to be looking for something or researching something - but that didn’t make Phainon any less nosy.. 

Though, that did enough to jar Phainon’s mind - making him slowly rake his eyes over that man who was furrowing his brows together. So genuinely focused on what he was doing to where Phainon wasn’t sure if he was the insane one here or not. 

“Hold?” Phainon echoed out, unable to stop the way he kept his head tilted as he watched Mydei - keenly and so honestly waiting for a reply to explain it all.

But that only made Mydei  give a heavy sounding sigh before he closed that book once more - instead flitting his gaze upwards to meet Phainon’s own eyes with a rather.. Harrowing expression burrowed beneath them. 

“For lack of a better term, yes. I believe he would easily override my own attempts to free you if you were that close with his soul, he would shatter it with ease.” Mydei explained to him in a solemn sounding voice - making Phainon 

“You have such little faith in your own skills?” Phainon asked, mainly in a teasing tone - hoping to relieve some of the tension in Mydei’s mind. Yet, Mydei only continued staring at him with that rather particular looking  

Mydei shook his head a bit languidly over it - as if he didn’t understand Phainon’s attempt to be rationalized, “.. He is a disembodied soul commanding legions of the undead and slaughtering entire kingdoms with ease while using dead kings like puppets.”

“I see your point.” Phainon admitted before uncrossing his legs just to sprawl them out in front of him, beaming a little smile over the way one of Mydei’s brows raised incredulously over that,  “So we.. Just need to cleanse the vase, somehow?”

“The easiest method is to shatter it.” Mydei agreed with a small little nod of his head, a movement that made Phainon click his tongue a little.

He really didn’t like the idea of that..

Did they.. Really have to break an antique? Couldn’t they just get a pastor or something to throw holy water at it, instead? 

Phainon had to sigh over his own thoughts - eyes drifting to that rocky ceiling above both their heads as he tried to puzzle it out more and more, “.. This is my nightmare, I think. Is there really no way to save the vase?”

“Why is the vase your worry?” Mydei immediately asked, and that was enough to make Phainon dramatically hang his head in a newfound depression.

They were not saving that poor vase, that much was obvious.. 

“Sorry, right, right.”

Mydei was quiet for a moment over that - and Phainon had no idea why until he slowly raised his head once more. Swallowing just a little harshly as those fierce golden eyes burned into him and were peering at him in sheer disbelief. 

All before Mydei shook his head once more, leisurely, and so judgemental in his movement that Phainon felt as if he were a drowning goldfish who was also on fire, or something.

He felt bad, that’s all you need to know.

“.. Really, we should try to employ a paladin, but it would be rather difficult considering both of our occupations.” Mydei mumbled under his breath, and Phainon wanted to huff over that - but really.. What kind of paladin who worshiped the holy-ness of the world and purified evil would want to hang out with a dead man walking, and a necromancer?

.. They should just go for Phainon’s plan of dousing the vase in holy water, instead. Sounds less like they would be killed by their companion that way, at least. 

But the more Phainon thought on it, the more insane he felt as he moved to cross his arms over his chest with a heavy and drawn out sigh escaping him - once again raising his eyes to the ceiling as he did his best to ignore how silly he must look.. His legs straight out in front, arms crossed over his chest.. He even felt like he was being a pouty child, but maybe he deserved that much.

.. The vase did nothing wrong, okay? 

“We’re fighting an army, and their commander is just hiding in a little glass decoration..?” Phainon asked as he blinked at Mydei, looking for confirmation in that man who had opened his book once more - seeming as if he was reignited in his search for something that Phainon wasn’t privy too. 

“Mhm,” He hummed, and that much confirmed it - Mydei was certainly battling some other demon in his mind now. 

“What a headache,” Phainon forced himself to sigh out as he instead moved to pinch the bridge of his nose while closing his eyes. His head was assuredly going to start hurting if the cat and mouse game kept up in regards to Mydei, but.. After this all was done, after that man was slain and they both were free.

.. Phainon could assuredly try to become closer to Mydei without a lick of shame, that much was easy to imagine and keep him in high spirits as he pressed out a lazy sigh. 

“We’ll start by slaying Kephale.” 

Mydei said those words so easily, spoke them so matter-of-factly that Phainon couldn’t help the way he dropped his hand from his face and stared at that man who was only looking at that book still. Appearing as if he were so very busy in his own mind with whatever he wanted to learn before the day was upon them.

But.. Phainon really was struggling to understand why they would want to attack the corpse, and not the vase?

“Huh?”

Phainon found himself gritting his teeth over that, some primal instinct in himself feeling insulted that Mydei would speak about Kephale in such a way. Only.. The more he thought about it, the more his nonbeating heart seemed to flutter as he looked to Mydei - noting the way he felt more attached to this man in some odd way.

That, and he had already accepted Mydei as his new king; even if Mydei had growled and refused, he still felt as though his heart and body belonged to that man to do what he saw fit. 

Thus, Phainon could only hang his head a little and force himself to bite his tongue over his desire to defend Kephale. Kephale was gone, replaced, abused, and mistreated in death.. And now Phainon had to face the future that was calmly sitting right in front of him warmly. 

“We should most likely split up to handle it.” Mydei added with Phainon’s prolonged silence, and that made Phainon cock his head to the side. 

“Split.. Up?” Phainon echoed out, but he still felt baffled beyond belief when he spent more than a mere second considering those words. 

“Mhm,” Mydei hummed in a rather deep and mellow tone, “One for the phylactery, another to keep his mind busy with controlling Kephale.”

Phainon found himself sucking in a breath over that.. Since Mydei had spoken about not wanting Phainon near that evil vase, that meant.. He would be fighting Kephale, himself? 

.. More worryingly, that meant Mydei would be alone, without Phainon by his side? That made Phainon’s hands feel twitchy, uncomfortable as he bit into his lower lip and tried to study the way Mydei was now looking at him. Golden eyes flickering back and forth just a miniscule amount as he studied Phainon’s reaction, taking his time to look at Phainon in a way that Phainon was struggling to understand.

All before Phainon exhaled so painfully deeply; “I refuse.”

“What a petty reason,” Mydei huffed out before sighing to place that book at his side - still open as he instead moved to cross his arms over his chest as if he was prioritizing his moody action over reading, “Have you such little faith in my own prowess that you desire to baby sit me?”

All before after some of the most cruel moments of Phainon’s life - Mydei merely shook his head with a click of his tongue over it. 

“You’re bothersome, but I assumed this would be the case.”

Phainon felt like he was saying this word a lot today, but honestly, he didn’t think he would stop anytime soon either; “.. Huh?”

Phainon couldn’t even stop the way he immediately cocked his head to the side - angling it a little as if the conversation would make more sense at a forty-five degree angle suddenly.

It didn’t, and yet, Mydei only continued with a shrug of his shoulders. 

“It’s why I’ve been spending much of my time making a homunculi to aid us,” Mydei explained as if that were the most logical way to go about the situation at all,  “Flesh abominations are not my strong suit, and I despised the idea of doing such a thing to those who had not wanted such a fate..”

Phainon found himself opening his mouth at that - trying to think of a reply before snapping his jaw shut once more, feeling more and more insane the longer he took to think about those words. 

Homunculi? He had heard.. Rumors of those - monsters that were demonic in their work and the reason why necromancy was widely outlawed.

.. And the other reasons, of course, but those things were a main one - and Phainon was lucky to have never had run into one in his line of work as a knight but.. Well, apparently his luck was doomed to run out now that he was following a necromancer around - huh?

“Thus, I had to use my blood as offerings to continuously speak with the dead, asking who among them would be willing - and giving them my oath that I will release their souls once more immediately after.”

Well.

That wasn’t doing much to get rid of his fears, Phainon could admit that much as his mind struggled to understand the fact Mydei had claimed to be speaking to the dead.. When on earth had he been doing that? Was he sneaking off while Phainon slept to make that.. Thing and to speak with the dead? 

“W.. What does that mean?” Phainon asked in a confused tone - unable to help his dazed thoughts from bleeding into his tone as he keenly watched Mydei move a little. His head swaying a little as he appeared to try to figure out how to gently explain this.

That much was obvious as Mydei pursed his lips together just the slightest of bits. 

“Quite a few agreed, but naturally, most did not and refused me,” Mydei told him in a voice that was rather hushed - as if this topic was choking him in its own way, “The souls of the anguished and angry dead are hard to barter with, after all.”

Phainon moved a hand up to his eye over that one - rubbing it a bit with his palm to try to figure out what to even make out of the idea of Mydei speaking to the dead still. 

“And.. Speaking with Kremnoans was not an easy task.”

Kremnoans..

That confession had Phainon knitting his brows together - doing his best to understand why Mydei would force that pain on himself.. Seeing people he knew and loved again, all to ask them to.. Become whatever he did to them?

“You.. Spoke with the deceased Kremnoans?” Phainon choked out, moving a little to fiddle with his hands - popping his fingers before really even pausing to wonder if that would have negative effects on his body or not.

.. He really needed to sit down and have a long talk with Mydei about how his body actually functions once this all was over, because truthfully, he felt as if he were completely in the dark still.

Not really at least, not as he trailed off again before moving a hand to his braid at the side of his head - a thing that had always caught Phainon’s eye, only now Mydei was twirling the gold cuff between his fingers a bit cutely. Looking distracted as if he were doing his best to  figure out what exactly to say. 

All before Mydei huffed and dropped that braid from his fingers once more, “The reasoning isn’t important behind it, but I was doing my utmost to be respectful.”

A simple gesture, merely moving closer to Phainon to help him to his feet at Phainon was powerless to immediately take that hand and let that man pull him with his feet. Once more mourning the fact he couldn’t quite feel the warmth of Mydei’s hand on his own, clicking his tongue a bit bitterly over it.

All before those thoughts vanished as Mydei gave him a little grin, followed by such an innocent sounding sentence; “Mm. Sounds, and looks it - would you like to see?”

“.. Opening the way out of that cave, and looking to Phainon to follow after him - all before continuing on again. 

Movements that made Phainon immediately move to follow after him, his feet feeling heavier and more clumsy than normal. 

Speaking to the souls of the dead, and saying something about being back with working with flesh. Only, this route was different, an area he hadn’t really gone to since being dead - a place that seemed almost untouched as Mydei brushed back bushes and twigs to make way for the both of them with a huff leaving his chest. 

Though, nothing could have possibly prepared Phainon as they finally pushed back another bustle of leaves back - exposing a rather large clearing.

.. But that wasn’t the only thing that now was on display as Phainon’s steps after Mydei suddenly failed him, instead blinking and staring at the new.. Creature.. In front of him. 

“What… Is that?” Phainon creaked out - unable to hold back his sheer awe as he found himself biting into his lips as Mydei didn’t even slow his pace at all. Only walking up to that abomination without a single fear, and Phainon.. Guts and flesh, sewn together messily - hearts moving in places they shouldn’t, much too big - not bigger than the trees, but about half their decent sizes. All while it swayed, a mess of eyes looking in every direction, yet it also focused on none as it seemed unsteady in its movements. As if it couldn’t quite get a foothold, and Phainon wasn’t sure if he wanted it to as his eyes slowly looked at its arms. 

Arms.

If they could even be called that - if anything, they were merely blobs of flesh, mountains of muscles that seemed to pulse with life in a way that made Phainon swallow heavily, feeling his throat bob over his own lack of saliva all while he still found himself stunned. The fingers and limbs that seemed to creak when it moved - all to twitch and jut out in various ways..

The low groaning, that was another thing - mixed with the thunderous heartbeat it seemed to be carrying in its veins and the rumbles of whines. Pitiful, and yet horrifyingly sickening in a way Phainon had never once expected - unable to tear his eyes away from it. 

All while Mydei  approached it - not having a care in the world as he let out a rather amused hum. A sound that was foreign to Phainon’s ears as he looked down at that man. Watching the way he so gently reached out a hand to touch a mound of flesh that could be called a leg for this beast.

“My homunculus," Mydei explained in a quiet tone, all before turning a little to look at Phainon - face as stoic as ever, as if he were waiting to gauge Phainon’s reaction first,   “It should be able to handle a bit of the frontlines.”

Homunculus..

And now.. His eyes were staring at one, face to face with the fact Mydei seemed to be just as capable of creating such a horrid thing as those monsters were..

“I..” Phainon trailed off, trying to figure out what words he even wanted to say before giving it another once over as he inspected the blood that seemed to flow through the monster’s thin pale skin - a sickening sight, truly, “This is demented, Mydeimos.”

That was all he could bring himself to say - he trusted Mydeimos, but this was a bit too much for even himself to stomach.. 

“I told you before, I will not be playing fairly, Mr. Knight.” Mydei huffed out as if he had expected such a reaction before turning to the thing with a rather fond look in his eyes. One that Phainon couldn’t understand at all when he was looking at what could not be explained away as anything but a flesh abomination.

Mydei didn’t look at him though, instead, he remained staring at it - eyes pointed upwards, “It’s quiet, isn’t it?”

And that made Phainon’s hairs rise on ends as he considered that thing listening to them, yet.. 

“Usually homunculi are crying out in anguish, in pain and terrible woe,” Mydei explained without even looking at Phainon, “But it’s quiet.”

Quiet..

Mydei was trying to make a point here, that much was obvious, but Phainon was clueless as to what sort of point the necromancer could be angling for. 

“I’m.. Supposed to ask why, right?”

Mydei scoffed at that, looking at Phainon again with a rather somber looking expression over that pointed question, “It’s due to asking permission, and I’ve not gone against my oath to them.”

Oath.. To them?

Permission?

Phainon had no idea what to even think of all of that, but he had to assume the man was implying he had.. Personally asked if he could do this to all of those people? He had asked the deceased for permission to warp and twist their souls into such a demonic thing like this? 

“Are.. They suffering much?” Phainon chose to ask, feeling his mind reel as he watched that necromancer only appear to admire his own handiwork - all before Mydei made a quiet huffing noise. A quiet exhale, a pained laugh of sorts, just as he looked to Phainon with a rather odd look in his eyes. 

“Extremely.”

A look that made Phainon’s hands twitch, staring at that man who was now speaking so quietly - hushed and monotone, yet it was seeping through with every single action.

Woe..

The absolute woe this man seemed to be in, over his own creation, as if he himself had dreaded making it - and yet, he had. He had gone through with it and had to live with that decision. 

“.. Huh?”

“Being a jumbled mess of souls stitched together is probably more than just agony,” Mydei continued to explain as he moved his eyes back to that monster - seeming a little less fond now, and a little more depressed in a sense that Phainon couldn’t quite grasp.

All before Mydei whispered out something so quiet that it was almost inaudible to Phainon who still hadn’t moved an inch closer; “I’m torturing them.”

“That’s..” Phainon tried to think of what exactly to feel, instead his voice was failing him as his own mind tried to figure out how to comment on it. 

“Are you going to scold me?” Mydei asked, all without looking at Phainon again - instead keeping his eyes focused on that monster. And Phainon was almost horrified to think Mydei was looking at the monstrosity in an endeared type of fashion, his expression much too soft with just the fraying edge of sadness leaking into it. 

.. Phainon really didn’t know what to think of that, not when he considered the target of those feelings were the deceased souls bound together into a fleshy mass of sewn together bodies.. 

“Huh?”

Mydei only blinked and looked at Phainon at that, his head tilting to the side a little, “Chastise me? Scorn me?”

.. Maybe a few months ago, Phainon would have done that. He would have found this action reprimandable, the worst offense ever, and completely disgusting. Yet, now, he could only blink at how that necromancer expected ridicule from him - hatred and rage.

And Phainon always found himself lacking those emotions when he looked at Mydeimos, he found himself.. More relaxed, honestly, when his eyes could land on him and felt safer with the knowledge that he was nearby. 

“If you got permission from them, what right does a lowly knight have to question it?” Phainon asked with a rather quiet laugh leaving his lips - pained and in a struggle as he tried to figure out his thoughts on it all, “.. Besides, I think I myself would have agreed to it, if I were more dead and buried.”

Phainon watched keenly as that seemed to work wonders to settle Mydei - watching the way he leisurely moved his eyes back to that monster before dropping his hand away from it. Looking almost.. Awkward as he stood there just staring at them. 

“Why is it only Kremnoans?” Phainon dared to ask, sucking in a heavy breath as he knit his brows together - he was doing his best to try to understand this man and the sorrow he seemed to be feeling right now.. But he had chosen this? Hadn’t he?

He had picked to torture himself and speak to Kremnoans, and Phainon had no idea what that would fully mean - whether they would be happy to see the prince, or scorn him endlessly..

.. Only Mydei knew what depths his agony had truly been sinking to. 

Mydei sighed over that question - quite loudly as he moved a little to give a small smile to Phainon, one that was more somber than he had seen from the man. One that easily clawed into Phainon’s chest and threatened to burrow into his heart and haunt him the longer he looked at it.

“.. I did not feel right asking anyone but those I failed once before already,” Mydei explained, but that only made that depressing feeling in Phainon’s bones creepingly worse. It almost felt as though it was choking him as he watched the way Mydei focused back on the creature at his side.

Though, even if Phainon tried to ignore that monster - it was nearly impossible due to the size of it, not to mention the awful little hums and thumping noises it was making. Noises of wetness that made Phainon feel as if his skin was crawling when he paid it too much mind, not daring to look at that thing anymore than he had to.

That was Phainon’s true thoughts on the matter as he stared at the prince who was still so painfully focused on that abomination - staring upwards a little all before Mydei shook his head. A chuckle of sorts leaving his lips as well before those striking eyes of his crept back to Phainon’s own.

“Regardless, this is merely a way for Kremnoans to fight once more - and get vengeance on the coward who killed them without a proper honorable fight,” Mydei told him in a now much more light-hearted tone, most likely due to the fact that Kremnoans truly were known for their love for the glory of battle, “My own people sounded the most likely to accept.”

.. It made sense, in a way, that Kremnoans who randomly died of the plague and decayed into nothingness would feel more at peace fighting once more. They seemed the most likely to accept a chance to prove themselves again.. At least, if Phainon was taking all of the rumors about Kremnoan traditions to heart.

Whatever the case, Phainon had to blink at Mydei a little over it.

Stitchcraft.

Phainon didn’t even know what to say as he looked at that .. Thing once more, feeling himself chewing into his own tongue over the way bones seemed to jut out here and there against the sunken in flesh - all before dipping his  eyes away from it.

“But it should suffice with my normal undead and breaking down the front walls to distract Kephale for just a bit.” Mydei only continued to ramble onwards, all before moving his eyes to Phainon with a rather innocent look on his face, “Long enough for you to guide us through and into a back entrance, correct?”

“Will.. They feel pain from their wounds in the fight?” Phainon asked, all while Mydei was beginning to walk towards him once more. And Phainon was so thankful that Mydei had not asked him to come closer to inspect his work, or something. 

.. He hadn’t even thought about how he did not want to even get a single step closer to whatever the hell that thing was. Not due to a distrust in Mydei, no, never that. But a secret, more obvious reasoning (fear). 

“I don’t know, but I hope not.”

Phainon found himself fighting back an odd noise over that, resisting the urge to whimper as Mydei now passed him by once more. 

“Come with me,” Mydei instructed him without so much as looking back at Phainon - making him swallow a little as he stared at that monster that was still oddly swaying. Standing there forebodingly and making Phainon feel as if he were going absolutely insane. 

“You’re just going to leave it here?” Phainon asked as he turned on heel a little to look after Mydei - trying his best to ignore the chill running down his neck over leaving his back vulnerable for that.. Thing..

.. Yet he was pretty sure he would hear it coming anyway. 

Mydei paused at that, copying Phainon just a tad and turning to look at him with an innocent tilt of his head, “.. You want them to come home and sleep with us?”

“N.. No, I’m fine.”

“Mhm.”

“Though, in this instance.. Their own hatred for that lich may sustain them easily enough without much effort from myself..” Mydei only continued his explanation, making Phainon glance over his shoulder a little over the noise of bodies following them, “Souls of the angry dead can be rather.. Peculiar things.”

So many dead corpses followed in Mydei’s wake, and the sight only made his hand twitch a little - moving to his sword at his side that he had a habit of sleeping with. Only to relax a little as they seemed to be keeping their distance, as if they were still too polite in their death to eavesdrop. 

.. What a silly thought. 

“Will.. I decay like them, after Kephale is gone?” Phainon couldn’t help himself but to ask that question as he kept his eyes glued to the other undead, his mind unable to think of a different question when he kept going over Mydei’s words in his head.

Every step he took with Mydei was a step towards Kephale, he understood that now - and yet, he was full of dread that sank and devoured his bones.. 

“No,” Mydei answered much too easily - making Phainon jerk his eyes a little to blink at that prince who still wasn’t really looking at Phainon. Instead he seemed much too focused on the familiar path through these woods and to Kephale,  “He doesn’t quite hold on to your soul..”

“Quite?” Phainon echoed out, unable to fully digest what Mydei was trying to imply here - especially as Mydei gave him a little incredulous look over his parroted out word. Looking at him as if he were truly trying to study something before blinking those meticulous looks away and back towards the road. 

“Worrying about that before a battle can distract your mind. Are you afraid to die, Phainon?” 

That.. Was not a question Phainon had been prepared to answer from Mydei - if anything.. He was not afraid to die, not at all, he.. He was afraid for Mydei to die, his own time had run out and now the sands were spilling from the cup in rivers.

But Mydei? Phainon had no idea how full or empty Mydei’s hourglass was, and he dreaded the thought of it being much closer than he could ever know.

.. It made him sick to even think about. 

“No, I’m.. Already dead, I was just curious,” Phainon flippantly muttered, doing his best to look elsewhere before creasing his brows a little in thought. Trying his best to ignore the way his stomach was still sinking every time he looked at Mydei.

If that man died tonight, where.. What would Phainon have left in this world? The few remnants of Aedes Elysiae were something he couldn’t even try to protect - if anything, they feared him more than anyone else ever would. 

Yet Mydei was the one person that understood his situation and still allowed him to be friends with him. Without Mydei he.. Wasn’t sure what to do. 

“It’s alright to fear death,” Mydei reasoned, but that only made Phainon’s stomach churn even more - making his insides twist so uncomfortably to be having this chat with the man he wanted to safeguard the most, “Even if you understand you’re already dead, if you like your current undead life, it’s natural to want your days to continue.”

.. Phainon wanted to live on, that was true. 

He wanted to explore the world with Mydei and see the sights that the prince had teased him about never seeing. He wanted to learn more about magic now that he had seen the depths it went, and he wanted to.. He wanted to stay by Mydei’s side while doing all of that, as well. Was that such a truly greedy thing? That for once in Phainon’s life of being a knight, he wanted to keep someone close and treasure them so dearly as his own?

“All I can tell you is that you will live on,” Mydei confirmed, as if Phainon actually needed that to be assured to him - reassuring him that even if Mydei died, Phainon would.. Still be here, without him. 

Without anyone he loved once more, alone with no one this time to reach a hand out towards him just like they had twice now in his life. There.. Was no third try, not in this life. 

“I don’t fear death, I’ve been a knight all my life; I just..” Phainon trailed off with a shaky breath, his eyes ducking down to his feet walking on that old dusty path as he grit his teeth together. Every step felt like it weighed as much as possible, and a piece of him almost wanted to beg Mydei to stay home.

To not come tonight, to remain safe where no one could harm him - even though Phainon knew that was impossible.

Mydei enjoyed battle, just like all Kremnoans were rumored to, and to ask him to do such a thing would surely be seen as insulting him.. 

“Mm,” Mydei hummed in a soft and rather quiet tone before he chuckled in his honey-rich octave voice,  “No reason to let your mind wander when we’re marching to fight.”

“.. Right,” Phainon nodded a little, all before sighing because he truly couldn’t help himself - not when his fears were not towards himself, but instead were in regards to that beautiful blond man who was leading the march so confidently.

His feet moved so steadily that Phainon found himself almost jealous as he tried to calm his own nerves, only.. It only got worse and worse the longer he looked at Mydei. The more time he spent thinking of how desperately he wanted to see that man again, and how terrifying the idea of him dying truly was.

To have Mydei vanish from his life, just like everyone else..

“Mydei..” Phainon whined out, aware of painfully woeful his voice sounded even to his own ears - so bad that Mydei almost stumbled a tiny bit before throwing a blank looking stare at Phainon.

“What is it?”

Phainon knew he was being painfully selfish, he knew that this man would never agree to his request. He knew that he was.. Probably a lovesick fool, and yet.. He couldn’t help himself as he clenched his hands into fists to try to calm his own nerves.

“Don’t.. Get harmed during this, alright? Use me as a shield if you must,” Phainon found himself ready to plead if he had to, biting onto his lip a little as he watched Mydei smirk a little of that. Amused, almost, by the request Phainon was trying to make towards him. 

“Denying a Kremnoan their chance to die a death of glory on the battlefield?”  Mydei asked with a laugh, a teasing one more than mocking, but a laugh nonetheless as he looked back towards the road, “I should sk-”

“I don’t want to watch you die, Mydeimos,” Phainon confessed, cutting through Mydei’s words with a knife as he said his own piece with practically a snarl. Unable to help himself as that prince seemed to be taking it much too light-heartedly.

He knew.. Of Kremnoan traditions and how much they valued combat, and yet he just couldn’t allow Mydei to be so at peace with the idea of dying. A piece of him was happy that Mydei didn’t fear it, but Phainon also feared him dying enough for the both of them. Phainon just wanted to have Mydei come back to tomorrow and every single day after that, that’s all. 

“.. I have no intentions of dying today, Phainon,” Mydei mumbled without even looking away from the road - instead seeming a bit more focused after being snapped at a little. 

Though, it wasn’t as if Phainon doubted Mydei was ever not focused considering the army behind them but.. Maybe he was a bit more aware of the fact Phainon was terrified for his safety now.. At least, Phainon was praying that much. 

Phainon had to press out a heavy exhale over that, shaking his head as he joined Mydei on looking towards the empty road, “That’s.. That makes me feel better, thank you.”

“Hmph,” And the conversation died there. 

That was fine - Phainon didn’t mind, not really. He was sated by Mydei just being beside him and walking with him, even if every step they took together could be their last - he found himself comfortable in that silence. As long as it was Mydei by his side, he felt a bit more confident, as if his soul was at peace around that man more than he could ever comprehend. 

Even as they neared that familiar kingdom, the arching walls and broken down gateway, he had to merely remind himself he wasn’t alone. That even with the view of everything he had known and loved coming closer, there was still someone he could do his best to save as he let out a shuddering little sigh. 

He had not even bothered to wear his enchanted cowl today - there was truly no point in it when the kingdom would most likely never hear from Mydei again from what Mydei had offhandedly mumbled sometimes. And if Mydei was leaving.. Phainon would undoubtedly follow him, even if a piece of him would miss it - he had already come to terms with it all.

His future wasn’t with his ruined home or the villagers who had been speaking of moving to Okhema, his future was with that man who was now leading him into that city without a second word. Fiery golden eyes fully transfixed on that castle before him - as if he had steeled his mind for this day arriving. 

“It’s so quiet in the kingdom now..” Phainon noted into that silence however, feeling a bit trapped in his mind as he fully had to come to terms with how dead the city was now. A ghost town of sorts, few people still living here - and even then, Mydei and Phainon had aided most of the remaining ones to leave. 

That was.. Nothing Phainon had ever thought he would have to help with, and yet.. He spent hours with Mydei moving boxes for some of them into a traveler’s caravan - an action the villagers had to be talked into due to their king threatening to gut them alive, but they.. Listened to Mydei and respected him. 

“Necromancy is a plague in this world that must be weeded out,” Mydei told him in a huffed out voice, sounding almost irritated as Phainon dragged his eyes across the once polished marble linings of buildings to look at that man who did, in fact, look annoyed. 

“Uh,” Phainon started, doing his best to ignore the instant little look Mydei gave to him with that simple word, “I appreciate the attempt at a pep talk, or whatever that was, but you’re surrounded by the undead..”

Phainon was smiling as he spoke, a genuine attempt at some sort of joke that only seemed to make Mydei pull his own lips into a tightened frown. 

“.. I never implied I was not a part of the problem,” Mydei grumbled in a voice that was less than ideal,  “Doing this to the dead is unnatural, and one day I will pay for my crimes.”

.. Pay for his crimes.

Those words were enough to make Phainon feel a shiver run down his spine - a shiver that threatened to coil around his neck and choke him. He had no idea what ‘paying’ for his crime of necromancer meant, but whatever it was; Phainon was quite sure he had no desire to let Mydei pay such a price alone. 

Phainon had to sigh over it, “.. Can you not talk like that after just speaking about how you would not die today?” 

“Both can be true at the same time,” Mydei told him as he flicked his eyes to look at Phainon a bit idly while walking, “I’ll not allow another necromancer or worse claim my life, for I still have retribution to pay.”

.. That really didn’t make Phainon feel any better, and he still had to sigh regardless. 

“.. Sometimes you speak more like your old prince self,” Phainon noted before dragging his eyes up to the sky - blinking a little over how a few stars were becoming visible now before looking back at Mydei with a soft little smile, “It’s nice, in a way.”

That seemed to do quite a bit of work on Mydei, making his pause just the slightest bit before blinking wide eyes of those words; “Nice?”

“To know that throughout all of this happening, you’re still you,” Phainon told him without missing a beat, unable to keep his grin back as that prince seemed to search his expression endlessly. Golden eyes flickering around in a daze before Mydei made a rather quiet tutting noise and looking back towards their destination. 

“.. I see. I guess.. In a way I do understand what you’re inferring.” Mydei mumbled quietly - much too quietly to where Phainon had to assume the prince was taking a moment to be contemplative. 

That was enough for Phainon to glance back at the horde of zombies following behind him - a thing that should make him feel nervous and yet.. It was only truly eerie due to how quiet they were as well. Sure, their steps following behind had made quite a lot of noise when combined with how many there were but.. 

.. Phainon had to tilt his head a little, feeling confused as his eyes didn’t find that familiar abomination in the sea following them into the city.

Had Mydei given it.. Some other kind of command? 

“Mydei? Where are you going, the entrance is back this way?” Phainon called out, unable to help himself - watching the way Mydei froze over that. Pausing completely as if he had been caught and was going to be scolded by his parents. 

Mydei seemed to exhale quietly over it - looking at Phainon almost innocently, “.. Nothing always goes according to plan, Phainon. I’ll be heading through the front door to distract Kephale.”

Phainon was powerless to stop the small laugh that left his own lips - shaking his head over that, “I told you, I refuse. If you’re changing routes, then I am as well.”

“You are a fool. We have one shot at this, and you wish to waste it by being overprotective of a necromancer you barely know.” Mydei snapped back instantly, making Phainon blink a little over that.

Barely know..? If that was true, then Phainon found himself wanting to spend the rest of his life getting to know Mydei intimately, was that so wrong?

“Making sure you leave here with your life is not a waste, and it never will be, Mydeimos,” Phainon explained with a little sigh, shaking his head over the way Mydei seemed to be trying to get them to part.

As if that was possible for Phainon to ever do again. 

“It’s a waste if we do not actually win today,” Mydei sighed out as a counter. 

Phainon clicked his tongue right back at Mydei, “I’ll not leave your side, Mydei, no matter what you say.”

Mydei studied him for just a brief moment before shaking his head over it - giving up it seemed, “Have it your way, but try your best to remain calm, alright?”

Phainon nodded over that, blinking his eyes a little to idly look at the shambling mess of creatures seemingly waiting for their directions to be given. Though, they all were focused on Mydei, more than anything. Hollow sunken eyes that seemed to glow in the moonlight, all staring at Mydei to where even Phainon found this to be eerie. 

.. But it’s not like Phainon was any different as he turned his head away from them to nod curtly at Mydei once more, aware of the way Mydei had been studying him incredulously and waiting for him to truly mean it.

“I will remain level headed, Mydeimos,” Phainon reassured him, doing his best to mean those words from the very depths of his soul as he spoke them. 

“Good boy,”  Mydei hummed and turned away from him - and something about it felt.. So bizarre to Phainon, as if Mydei had folded much too quickly on this topic but. He was glad at the same time, so what could he do besides follow after Mydei and ignore wherever his zombies were going. 

For some reason, he couldn’t help but throw a glance at them idly though - a look over his shoulder to blink at where they were heading off to before following his prince. Staring at the solid black clothing Mydei was wearing and how deeply he hated it - that man always kept those golden gauntlets on his hands, but never anymore armor. 

It drove Phainon insane, really, to think this man was walking into battle and was practically defenseless.. Phainon was the same, sure, but at least if he got stabbed he wouldn’t even feel it.

“Mydei,” Phainon called out, feeling his hands moving to clench and fold against each other - wringing a little as he continued to follow Mydei. 

“What is it?” That necromancer asked rather boredly back, as if he wasn’t expecting much to be asked or said - not in the few final moments before the storm would begin.

Before the battle that Phainon so desperately did not want to be Mydei’s final one.. 

“Promise me you’ll prioritize yourself first and foremost,” Phainon found himself choking a little as golden eyes flicked to him - not looking amused in the slightest as he seemed to study Phainon and his words silently, “That you.. Even if everything goes wrong, you’ll go on living.”

“.. I cannot promise you that, Phainon,” Mydei spoke before pausing his steps - his head barely turning to look at that large grandeur entrance that seemed to be taunting them both just a few steps upwards,  “I would rather die here knowing I fought m-”

“I know,” Phainon cut in, unable to stop himself as his tongue felt more and more like cotton under those golden eyes that were trying to parse him, “I know you cannot live with the guilt of him going on living if you fail, I know..”

Phainon understood all of it - he knew that he was asking Mydei for something that man couldn’t promise, he was being selfish and asking Mydei to sacrifice something that meant way too much to Mydei. A piece of himself and all he had left of Kremnos, and yet.. Phainon wanted him to refuse it - to live another day at all costs. 

“You can’t live through watching another kingdom perish,” Phainon supplied, watching the way Mydei’s eyes flickered just a little bit - enough to dip away from Phainon and focus on something else, anything else,  “I know..”

Phainon found himself hanging his head a little over that - trying his best to get a grip on his mind as he let out a little sigh over his thoughts. He didn’t want Mydei to give up these things, not really, not when he understood Kremnoan traditions and how deeply they meant to the once-crown prince, but he.. Also couldn’t help the yearning he felt from the depths of his soul. 

The unbridled desire to make Mydei live to see another dawn no matter his own sacrifice he had to give to make sure that came true.. 

“I just.. Wanted to try to be greedy, just this once,” Phainon confessed as he forced his eyes to rise from Mydei’s feet - feeling how much his skin was burning in the moonlit night as that man only egregiously watched his every move. So keenly studying him, all before huffing a little sigh - his eyes moving to look at that door again idly. 

“Forgive me..” Phainon was genuinely asking for forgiveness, more than a little aware of what he was asking from Mydei as he looked at that dazzling man. Swallowing a little as Mydei moved his gaze back to focusing on Phainon languidly. 

“.. You’re forgiven,” Mydei told him in a tired sounding tone, “But if I do somehow perish here today.. Know that I was at the least happy to be fighting by your side.”

That wasn’t enough, it could never be enough, and yet - Phainon had to accept it as enough for now; forcing himself give a somber smile on his lips over those words. 

“.. Mydei, you’ll make me cry before we go in there!” Phainon chirped out as well - moving already to bump into Mydei’s shoulder a little with his own. Pleased to hear a huff of laughter from that prince in return over it. 

“Do not be so foolish,” Mydei hummed out over that, “Ready yourself, Phainon.”

Those words were said in a warning as Mydei once again began to rise up those steps to that door with Phainon in heel, making Phainon swallow harshly. 

This would.. Assuredly not be the most simple of tasks, Phainon knew that much. But he did find himself wishing he knew what Mydei was thinking and was planning out, or why they were entering through the front..

Whatever the case; Phainon tried to stop the way his hands were unsteady and were trembling so horribly, the way his mind was still stalling again and again in his worries for Mydei more than anything. This was a battle to make sure no other kingdoms suffered, to make sure no one else died to this lich, and that included Mydei, as well. 

Yet, he followed Mydei again and again - and this was no different as his eyes watched Mydeimos move to place a hand on that great door. Pushing it open with relative ease just for Phainon’s stomach to sink so painfully. 

The amount of dead lining the halls along with the way no lanterns were lit outside of a two eerie large green ones beside the throne. Sitting on top those rows of stairs in that great hall that lead right to where they were wanting - right to that false king who was undoubtedly watching every single step they took into that hall.

And every footfall made an echo in the empty and silent world, a horrible sound that made Phainon’s eyes move to those guards who he assumed were undead. Unmoving, just as they always had been, unwavering as two people neared their king in silence.. 

It was enough to make Phainon’s skin crawl from that alone. 

“Oh how bold you both finally are..” That familiar voice began in a tone that made Phainon’s feet stall the slightest bit - a voice he had known and trusted for so long. Only now it was being used in flat mockery, a laugh between his words as Phainon moved to follow Mydei through that throne room he knew so well, “So brave to walk these halls all while seeking to take my life.”

Phainon eyes leisurely took in the sight of that throne room.. It wasn’t.. The sight of marvel he once knew, the home and pride of the land he lived in and worked at. No longer were the insides of it polished and well taken care of, now.. Even that rug had vanished to leave their steps hollow and echoing every inch they neared. The walls were decaying, cracked and aging on the inside as if no life had been here in months.

.. Probably because they hadn’t, that much was obvious as Phainon’s eyes moved back once more to those guards who had watched him die - still haunting, unphased… Undead, probably.. More worryingly, their numbers seemed to have grown from what Phainon ever quite recalled. No longer were there merely the loyal guardsman that protected the king.. Now it looked as if there was.. An army here?

.. Had he somehow expected them both to be coming here today, or had he merely become more prepared for a war of sorts? Was he getting bored and instead was preparing for the next kingdom he was planning to ruin?

Those thoughts made Phainon’s stomach churn painfully uncomfortably.

“Tell me, Kremnoan, what do you hope to achieve with such puny skill in necromancy?” That false idol sitting atop his throne only spoke again - making Phainon finally look up those sets of stairs and at the man he once had served, body, heart, and soul.  

A man who had been long gone.

“Is the trophy you stole from my shelves enough to make up for our disparity?”

Phainon found himself pausing at that; staring at the rotten corpse of a man who had once glowed so brilliantly - a source of pride and happiness in their kingdom. 

Now he only looked as if he were nothing more than a decaying corpse, bones jutting out of his skin that seemed as thin as possible, eyes sunken in and glowing in such an eerie inhuman way that Phainon found himself uncomfortable even trying to look him in the eyes. He looked sick - unwell and frail with his bones jutting out, not even his clothes seemed to hug him correctly anymore.

If Phainon wasn’t already privy to the fact that was just a walking corpse, he may have thought he was just direly sick. Yet, instead, Phainon had to swallow over the sight - idly allowing his thoughts to wonder if he, too, would rot like Kephale’s body was, eventually?

Though, while Phainon was busy pondering his own mortality, Mydei spoke from his side in a chuffed sounding tone; “.. Trophy?”

“My knight, of course,” That easily said and sighed out word was enough to make Phainon’s blood freeze in his veins - even if he had none, “Those who go through such anguish and betrayal before they die always make the best puppets, don’t you agree?”

Phainon couldn’t help the way he was remaining standing there with his hands wrapped around the sword Mydei had given to him. A blade to replace his own that the man on that throne mockingly laughing at him now had stolen away from him - and even had the gall to have it resting beside his seat. 

His pose was lazy and lax, one that didn’t fit the man Phainon once knew. 

“After all, he’s merely been your puppet all this time, hasn’t he? Forced to obey and listen to you, perhaps even tricked into caring about you?” Kephale asked, and that was enough to make Phainon scoff over that himself.

That simply wasn’t true, not when Phainon had been given so many chances to leave - not including the way Mydei himself would leave Phainon for hours at a time.. That simply wasn’t possible, and yet, for some reason - it made Phainon’s mind itch a tiny bit. Just enough to make him clench his hands into fists tighter around his sword as he attempted to steady his mind. 

“Humorous, really, if only he could remember his true feelings for you; the fights you both used to partake in..” Kephale only continued, clicking his tongue a little as if he actually felt some sense of pity towards Phainon, “But you won’t let him, will you?”

Phainon had to laugh over that - one that was cold and disjointed even in his own throat as it left him. This truly.. Was not his Kephale, the man he knew and adored would never assume such cruel things about someone or try to frame them. The man he knew would have never had killed him, either.. But to speak so foul about a man Phainon cherished.. Kephale would have never had done that to him. 

“Speaking for me is more than a little foolish,” Phainon hissed out as his bark of laughter failed to continue, shrugging his shoulder a little as he stared at the way that false king still seemed so amused by it,  “But arguing with a lich is even more idiotic.”

“Are you really so much more confident in a man you barely know, versus the king who has housed you from the day your home was lost?”

That was enough to make Phainon feel his own jaw tighten uncomfortably, his tongue feeling too fat for his own mouth as he chewed and swallowed those words down. 

“You speak of a man who is not you,” Phainon growled out, feeling himself bristling over that man was trying to abuse his  relationship for his own gain - a relationship that was not anyone’s to touch anymore. 

Only, that king looked a little bit wounded by that - frowning heavily before sighing, “.. Do you truly have no more love for the man who cared for you for so long, that you would dare draw your blade before him?”

“I draw my blade to defend those who I love,” Phainon explained in a level tone, doing his utmost to try to stay calm when this monster was making a mockery of his affection for Kephale, “And that is certainly not a man who calls me his ‘trophy’.”

“Ignoring the ignorant fool who does not know what he says to his dearest father,” Kephale clicked his tongue over that - tutting a little all while Phainon felt his face burn over how that voice sounded so much like the man who was his ‘father’. Yet with a gruffer layer beneath it, full of anger and rage - traits Kephale himself never used to show before.

Though, that false king only continued onwards with his eyes moving from Phainon now, “You must be the necromancer named Mydeimos.. A Kremnoan, and the one who has been blamed for Castrum Kremnos’s fall.”

Mydei didn’t reply to that, but that didn’t seem to phase Kephale as he only prattled onwards with, or without Mydei.

“I became quite curious about you once my knight mentioned you as he laid bleeding on the floor; imagine my surprise to learn one of their royal bloods had escaped their judgement day..” Kephale laughed a little between his words, as if the idea of one royalty of Kremnos living was amusing to him, “All for himself to become a necromancer.. I suppose your mother truly was the only person in that kingdom that wasn’t a complete buffoon?”

Mydei still didn’t respond to that - instead he seemed to cock his head to the side with those words. 

“Not going to reply to me? I thought a prince would know his manners when speaking to someone above him?” Kephale’s mockery only continued, making Phainon fight the urge to speak on Mydei’s behalf but something.. Told him not to. To stay quiet and listen to whatever this man was choosing to spend his time bringing up.

Not because the words were important, but because there had to be a reason why Mydei was silent through it all. 

“Though, I must say..” Kephale trailed off, shaking his head as he lazily sat on his throne, “It’s quite obvious how stressed you are.. You must be doing your absolute best to make sure your hold over my knight still stands, hm?”

.. Hold? As in the thing on Phainon’s neck that Mydei had explained so long ago?

“He seems like such a burden.. Are you sure you wouldn’t merely prefer to hand him back to me? No need for a fight between us here, after all, we’re both just..” Kephale chuckled darkly over that, “Comrades, aren’t we?”

That was enough to make Phainon echo out that word confusedly,  “.. Comrades?” 

“Aw.. My poor little knight, do you know nothing? Has that necromancer by your side taught you not a thing about himself?” Kephale spoke in such a soft voice, as if he was truly pitying Phainon this time around. 

A lie, truly, but the lies didn’t seem to stop there; “From whom else do  you think he learned necromancy, if not from me?”

Those words were enough to make Phainon feel dazed over that - staring at that king as he realized he.. Didn’t actually know where Mydei had first learned necromancy? He doubted it was from this man who had killed his family, but.. It was a bit odd to think about..

That seemed to be enough however, making Mydei scoff loudly - a broken laugh fluttering out of his throat as he moved to cross his arms over his chest, “What an odd game you’re playing here, lich; have you not toyed with him enough when he was still living?”

Phainon couldn’t help but to be a little nosy over it as he looked at Mydei curiously, “Was it.. Really from him?”

“What? No,” Mydei huffed with a little roll of his eyes - as if he couldn’t understand why Phainon would even ask this. And well.

Phainon had to say it was not due to the fact he was believing the words of this skinwalker - he really was just kind of.. Wondering about it?

There were so many questions he wanted he still wanted to ask Mydei - to get to know Mydei and now.. He felt nervous, antsy, even as he stood there and looked at the man to his side. A man who could lose his life today; and Phainon would be left with the mess of what ifs and what could have beens. A mess of emotions that were making such a heavy knot in his heart as he tried to keep his thoughts in line, and yet..

“Then who?” Phainon asked earnestly, not at all judging the way Mydei seemed annoyed by this - his eyes flickering from the man named ‘Kephale’ and to Phainon with a heavy sigh. 

All before Mydei made a quiet snorting noise, “.. Castorice.”

“Castorice? From Styxia?” Phainon echoed out with a confused jerk of his head back a little - that would explain why he knew Styxia so well, and the odd words he had said about the magic in the air there. But for some reason he never could have considered they would have actually have had been.. Close?

Something about it made Phainon’s stomach churn and twist a little uncomfortably, as if his skin were itching as he thought about how that made sense.. Mydei was a prince, and Castorice was a princess.. They could have been more than just friends, huh?

.. Phainon didn’t much like that idea as he bit into his tongue a little, trying his best to conjure up what to say over that, but it didn’t matter. Not as the man on  that throne coldly laughed over their conversation as well - making Phainon jerk his head up to look at that man. 

“Fascinating information for myself to learn.. It appears I should visit her once this matter is handled,” Kephale chimed in, sounding so painfully amused that Phainon couldn’t help but tilt his head over that.

A threat; it was a threat towards Mydei’s friend, or lover, a thing that seemed to have easily made Mydei’s grip on his sword tighten. The metal of his gloves creaked just enough to make Phainon look at him a bit bewildered, doing his best to understand that rage that was seeping through Mydei so obviously. 

“Like hell..” Mydei hissed, all before he seemed to relax a little once more - a deep breath leaving his chest before he grew a rather.. Coy smile, one that Phainon had to blink at as he tried to understand what was happening here today,  “Be upfront with me, Kephale.”

“Hmm?”

That hum was purely out of amusement, obviously willing to indulge Mydei and their conversation solely because it was a little show for him, wasn’t it? Just like Phainon serving him while he killed their kingdom, making him  truly believe Mydei was at fault, all while mocking him.. 

.. Was Mydei trying to abuse that oddly human emotion of wanting a good show, for some odd reason? Phainon really couldn’t say, all he could say was the way his body froze as Mydei tilted his head and spoke an innocent question. 

“This knight, and your trophy; He’s a bit more than that, isn’t he?”

.. More than that?

Phainon’s mind raced to try to figure out what that meant, to figure out what Mydei was implying now as he furrowed his brows at that blond man. Though, Mydei seemed to be making it a point to not look at Phainon - to ignore him in favor of staring daggers into the man who was still looking down upon them both. 

And Phainon.. He didn’t dare look at that man who had called him a trophy, he didn’t dare glance to see what kind of expression he was wearing over being asked this question. To be weighed his measure once more by the skinwalker lich just a few mere feet away. 

“Hmm.” 

That hum was a bit different this time around - sounding somewhat more perturbed over being asked such a thing. A question that didn’t make much sense in Phainon’s mind when he thought it over, but it still seemed to bother Kephale to be asked it.

.. Because it was a loaded question, correct? Mydei already knew the answer, and that was why he was asking - an odd little mindgames attempt, and more importantly, a waste of time..?

Phainon really didn’t understand what was happening here as he slowly looked Mydei up and down, inspecting him slowly to try to get a grip on the situation. 

“It’s been quite interesting to note his body - it doesn’t seem to rot like your current one,” Mydei noted as his own eyes flitted to Phainon’s, all before moving to cross his arms over his chest, “Your desired vessel, correct?”

.. Vessel?

Those words were enough to make his stomach drop over the way Mydei was staring at him now - devoid of the warmth and joy that those eyes usually had buried within them. Now fully looking at if he were inspecting a craft, a blade, a weapon - and those emotions were aimed at him so cruelly. 

Phainon wasn’t even sure what to do with his hands, feeling them twitch at his side as he debated rubbing at his chest - at that scar that was from his own blade piercing him all the way through. Everything about this situation was making his mind jerk and struggle to keep up, though..

As he dragged his eyes up to meet Mydei’s again from the floor - they seemed to have softened once more, looking honey sweet and just as brilliant, dazzling in their own way as if he were trying to calm Phainon’s fraying mind. And really, Phainon felt like he should be more embarrassed over how easily that did work on him.

At how genuinely he wanted to find comfort in Mydei’s expression, and how easily he found himself being a little bit soothed by Mydei giving him an ounce of pity in this situation. 

“Perhaps, his soul is a bit unruly for my own tastes; a vast difference from what I desired from him, and expected with how easy he was to warp while living,”  Kephale sighed out as if the topic was just a little boring to him - as if he had thought about this so many times before but Phainon.. 

Phainon found his mind struggling to adapt to it all, the idea of his own soul being called ‘unruly’ while he was being messed with so much while he was alive. Betrayed and mocked, all to be a tool for this monster who had stolen the body of someone he adored to make Phainon’s walls be down so easily. 

“.. I’m no doll for you to toy with,” Phainon found his voice saying without a second thought - jerking his head a little to glare at that man who seemed to be leisurely standing finally. As if he himself was getting bored of their conversation and was ready to end this farce - but Phainon found himself flicking his gaze back to Mydei.

“That’s true,” Kephale sighed with a shake of his head, “I’ve learned souls like yours are quite the struggle to break, even while making you slaughter your own kingdom’s people you refused me so ruthlessly time and time again..”

Kephale sounded almost annoyed as he spoke those words - making Phainon crease his brows and try to steel himself for whatever nonsense this man was about to spout and direct towards him. 

“Never slaughtering enough, always forcing your body to return home after only killing one or less for the day.. It became quite the annoyance,” Kephale mused, as if he was merely talking about sending Phainon out to garden or pick up supplies - not slaughter people in the streets,  “Only for that necromancer to make it worse, while also making himself into such an easy key.”

Phainon did not enjoy the way 'key' was spoken as if it was the most interesting idea and thing in the world to Kephale - as if he was endlessly amused by whatever Mydei had done to Phainon. 

“A soul only has value if they still cling to something in this world,” Kephale rambled onwards, “At first, you were clinging to try to save your people, and now.. You seem rather fond of that man.”

.. His soul was clinging to Mydei? Well, that wasn’t that odd, really. He did find himself clinging to Mydei in general even if he tried not to show it.. 

Kephale only hummed, “Love is a curious thing for humans, isn’t it?”

Love.

That word was enough to make Phainon’s body feel stiff - that was the emotion he felt for Mydei so deeply yet had never come to terms with it quite yet. A biting feeling of how much he meant to Phainon, all while Phainon found himself shying away from saying such a  thing - only for this monster to so easily be able to tell his feelings for him.

“I must say, this is a rather interesting tactic,” Kephale commented with his voice thick with amusement over his own thoughts now, “Do you think you can win in a battle of tenacity, little necromancer in training?”

Kephale only sighed so dramatically - so loudly that it made Phainon feel a prickle of annoyance as he looked at that king who was slumping over more now with his head propper up on his hand, “I cannot help but notice your assault on the back entrance of the castle.. A curious approach, if I were you, I would have forced that knight away and searching as well..”

“Instead you’ve blindly sent the undead through these halls looking for who knows what..” Kephale trailed off, shaking his head a little, “Do you truly believe in him that much?”

That was a question that Phainon felt his own mind blank over the idea of Mydei trusting in him so much, and yet there was an odd blur of gold to his side.. 

“Mydei!?” Phainon choked out as Mydei didn’t even answer, instead he had moved to pull out his sword - all to begin lunging towards some of the undead lining the room, “Mydei! Wait, we need a plan!”

Mydei’s actions however made the swarm of undead begin to move just the same, wrapping around them and beginning their fight as Phainon found his mind still racing alongside his hands tightening on his own blade, “Mydeimos?!”

“No plan needed, we kill him and move on,” Mydei growled in a tone that felt so foreign to Phainon’s ears, one almost made him think that Mydei was pressing himself to stay calm. Or something else?

Either way, Phainon couldn’t help but twitch his head to the side, blinking at the way Mydei looked so prepared for battle now. A frown so thinly on his lips as he appeared more than a little ready to snarl, and Phainon..

“But the-” Phainon didn’t even finish his words as Mydei instead began to move at a speed Phainon had only rarely seen months ago during their own fights - a blazing quickness from a man who seemed to be deadset on something now,  “Don’t just charge in!”

Those words didn’t truly matter, not as the clinking of metal coming to life was blaring against Phainon’s ears - enough to make him twist and grit his teeth over the way those undead guards seemed to be coming to life. 

Movements of them slowly descending on the duo as if to defend their king who had leisurely sat back down onto his throne to watch them - and Phainon.. Phainon couldn’t understand how many zombies there were, yet they seemed almost.. Sluggish and slow. Ancient in their movements against Phainon - and that was more odd than anything. 

Something about all of this felt so painfully off as Phainon moved again to hold his own against one of those undead guards who were now moving about the throne room - allowing more and more to funnel into that once gorgeous and stunning room. But Phainon’s mind could only continuously return to the fact that Mydei.. Was not acting like himself.

Sure, Phainon had learned a lot about Mydei’s fighting style and how wild he could get as he lost himself in combat; but this was different.

Reckless, in a way that almost felt too..

.. On purpose. 

Calculated in a way that had Phainon confused on if he should actually be worried, or if this was somehow going according to play for Mydei. Whatever the case, Phainon had to move to parry every single blow - all while his eyes kept moving back to Mydei to make sure he was just as fine. 

Every movement of Mydei's was precise, as if he was attacking with intentions to slay the undead before him - but not aiming for the man on the throne. Not yet, at least. 

“Heavy handed with your blows, maybe you should have tried to lean more into necromancy before this..” Kephale spoke on top of his throne, making Phainon click his tongue a little in annoyance over that - of course the man who wasn’t actively fighting at all was having a lot to say to Mydeimos of all people right now. 

“.. Some people prefer to be heavy handed in their swings,” Mydei growled back, though, Phainon found himself sliding his sword to slash through another corpse before chancing a glance at that man. His ears keening to listen to the way he was panting now with the thrill of battle in his veins, but..

For once, there was no smile on his lips in combat - no fond little expression like he always had while fighting and sparring with Phainon, this.. This was something more determined as he moved to fight off yet another undead. Something Phainon had to copy as he attempted to get his mind out of the clouds - a bit more dazed with how it felt almost eerie.

As if those undead were.. Going easy on him for some reason, languid in their movements while swarming Phainon, almost making him feel his mind reeling over why that could be.

Obstacles to block him from Mydei, to split them up, was the most obvious one. And Phainon’s mind honestly failed to think of another reason as he felt horror creeping into him over that - not wasting a single moment before turning on heel to where Mydei himself was still clashing with the undead in his own little area.

It wasn’t as if it mattered if Phainon was stabbed in the back trying to get to him, he would be fine, Mydei.. Mydei on the other hand.. 

“Amusing,” That now painfully grating voice hummed into Phainon’s ears as he moved to easily bash away yet another unfortunate knight - his heart dropping a little to idly wonder if these were people he had worked with for years.. But there was nothing to be done for them now. If anything, he had to figure he was freeing them from this torment.

Either way, Kephale only remained watching and speaking, “Are you one of those people, or are you coming up with excuses like your father?”

Phainon felt himself tutting over that, not caring for those words as he continued on his creed to get closer to Mydei - the talks of a father with the person who stole Kephale’s body.. Humorous, really, though..

“My..” Mydei sounded a bit distracted, and that in itself was worrying to Phainon’s ears as he moved to continue swiping annoying bodies from his path - his mind only stalling to notice most lacked weapons. For what?

“Father?” Mydei echoed out a bit slowly, and Phainon couldn’t let himself dwell on that, not right now. Not when he was still a few feet away from Mydei, still a few bodies away that he had to hit to the side and prayed they didn’t rise again to grab at him. 

“Stay focused now! What if you were to die? I’m sure that little knight beside you would be rather distraught!”

Phainon could feel his face burn over the mockery - but it didn’t matter. Not in comparison to Mydei being alone or worse those words coming true, Phainon’s eyes were only bent on getting to Mydei now, determined to see that Mydei saw the next day before anything else.
