Nothing else mattered, not right now when the horde of the dead seemed endless..

“Mydei!” Phainon cried out as he finally seemed to break through them - blinking as golden eyes lashed to him quickly in between his own fight, all before returning to focus on the assaulter before him, “What is your plan here?”

He had to ask that, his mind was so baffled over what was happening that he just wanted a single clear answer.

Only, Mydei laughed a little quietly at that between a loud clashing of metal as he parried yet another dead soul with a sword - making Phainon blink over how better armed they were here. As if this area was more.. Intent on Mydei’s death rather than Phainon’s. That was a bizarre thought as much as it was terrifying.. 

“.. A battle of tenacity, didn’t you hear him before?” Mydei answered after a moment, never letting up in his battle and Phainon couldn’t help but choke a little over that. 

“You can’t.. Be serious?” Phainon found himself moving to aid Mydei, now keeping as close as he could to that prince due to him being unable to run once more to try to get closer to Kephale.

At least, it didn’t seem like that was the plan anymore for Mydei as he instead seemed more intent on wildly killing the undead one after another. As if he didn’t even care that those bodies seemed to shamble back together - picking themselves up and rising once more even as the duo continued to weed their numbers down. It could never be enough.

.. Surely Mydei didn’t seriously mean that they would be here fighting for days.. Phainon could manage it, he didn’t need to rest - but Mydei.. He would eventually need to rest, and Phainon certainly wouldn’t allow him to die here.

Even if it was dishonorable, even if Mydeimos hated him for the rest of time, he would pick that man up and carry him away even if Mydei was doing his best to stop him.

“Deadly,” Mydei supplied, and that was the worst news of Phainon’s life as he felt his stomach gaining a new empty pit in it - one that made him swallow harshly as he moved to slay yet another undead approaching them, “Have you not noticed it yourself?”

“Noticed..?” Phainon echoed out confusedly over Mydei’s question - unable to even think of what he was supposed to be noticing. His eyes only roamed the tiniest of bits, doing his best to figure out what on earth was needing to be focused as his eyes struggled with it.

It was hard to ‘notice’ anything outside of the undead he was hacking and slashing his way through - feeling the way sinew and rotting flesh caved beneath his borrowed blade but.. Noticing nothing in particular. 

“The way he moves,” Mydei replied easily, making Phainon blink his eyes a little - trying his best to comprehend what he meant by that before his eyes crept up to Kephale himself. His eyes lingering with how that man.. Wasn’t moving much in general, in fact - he looked archaic. As if his bones would crumble at the slightest of movements as he sat there.

Watching. 

“That’s..” Phainon trailed off, unsure of what to even make of that sight as he slowly tried to understand the idea that this really was a battle of stamina. 

Between the lone living man, and the undead now.. It was a game of who would fold and fail the fastest?

Insane, that was an idea conjured by the utterly insane - but Phainon couldn’t find himself blaming Mydei for that. Not when he knew Mydei had to have been always a little bit.. Quirky to become a necromancer in the first place.

“Are you attempting to imply you knew, and yet, you let that knight of yours follow you into here regardless?” Kephale asked, all before chuckling over that - a sound that made Phainon feel his lips crease in annoyance, “Are you overconfident, or a fool?”

That wasn’t Kephale’s laugh - that one was hollow and forced, stolen and made a mockery of to tarnish the name of him even further. And Phainon could only stay by Mydei’s side and cast idle glares to Kephale between his fighting - thankful, for once, that he was already dead and did not need the rest.

Though, that only made him worry more and more for Mydei as he moved to slay undead after undead, unsure of when the end would come with their game of stamina in full swing. 

“.. Who can say until the end?” Mydei hissed out, as if he himself was trying to answer Phainon’s thoughts as he lunged for another zombie - not appearing phased at all as he continued his own precise and practiced movements. 

“A pity,” Kephale sighed out over that rebuttal, “In another lifetime, you may have achieved something more if you had not thrown your life away.”

“This talk is bothersome when Mydei has done nothing wrong,” Phainon cut in with a tired sigh over these arguments, still moving to slash away another monster rising to their feet, “Granted, I feel more baffled than anything else, but I-”

“It’s quite cruel he had not warned you beforehand of what he intends for you to go through,” Kephale cut in, making Phainon’s words halt in his mouth a bit bitterly. Not because he would ever actually believe whatever this man was about to start snarling at him, but because he was so rude.

Rude and interrupting Phainon while possessing Kephale’s corpse, it was truly starting to piss Phainon off so much as he moved his blade to gash down another being. Wincing a little as he stared at the familiar armor all the knights wore and matched together - his own co-workers who..

.. He had to think this was freeing them in some way, blinking away his thoughts away instead of allowing himself to finish them with a heavy heart and a heavier sword to still swing. 

“I would explain, but you may only believe his words.. Love is a cruel and confusing thing in itself,” That man only continued to sigh out, wholly unaware that Phainon was bent on borderline ignoring him at this point.

“Go ahead and explain for me, Mydei,” Kephale sighed out once more, making Phainon click his tongue over that offense. Feeling his ears burn over that voice saying Mydei’s name like that, a voice he would have once loved to hear greet the man he had grown to love; distorted into such a horrid mockery.. 

“Don’t.. Call him Mydei, you do not know him,” Phainon found himself growling out, doing his best to keep himself sane as he moved his eyes to look at that demonic being.

One that was much too far gone, really.

“Allowing us to talk when the time keeps ticking on your clock? How kind of you,” Mydei grumbled out, seeming a little perturbed over it all - or maybe he was just focused on something else entirely. Phainon didn’t know, and it felt like he didn’t know most things about this fight going on right now..

“I have enough time for my jesters to attempt to entertain their king one last time,” Kephale chuckled out - but it wasn’t as if that horde of shambling undead were stopping either.

Instead, Phainon was straining to pay attention to the conversation happening while slashing away at the corpses moving closer to him. Every single step forward felt as if they could be instantly yanked backwards again with how the dead seemed endless.

A tidal wave of them, bent solely on making sure Mydei left here alive - all while Mydei had only brought Phainon with him.. Surely, his army was working to find the vase, but was that really a good idea? Did Mydei have such faith in his mindless undead that they could shatter it on the backlines while they remained fighting up here?

.. Or were they not as mindless as Phainon was assuming them to be? Were they more intact with their souls than he had ever tried to comprehend? That sounded impossible, and yet his mind only continuously returned to that giant who seemed so.. At peace, oddly. 

“.. Very well,” Mydei began with such a heavy sigh - sounding almost as if he were also panting due to the physical exercise they were currently undergoing, “He’s implying I am foolish for allowing you in this room when he desires a new body to host his soul.”

.. Well, yes, Phainon was pretty sure they had already spoken about this? But well, it’s not like Phainon was going to bring that up when he knew now Mydei needed to buy time somehow - and if talking stalled the lich’s mind a little, Phainon would listen to whatever rambles either of them had to say.

Mainly because he loved to hear Mydei speak, but also for the sake of the matter as well, naturally. 

“The counter is ticking down on that rickety old body, and yours has no counter on it,” Mydei explained, though Phainon really was feeling like this was some type of deja vu, “You’re the perfect vessel, as stated before; the thing he desires most.”

Phainon had to huff a little over that, over the idea of being the ‘thing’ that man desired the most felt like a horror story more than anything.. Why couldn’t it be Mydei wanting that from him instead? This was some odd kind of torture.

“I don’t..” Phainon tried to think of what to say to that - trailing off a little as he was told about being Kephale’s vessel again and again to make his head swim worryingly in his thoughts, “I couldn’t leave you..”

“It’s fine,” Mydei swiftly told him, already seeming to lunge forward to claim another zombie’s undead life as his blade’s own, “I already told you I have no intentions of dying here today.”

“Is.. Is there something I need to do?” Those words left Phainon’s mouth before he even really had a moment to process them - swallowing so roughly as he flicked his eyes to look at Mydeimos in the spare moment he could. 

In between the moments of fighting for Mydei’s life, only to find those golden eyes already on him. As if he was keenly watching Phainon for some reason, and that.. Phainon found himself looking away, not wanting to read into whatever mixed emotions were in that gaze. 

“No,” Mydei huffed after that, as if that was the kind of reaction he wanted from Phainon.

But Phainon found himself powerless to give a scoff over that, echoing that word; “No?”

“You have enough ties keeping your soul in this world, don’t you?”

That question made Phainon look at Mydei blankly, pausing his movements to instead spare a glance to the man who seemed to be asking him such a loaded question that made Phainon feel like he was supposed to easily say yes. To agree and say he wasn’t worried - yet.. He was endlessly worried now.

Being some evil lich’s ‘desired’ and ‘perfect’ vessel with his own necromancer only seemingly speaking in riddles gave him plenty to worry about, actually!

Though.. Phainon had to wonder what counted as a ‘tie’ for his soul, anyway?

“How sweet..” Kephale spoke once more, apparently not fond of the idea of letting Phainon ponder that question for long, “That knight has lost everything, everyone he ever loved, his kingdom slaughtered by his own hands.. And you think the guilt doesn’t eat him alive?”

Phainon opened his mouth to reply to that - to try to snarl over the way it did in fact creep into him and keep his mind racing. The fact that the senseless slaughter had been happening by his own hands, and he couldn’t have even stopped it - that he was so weak to be used as if he were a puppet and nothing more. 

But he said nothing, how could he speak when Mydei spoke first? That would have been impolite of him. 

“The guilt of his own crimes you forced him to commit should be enough to make him stay sane alone,” Mydei growled out as he continued to chop down foe after foe, all while Phainon found himself in a daze as he tried to understand what was going on here, “Let alone anyone else’s presence having a say in it. I believe you underestimate his soul.”

From what Phainon was understanding, this all had something to do with his soul; a thing that Mydei seemed to have full confidence in, all while Kephale seemed to believe it would shatter at any point if given the chance.

.. Insanity, he didn’t even know how he was supposed to tell what kind of shape his soul was in! Let alone how they knew enough about it for him to be bickering over it?! 

“Underestimate? No.. I’m quite aware of the struggles his soul enforced upon me,” Kephale explained with a chuckle that really did sound like he was having too much fun for the situation Phainon and Mydei were in right now,  “I just find it amusing that you’re this confident in him.”

Confidence in him.. In his soul, Mydei had that with him?

.. Phainon seriously didn’t understand what was going on at all when he kept thinking about it, but one thing he knew for certain no matter what.. He just wanted Mydei to remain in his life.

“Mydei,” Phainon breathed out, creasing his brows as he moved just a bit closer to Mydei, “Don’t leave my side..”

Though, this only worked to earn a rather loud and mocking laugh from Kephale, as if he fact Phainon’s yearning was the funniest thing he had ever considered in his entire.. Unlife. 

“He’s clingy to you like a small pup,” Kephale chuckled in between his own words, “Your death will easily shatter him.”

Death.. Phainon found himself scoffing over that; a pitiable threat considering how many times Mydei had promised that he would not die here today, and Phainon.. If Mydei had confidence in Phainon, Phainon easily had just as much confidence in that man and his words. 

Though, oddly, Mydei didn’t respond - he instead remained fighting with his sword clashing into the dead’s moving to slaughter them again and again in that throne room with their practiced dance of defending each other’s vulnerabilities. Staying to themselves in that small clearing they had earned from the piles of shambling bodies that didn’t seem to care how many bones Phainon cleaved through; they only remained attempting to grab at their skin and tear at them. 

“Mydei, you’re speaking less..” Phainon found himself whining a little over it, only hearing a slight click of Kephale tongue at that. Tutting, as if he were about to scold a child. 

“Didn’t you hear him, boy?” Kephale asked, and Phainon almost glanced at him before deciding it simply was not worth it at all, “It’s a battle of stamina, and he’s doomed to lose.”

“Mydei..”

Stamina.

If that was what the issue was time and time again, Phainon found himself struggling to understand how Mydei could lose in that department considering the way that man had been practicing that for months. Spending his days enduring long nights of working with the undead and how long he could keep them out, mixed with other physical training Mydei seemed fond of..

Phainon found himself.. Puzzled over all of this conversation, as if he was missing some or of key part to it that only they were privy to. 

All before Mydei’s voice chuckled a little to his side, gaining his attention and cutting through his thoughts effortlessly; “When a candle is running out of wick, do you let the fire drown in its own wax, or do you blow it out?”

That was enough to make Phainon pause a little as he cut down another foe - feeling his steps slide just a little bit as his mind.. Tried to understand what the hell he was being asked at a time like this. 

Phainon moved his eyes to look at that man - feeling like he was a bit lost as he blinked at Mydei painfully languidly, “Are.. You asking me that?”

“I am,” Mydei answered without missing a single beat as he instead seemed so focused on slaying the monsters in front of him. Another slack and clamboring of metal to only make Phainon’s thoughts feel even more confusing as they banged against the side of his skull. 

“I.. Would let it burn itself out?” Phainon slowly answered - there was no point in saving a candle if the wick was already gone, was there? What kind of question was that? Wouldn’t you merely be left with the glass and a useless candle at that point..?

“Naturally,” Mydei answered rather flippantly and with a small huff of laughter leaving as an exhale through his nose, “There’s no reason to preserve something that has no use left.”

“Am I to understand that as a threat, necromancer?” Kephale spoke at the end of Mydei’s sentence, making Phainon feel just more confused as he moved to slice at another undead - doing his best to try to keep up with it all but at this point he felt like he was here to solve riddles while hitting undead for training..

“I would never threaten another ruler of a country,” Mydei explained in a tone that sounded almost like teasing, one that he may have used while tutting a little when Phainon tried to read his confusing books and was caught red handed, “It goes against my wish for a better life for my people.”

.. Better life for his people felt like salt in the wound, and Phainon didn’t even know if he meant his own wounds or Mydei’s regarding this topic.. Still, his eyes stayed on that man between defending himself and slaying enemies. 

“If.. His time running out was a threat, why would you bring me here today, Mydei?” Phainon felt himself asking - feeling more and more worried about how he had been called a vessel so much today, “Why did you not buy more time and have him waste away?”

“You think a lich would really merely let his time run out? No,” Mydei laughed a little between his own thoughts, turning his head a little to glance rather playfully at Phainon - a look that made Phainon’s head feel fuzzy, “He’s greedy and wants his vessel he desires, so greedy that he would watch through your eyes and wait for me to bring you to him, all while refusing to move his soul beforehand.”

.. Right, this talk again about how his body or whatever was the most valuable thing in the room - all while Phainon had to wonder if Mydei really was simply working on finding the vase in the back of his mind. As if Mydei was talking more than normal right now to try to distract Kephale while his armies looked around for the actual thing holding Kephale’s soul..

“Greed is the most interesting of things,” Kephale hummed in slight amusement as he continued to listen to their ongoing talks,  “I fear you’re not wrong, either.”

Mydei had to hum over that in between slashing down another shambling body that creaked much too much as his sword severed its bones, “Even for a lich moving your soul can be tiring, that’s why he would prefer to have the body he preferred before moving..”

Phainon couldn’t stand it anymore, feeling himself sigh over that - over how his body and soul kept being brought up, yet it felt like no one was actually doing anything. As if the two necromancers were in some odd stalemate and Phainon was just.. Some guy hanging out.

“.. Then.. Why are we talking so much?” He couldn’t stop himself from asking, not when he was so confused and baffled over how Mydei seemed so fine in this situation to just be talking amongst the three of them while they fought for their lives.

Phainon’s eyes even could see the beads of sweat beginning to form on Mydei’s skin due to his own exercise he was getting in now - and yet, they were still.. Just talking and not charging the man watching and mocking them? He was so.. Baffled by this process. 

“That’s all he really can do anymore,” Mydei answered with a bark of laughter - as if he was finally at some kind of breaking point between them all, “A hunger so great that he has to wait for us to move.”

“I could merely have my undead carry me as a king deserves,” Kephale hissed out, sounding much less pleased by Mydei now than he had ever sounded before - making Phainon snap his head upwards a little to look at that man that was heavily glaring at Mydei from where he sat, “Do not think so little of me.”

Mydei seemed unable to fight the urge to laugh over that again - all to earn Phainon’s eyes dancing back to him between defending himself confusedly, “Needing to be carried around already makes me think little of you.”

Phainon had to agree with that as he tried to focus more on attacking those monsters - only to pause a little as Kephale sighed so dramatically loudly once more.

“Can you not feel it? The way that necromancer beside you has already branded your skin? Your soul?” 

Right.. That sun mark that seemed to have been burnt into his skin; honestly, Phainon had almost forgotten about it outside of the way it seemed to glow in the dark as if it had its own heartbeat. 

“Right on your neck.. Such a deep and personal thing to brand you as his own, and yet he never once asked you, did he?”

This foul man must be truly out of tricks and cards to be trying this sort of approach of turning Phainon against Mydei repeatedly. Trying his best to sow discord into Phainon, yet, he could only huff a little bit of laughter over how idiotic it really was. 

Phainon shook his head slowly with his own thoughts, “.. This is a strange way to try to turn me against Mydeimos when you yourself didn’t particularly ask for permission to make me undead, either.” 

Though, he supposed liches didn’t need to be considered ‘smart’, really. They just had a knack for hiding and playing these games where they seemed to tear their souls from their skin. Insanity more than intelligence, that much was apparent to Phainon now. 

“Hah..” Kephale seemed a bit weaker with that breath of air, tired even, “Children are always so unwise when speaking back to their parents.”

“.. I’ve had enough of this, Mydeimos,” Phainon confessed with a heavy sigh - not wanting to continue feeling lost. On the battlefield, that was where he knew and understood himself best - yet his blade barely needed any force behind it to slaughter the undead before him.

It was mind numbing between how easily they fell, and the words scratching his brain and confusing him more between the two necromancers. 

“You can’t.. See what’s fully going on, but I’ll follow your lead,” Mydei told him in a stern voice, nodding curtly and that made Phainon huff a little, shaking his head. 

He knew he couldn’t see fully, but that was all the reason why he needed to end this faster than both of these rambling necromancers were trying to imply it would end!

“Be careful, little knight, we all know just how desperately you want that necromancer to live after all,” Kephale spoke as Phainon only moved to slay yet another of his army - feeling himself rolling his eyes with how tired he was of hearing that voice prattling on about things, “Don’t act too rashly, what if it costs you everything?”

“I feel like I’ll be leaving here with a headache more than anything,” Mydeimos grumbled out, making Phainon give him a little worried stare as he moved forward to slash away at flaying skin - moving to hear more bones crumbling to the floor uselessly. Making shivers run down Phainon’s back as he attempted to still stay close to Mydei.

This was annoying, more than anything. 

There was clearly more to the picture, and Phainon had a sneaking suspicion that it had to do with Mydei’s missing undead army that he had sent through the other entrance. A battle on two fronts and a battle of stamina.. That sounded like it would wear down both necromancers, really. So was Phainon the deciding factor in all of this somehow? Was that why Mydei hadn’t fought him too hard on coming with him?

.. Or was he over thinking it and needed to just keep hacking down zombies as they formed together again with messy and loud gurgles from their lungs releasing air. Death rattled their bones as they tried to gain the upper hand again and again, and Phainon really did think it was frustrating. 

Mainly due to the fact most of the dangerous weapons were aimed at Mydei - was his body too.. ‘Perfect’ for Kephale to want to wound?

That was infuriating enough on its own - if anything, Phainon had come to terms that out of the bodies he had seen; Mydei’s eas easily the most impressive! He was practically flawless in ways Phainon didn’t even think possible, minus the scars on his hands.. But those were a part of Mydei as well!

Phainon found himself tightening his grip on his sword over that - eyes moving to look at the way Mydei was holding onto his own with those gauntlets protecting those hurt and wounded hands.. Hands that Phainon wanted to feel so gently into his own. And that.. That was why he had to end this - somehow. 

“Phainon,” That word was enough to jerk him out of his head, blinking to look at Mydei who only looked right back at him, “Ready to climb that throne?”

“Always, I will protect your back,” Phainon instantly replied with a swift nod, unable to keep himself from seeming more than a little excited as he breamed a sharp grin to that prince. 

“Do your best to keep up then,” Mydei smirked at him - eyes gleaming in a way that made Phainon's heart always start to beat again. Thumping in his ears as he smiled right back at that man. 

“Always,” A repeated and echoed out word, because he meant it time and time again as that prince now moved forward with such confidence that Phainon would be a fool to not continue to follow him.  Moving just as closely behind to make sure he came out of this unharmed, parrying and deflecting attacks between his own movements to make sure Mydei was just as fine in the front.

Praying to whatever god would care to hear him out in this one rare moment to make sure no dead that was already discarded into piles on the floor grabbed at Mydei’s ankles or something else. Horrifying.. Phainon really did need to stop borrowing Mydei’s necromancy and horror books in his spare time, probably..

Phainon felt himself scoffing quietly as they neared that man however - watching Kephale rise to his feet and grab the sword at the side of his throne with a small little laugh escaping him. A mocking one, but it’s not like Phainon himself had come here not expecting a fight from that man. If anything, he would have been almost disappointed if Kephale had just sat there the entire time. 

Though, Phainon already didn’t enjoy the way Kephale’s eyes seemed fixed on Mydei - as if that was the only real threat as he languidly moved closer. Eyes that seemed so focused on the prince that Phainon had to click his tongue over it - making sure to force the undead to  keep their distance from Mydei all while getting closer to that king.

False king, a painful thing as Phainon tried to ignore the sting he felt in his back - an ache of where the blade he loved had been used for something so foul. Disgusting, and yet today he would claim it for himself again - gritting his teeth a little as he followed Mydei and approached that man.

A shambling and decaying body that should not be able to move the way it did - immediately lunging at the both of them and wielding that blade like it was nothing. A movement that made Phainon instinctively move to block the blow - only to find his own sword matched by Mydei’s, both of them blocking it together.

.. Romance may be dead since Phainon was quite dead - but Phainon found it alive in his unbeating heart all the less as they both moved to parry that sword. A sword that only came down repeatedly, again and again while that king’s tattered garments now were so obviously torn and ruined from his decay. 

White and flowery - golden trimmed, now awful and graying, as if they hadn’t been washed from the moment that man claimed Kephale’s body as his own and gave up his act with Phainon. Instead now he seemed to be sneering while aiming every single attack for Mydei - precise movements bent on harming Mydei every time he slung ‘his’ blade forward. 

Not to mention the undead still creeping around them, still armed to the teeth with blades bent to claim Mydei’s life and end it all - if Mydei did fall here, Phainon felt an odd sense of dread over the idea of trying to find that vase thing Mydei told him about.

That, and something about the idea of Mydei dying made him worry about the marking on his neck amongst.. The other worries. But there was no use lingering on it - instead moving to do his best to attack alongside Mydei, feeling his mind be baffled over how easily that man was moving with almost hysterical laughter leaving his throat in a gobbled tone every time they failed to reach him.

Dancing away from them so easily before moving right back to try to claim Mydei’s life, an action Phainon absolutely couldn’t allow as he felt himself repeatedly trying to step in and stop that man. Doing his best to land any attacks he could all before feeling his eyes snap to the side just in time to see someone new.

A zombie, and yet, between blocking that aggressive king, there wasn’t any possibility he could help Mydei - he couldn’t move his sword from Mydei’s own with the crushing force of a lich pushing down on both their blades. All he could do was feel the horror creep into him as Mydei moved once more to dodge another attack. 

Phainon couldn’t help the ragged breath he took in over the sight of Mydei’s arm being slashed from that nameless undead - along with that prince stumbling back just a hair before retaliating without missing a beat. A sharp exhale from Mydei along with his sword swinging to slash the undead down before moving to focus again on the fight.

But Phainon felt his mind running rampant over the blood he could see now - the splatter of blood on the marble flooring, “Mydei?!”

“It’s not deep,” Mydei growled out, not passing up a single moment to instead attack that zombie once more - a ragged breath seeming to leave his throat as he moved, “Worry about the king in front of you.” 

That.. Was what he should be doing, but instead he kept becoming more and more afraid for Mydei - only able to move and attack Kephale almost languidly, his mind not even allowing him to listen to the quiet whispers that Kephale seemed to be uttering inaudibly.

Everything almost seemed as if it were moving in slow motion - his eyes trying to focus on Kephale, yet it all felt like he was in some type of haze as he continuously danced with that king. Steel against steel, doing his best to parry for his beloved prince, all while trying his hardest to land any attack on that zombified king. And yet.. 

He was struggling in a way he had never thought he could before, instead finding his movements heavy and slowed - as if he were in a daze now. 

“Phainon,” Mydei spoke, making his snap his head a little to look at Mydei between his movements - blinking a little, “Stay focused, would you?”

That was easier said than done for some reason, making Phainon feel his hands on his blade relaxing a little - as if he were getting ready for a nap all before watching Mydei grab his chin roughly. Yanking him forward just a tiny bit, “Focus on me, if you can focus on nothing else and stay awake, you fool.”

.. Awake?

Was Phainon actually falling asleep mid fight? That didn’t seem like him, yet he found his skin burning with Mydei’s touch, huffing a little laugh as Mydei moved to quickly lash at that king as if he hadn’t just been panting in Phainon’s face. 

“Focus on you? I’m never not watching you, Mydei!” Phainon countered after a few moments, moving to join that man all while trying his best to ignore the way his body still felt sluggish - as if it were fighting him in his time of need insanely. And Phainon.. Had a sneaking suspicion that it had something to do with that odd chant Kephale had taken up.

That he was somehow messing with Phainon now that he was this close, and in a way, Phainon was regretting this. Regretting the fact he had gotten closer and maybe added more strain to Mydei - especially due to that new wound on Mydei’s arm.. 

But all he could do now was listen to Mydei - his eyes continuously finding their way back to the man he wanted to see the dawn with. The man he wanted to watch grow old, and be there every step of the way. The man he felt so selfish towards wanting to be by his side forever, and that.. Had to easily be enough to keep him awake.

If it wasn’t; looking at that bleeding wound with his torn fabric on his arm did enough in itself alone. 

That seemed to help with the fog in his mind rather easily - aiding him in darting forward and doing his best to kill that man, all while still fending off zombies. He now was a bit more focused on the zombies due to that wound, as well. Undesiring for another to catch either of them off guard and instead determined to defend Mydei while the both of them battled that man.

Even if he felt almost dizzy in this battle, he could only try his best - right? And what kind of knight was he to allow his king to become wounded on the battlefield.

.. He would never live this down in his mind, and yet he still moved to fight. 

Every swing was one that he dreaded, that he prayed would meet with flesh and they all would crumble one last time. Never to stand and walk again, all before his mind felt like it was falling deeper and deeper into an odd slumber.

“Soon,” That was the word that made him snap his eyes to Mydei - taking a moment to process it as Mydei flawlessly moved to lash out at Kephale again. The metal rang in Phainon’s ears as he realized what that meant - soon, Mydei’s army would find that phylactery and end it all. 

That Kephale’s time was running out as they continued to fight here, that every movement could be Kephale’s last as he continued his odd gibberish chanting up annoyingly. 

That this lich would go down in history as a monster, and nothing more - that this slaughter would end and Phainon and Mydei could both try to move on together.. 

“To be a lich and have such weak defensives around your phylactery.. Were you planning on leaving?” Mydei asked as he blocked a blow, holding his ground from that lich so easily.

All while Kephale chuckled lowly over it, yet he didn’t reply. Instead opting to continue that chanting beneath his breath in a language Phainon couldn’t understand - one of the ones in Mydei’s books, surely. 

But Phainon found it for his best interest to do his best to ignore whatever it was - instead moving to try to slice off one of those hollow appearing arms only to be refuted easily. Groaning a little over how quick on his feet Kephale was, all while looking like a small gust of wind could take him down.

.. That probably had something to do with the idea of a lich enchanting their own body, probably. Along the lines of the make Mydei had given to Phainon, if he had to guess about it.

Though, every movement felt like he was still in some kind of daze as he tried to fight that man - becoming less sure if he was just too quick, or if his mind was just fraying at the seams. 

Nothing mattered, how could it ever matter as there were creaking noises around Phainon - metal clanking to the floor and bodies dropping so swiftly that it made Phainon’s eyes dip around worriedly. 

And nothing prepared Phainon for the way Kephale froze, such a quick second that Phainon was stunned with how quickly he flopped down onto the floor messily - on his back with an expression of acute horror marring his face. A movement of fabric and limbs that sprawled out in such an odd fashion..

The clattering of metal along with his flopping to the floor was enough to make Phainon take a step back - eyes wide as he watched his own beloved sword fall to the ground. 

Phainon’s head snapped to look at the man - stunned over it, though he couldn’t help but notice the way Mydei had frozen as well, seeming more dazed than Phainon almost which was impressive considering the way Phainon’s mind had seemed like a blur for the last few minutes. Now blessed by a newfound clarity that made him feel more human again, just a bit.  

“He’s..” Phainon croaked out, eyes unable to look away from the man who had just fallen to the ground as if he were simply a sack of potatoes. Now he laid there - motionlessly, and so uselessly. Surely that wasn’t a ploy of sorts - not when the eerie glow of his eyes seemed vacant as well, and his whispers had ceased tearing at Phainon’s consciousness.

Yet, Phainon only barely turned to look at him, feeling his boots scratching against the floor beneath him as his eyes glanced at those zombies that were now turning to dust as well. He had half of his mind to wonder if that was his fate in a few moments as well, eyes instead finding their way to the prince beside him.

All the words he had never said to Mydei, the things Phainon had wanted to see with him by his side, and now he felt choked up over the idea his time was out.  That freeing his people, obtaining justice.. It was a bell tolling for him as well, if he was truly still chained to that man.

Mydei huffed out a quiet little noise, all before taking a step closer to Kephale - an action Phainon couldn’t find it in himself to allow as he instead jutted his arm out to stop that man, “I’ll make sure he’s dead.”

Phainon said those words; sure. But even he could hear the way his words quivered on his tongue, hanging in the air uncomfortably and burning into his throat. All while he didn’t move, he didn’t think he could move yet as he remained there stopping Mydei from moving, and a piece of him was thankful that Mydei.. Seemed to understand.

In some odd way, at least, as that man sighed softly - but not in a way that read as annoyance, instead; he spoke so painfully sweetly.

“.. You don’t even know what you’re looking for, my undead killed the phylactery, but..” Mydei pointed out timidly, a ghost of his normal voice and Phainon couldn’t blame him for that. Not as his own eyes roamed over Kephale’s body once more - trailing up to his face that seemed twisted into an expression of horror.

.. And Phainon felt some level of annoyance at that. 

Ironic for that monster to be horrified at his own ending finally coming to him, while puppeting a man who would have looked like that the entire time he did all those crimes.

Though, Phainon found himself basking in some level of terror because he truly had no idea if he was still.. Himself, not when he was standing there unmoving - as if he was waiting for some force to take his mind over and make him surrender or have everything fade to black. He had.. No idea, but one thing he knew was how desperately he needed to make sure Mydei wasn’t in danger..

“I’ll stab him and leave this sword in him, happy?” Phainon forced himself to say, his hands loosely gripping onto his own sword before glancing at the sword he actually knew. A bit to the side of Kephale, sitting there with the blood of innocents forever smelted into its blade.

It was enough to make him sigh as he moved to that man’s side languidly, staring at the rotting body that laid before him - a thing that made his stomach churn so painfully uncomfortably at how Kephale had never been able to rest. 

“Tear.. Open his chest.”

Those words were enough to make Phainon pause, coming even more to terms that Kephale still wouldn’t be able to rest - not with what Mydei was instructing him to do to that corpse who just.. Deserved to be buried. 

Phainon had to slowly turn his feet to Mydei - looking at him with a meticulous stare as he tried to figure out if that necromancer was being serious or not. 

.. He surely was, there was no reason or possibility that Mydei of all people would be joking right now, and yet - Phainon’s brain simply couldn’t comprehend what that man was saying to him currently. As if he was speaking in a language Phainon didn’t have a grasp on like Mydei’s books or something else.

“.. Huh?” That was the intelligent reply Phainon conjured up after a few moments of staring at Mydei - looking at the way he only had such a heavy and dark serious expression on his face. As if he knew how truly grim this request was that he was asking of Phainon to complete. 

“There should be a magic jewel in there, if you want to make sure he’s dead while forcing me to stay away.” Mydei explained with a quiet little sigh leaving his lips as he flicked his eyes south again - at that body they both were staying a little away from, “Start tearing open his chest and digging, or start stabbing into it blindly.. Whichever one suits you best.”

Whichever suited him best.. Those were silly words as Phainon forced himself to look away from Mydei - his eyes finding purchase on that deceased man once more only to feel his hands quiver again. It was hard to keep them stable when he thought of that man and how dazzling his light once was, how beautiful their kingdom and seas of wheat were - all of that had crumbled so far.

“Just.. Don’t come too close, Mydei,” Phainon forced himself to grumble out - barely even speaking out loud from how pained he actually felt. 

This was not.. How his story with Kephale was ever supposed to end, it just wasn’t fair to his mind, and it never would be.. 

“.. Mm.”

Phainon’s hands were shaky on his sword, naturally - how was he supposed to stand there above Kephale and be normal about this task he was given. He was determined to do it, to protect Mydei - and yet he could only see the man he had cared for so deeply now, the man that had been gone for so long.. 

.. Now he had to stab into that man blindly, or tear his chest open and search for something he didn’t even understand. Phainon.. Could only find himself moving his other hand to hold onto the hilt of his blade to try to steady himself - not willing to think twice about what he was doing before bringing his sword down into that man’s chest.

Once.

Twice.

Three times. Four.. Five.. Six.. He lost count after a point, really. 

He didn’t know anymore, not as he felt the burn of his own tears on his skin while he continuously brought that sword down - his ears aching every time he listened to skin giving way for a blade to sink into that body, every movement making him feel more and more ashamed.

Ashamed of how deeply he had failed this man, ashamed that at the end of the day they had both died such horrible deaths, ashamed that he couldn't help him at all. And now he was defiling his corpse in such a horrid way - would that man ever forgive him? Would he ever see Phainon at the end of it all and still smile at him?

Did Phainon even deserve such an expression when his hands should be hollow and rotting like Kephales? Weak and decaying to join the earth, and instead he was fine - his body was safe and now he was ruining Kephale’s even more. 

What right did he have to keep stabbing this man who was undoubtedly dead? The man who had meant so much to Phainon and now all he could do was repeat the action of pushing his blade into his chest again and again.

“.. Phainon,” Mydei hushedly said, his hands already cupping over the top of Phainon’s shaky ones in a plea to be heard, “You can stop now.”

That was enough to make his hands pause - eyes barely able to tell that the gentle gauntlet a top of his own was Mydei’s through his blurry tears. Head tilting a little to look away from that mangled corpse and to the man who was telling him it was enough.

Phainon.. Didn’t know what to do as he slowly unhanded that blade - eyes not looking down before he let out a shuddering breath to instead move to his sword from his sister. The one she had laughed and called Dawnmaker, and now it was truly all he had left of his homeland besides the pile of corpses and bitter memories.. 

Phainon had to try his best to ignore it - to move instead to look at Mydei who was bent over, kneeling beside Kephale to apparently close the corpse’s eyes for him with clawed yet somehow tender hands. Every movement precise as Phainon watched him, and yet, his eyes could only focus on the blood that was still seeping out of Mydei’s arm slowly. A wound that made him suck in a little bit of breath before approaching that man. 

“Mydei.. Speak to me before being reckless with your plans!” Phainon growled out as he moved to grab at Mydei’s uninjured arm - moving to turn him to look at Phainon. Though, those fiery amber eyes were still focused on that unmoving body of Kephale, as if he couldn’t bring himself to look away for too long and that made sense.. 

Who knew if they were actually successful - Phainon certainly didn’t know with how much he had stabbed Kephale yet Mydei was focused on the corpse still.. Well, Mydei probably was aware of it or not if his undead were fighting still or at peace - whatever the case, Mydei’s eyes took their time actually moving to Phainon from that butchered corpse. 

“Forgive me,” Mydei gruffly mumbled out, and that was enough to make Phainon’s hands pause a little, his eyes trailing the blood on Mydei’s arm a little languidly before daring to look at that necromancer who seemed to swallow heavily under his gaze, “I was always aware of it.”

“Aware.. Of it?” Phainon echoed out in his pure confusion, not sure what that man was really saying to him as he tried to understand what Mydei was trying to convey - only.. Mydei looked so painfully uncomfortable over that question, shuffling his weight a little even as Phainon kept his hands on Mydei’s arm. 

“His grip on you, so small that you most likely never even noticed it. Such a little thing that I couldn’t figure out how to pry it from you without chipping at your own soul,” Mydei’s mouth stayed open for a moment, all before seeming to steel himself about something,  “Telling you actually important information was out of the question.”

.. Out of the question?

All this time together, and Mydei could never fully trust him - because he.. Knew something was wrong with Phainon? All these months, and Mydei was most likely somewhat on edge around him? Denying their closeness, denying Phainon being his knight, and refusing to explain most of his plans like today..

.. Was because a piece of that lich was lurking inside of Phainon, waiting? 

“H.. Huh?” Phainon choked out, trying his best to stop the blooming nervous laughter he could feel in his gut as his mind raced over being told this now, “I was.. Always just his puppet..?”

A tool? Was that all Phainon had ever been, even in death he had been used as a little jester doing a dance for that man? A tool to spy on Mydei, and their lives, for his own enjoyment? And Mydei.. Had to just live with that knowledge silently?

“No,” Mydei replied rather flatly, making Phainon hands tremble a little over how little Mydei seemed willing to even think about that idea, "That's not what I meant. If anything, it’s more like you were his window he could see out of and watch keenly. A piece of him he could yearn for, but never force or control.”

“I.. A piece of him.. I was some sort of portal for him?” Phainon asked in a broken and confused voice - even to his own ears as he struggled to comprehend what Mydei meant. He had heard their conversation earlier, sure, but he just.. Didn’t know exactly how far being a ‘vessel’ actually meant.

“Not quite, more like a one-sided window, but I’ll agree to it.” Mydei mumbled, sounding a little distracted, but that only made Phainon feel more and more antsy as he stood there so close to Mydei.

“You’re.. You’re wounded, can I be trusted enough to-”

“Phainon,” Mydei hissed out, already moving to place two hands on both of Phainon’s cheeks - squeezing him just a little to make blue eyes clash into golden, “You are you, I promise you that much. He could see from your own eyes, nothing more.”

Phainon didn’t have a breath to even attempt to steady, and yet, he found himself taking a moment to sweat a little in Mydei’s tender hold. Stern and tight, yet nothing that could ever hurt Phainon, just enough to ground him in this situation and demand his attention. 

It was enough to make him sigh and flick his eyes downwards to Mydei’s arm again, “You weren’t supposed to get hurt.. Not again.. Not while I’m at your side.”

Phainon found himself sighing as Mydei released his hold on Phainon’s cheeks, allowing him to focus his eyes wholly on that wound and slowly move his hands to Mydei’s bicep tenderly. Every single movement made his body shake with absolute dread, a raw fear that he could be causing this man pain and Mydei probably wouldn’t show it. 

“Things happen.” Mydei huffed out, and Phainon had to scoff over that, knitting his brows together in worry before biting on his lower lip a little - still gingerly touching at Mydei to look at that bleeding wound. 

“.. Can you ask them to stop happening?” Phainon hissed out, unable to stop himself as he noted the wound there wasn’t deep.

Not at all, it probably wouldn’t leave a lasting scar on Mydei - and that was a thing to be thankful for, even if now he was very aware that this prince should at least wear some armor.. The clothes he decided to wear into battle hadn’t been enough at all..

“I’ll try.” Mydei mumbled out, though his tone was light-hearted, a bit of a joking hum as he managed to say those words. 

“Thank you.. I don’t ask for much..” Phainon murmured back with a small smile on his lips as he instead moved to shuffle his hands into his pockets - fishing out a small cloth to at least cover the wound and stop the bleeding. And at this point, he was endlessly thankful that he had begun to carry around bandages like this all the time. 

“Hmph,” Mydei didn’t really move however, remaining there as he allowed Phainon to rather timidly wrap his arm in a bandage, “How are you feeling?”

.. How was Phainon feeling?

Why were his own feelings important when Mydei was the one wounded? That question and realization made Phainon jerk his head a little to look that blonde haired man in the eyes - blinking as he tilted his head a little to the side. 

“Why? Should I be worried about losing control of myself?”

It was a genuine question, and a new fear he had gained suddenly. 

All to make Mydei give him a rather flat looking expression, less than amused - and more so pitying, as if he couldn’t even believe this was a thing Phainon was now dreading. 

“.. No, I meant mentally.”

“I..” Phainon flitted his eyes away at that, trying his best to find reasons in his mind to keep messing with Mydei’s arm - to continue holding onto him for some sort of comfort, “I would be better if you hadn’t been injured.”

“It’s a minor flesh wound, Phainon,” Mydei’s voice was soft, soothing even - as if he was doing his best to calm down Phainon even though he himself was the wounded one. And Phainon..

Phainon could barely control the tremble in his hands, that mounting fear in his veins over failing to defend Mydei and seeing him fall in combat. This was the second time he had been wounded while fighting alongside him and Phainon felt as if he were slowly going mad over it.

“A wound is a wound..” Phainon chuckled out a little bitterly, gritting his teeth over it all - would Mydei have been better off alone and without him, truly, in this fight? If Kephale had been using him to spy, why did Mydei stay with him? Why did Mydei allow Phainon to cling to his side for so long..?

Phainon now understood why Mydei had changed the actual plans and not informed him, and yet he still just felt so dreadfully unsure of himself..

“Can.. He really not use my body? We..” Phainon trailed off, unsure of how to even ask this question as he sat there staring at that wound. Not even deep enough to bleed through the bandage Phainon had wrapped around his arm, and yet it felt world shattering to him.

A tiny little crack in Mydei that felt as if it was a stab through Phainon’s own chest, a painful and dull ache that sent shivers down his body when he looked at the torn flesh there. Mydei had surely gone through much worse, but Phainon couldn’t help but feel at fault for this. 

“We broke his phylactery, his soul is no longer bound to this world; Not even to make you into a puppet, Phainon.”  Mydei explained in that same voice that was as sweet as possible, laced with a layer of near-seduction that Phainon couldn’t help but pay attention to as he dared to look Mydei in the eyes, just a little, “Besides..”

Mydei gave him a somber smile at that - one that was almost near disarming with how honey filled it seemed. Enchanting Phainon the more he looked at him, and easily making his derailing thoughts stop in their tracks. 

“I promise you, I would merely kill you and make sure you stayed down if you were truly lost.”

Phainon shouldn’t feel comforted by that, he should feel scared and almost insulted that Mydei was threatening him in such a way that made his body shake. Only, when he truly considered it, that shake was not out of fear, nor terror. But something else, a thin feeling of yearning and warmth, a desire to reach out and cradle that man while thanking him for that mercy he was granting him.

Phainon found himself slowly exhaling over that - whatever breath he had as a man that didn’t need to breathe leaving him as he cocked his head to the side; “.. You truly will promise me that?” 

He was hopeful that those words were true, and that Mydei meant them fully. 

“Would it allow you to rest easily?” Mydei asked in that same soft tone - one that almost felt a bit off putting to Phainon, at least, it should. He should find it odd that Mydei was being so gentle on this topic, kind of caring - all while saying he would kill Phainon, if he wanted it.

And well.. Phainon wanted that to be his fate so horribly bad; “.. Yes.”

“Very well,” Mydei mumbled as he immediately took his arm from Phainon - an act that made Phainon feel a deep rooted amount of sorrow for just a moment. All before Mydei rather gingerly placed a hand on Phainon’s shoulder, shaking him the tiniest of bits, “Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, I vow that if you one day lose yourself beyond comprehension; I will hunt you down to slay you and lay you down for your true final rest.”

Something about that felt wrong, even as Phainon stayed there with a hand on his shoulder - staring into those golden eyes that seemed so welcoming and understanding.. He knew fully this wasn’t what he wanted.

This wasn’t the true thing he needed from this man, the reassurance that Mydei would slay him was comforting, absolutely, but he found himself only craving more from him. A thin frown on his lips as he breathed out such a heavy sigh over that vow he had been given.

“Thank you..” Phainon forced himself to say, though he already found himself fighting the urge to chew into his own bottom lip as he blinked at those fierce golden eyes,  “I have.. Another selfish request, Mydeimos.”

“And what is that?” Mydei asked so innocently, so blissfully unaware that Phainon felt almost guilty - he was so selfish with this man. He felt the burn of how much he desired those eyes to always be on him, to always pay him attention and be mindful of him.

He didn’t dare read any further into it, though, he knew fully well he was yearning for more from Mydei than he had ever assumed or thought possible to want from someone else. 

“Knight me.” 

Those words left his lips without a second thought, so greedily said in a way that even to Phainon’s ears, they sounded like a demand. A command for the man he himself found to be his king, his desired ruler over him, and yet - he was so painfully needy in regards to him that he couldn’t keep himself back. 

And the boldness of such a statement wasn’t only a shock to himself it seemed - not as Mydei’s eyes widened in blatant disbelief, unsure of what he was supposed to be making of this conversation or that demand being made of him now. 

“.. Pardon me?”

“Whether I am to become a tool for you to use and throw away, or someone you trust more than others,” Phainon barely took even a second moment to rethink his words - instead moving to fall to once knee. His hands presenting his own blade towards that man now as he keenly stared upwards to him. Phainon would have desired to bow his head in respect towards his kind usually, but.. He fully knew Mydei would prefer eye contact and mutual respect when speaking instead.

Thus, Phainon could only let out a shuddering breath as he stared at that man who looked a little.. Amused by this display, golden eyes only slowly tracing over the blade held between Phainon’s two hands, “Please.. Grant me this mercy and give this blade a different meaning than all the bloodshed it has seen before it. It was never my sister’s intention for it to be used on our own people, let alone myself.”

And then there was silence, a painful thing as Phainon dared to remain staring at that prince - waiting with bated breath for whatever reply he would earn. Whatever it was, he would have to accept it somewhere in his heart - though.. 

He knew he couldn’t do that. Not when this man had begun to mean so much to him. 

“Whatever knight ceremony I can give to you holds no water, I am-”

“No king. I’m aware of this, and yet you are the king I have chosen, is that such a bad thing? To selfishly seek solace from a king who has lost it all, while being the same as he?” Phainon was genuinely asking, nearing his limit for all the times he had heard this man oddly put himself down - to deny his own heritage and bloodline. More importantly, to be so obviously running from something.

It wasn’t like Mydei, and perhaps he was only like this towards the topic due to his own family being at the core of it; or the fact he was the only survivor haunted every step he took.

Whatever it was, Phainon only wanted to remain near him and take those steps along with him. Was that such a bad thing?

“Must we truly find repentance for such a crime, or will you allow me to be greedy, just this once?” Phainon continued on, feeling himself swallow over his own words as he thought about how truly greedy he was being. Begging Mydei here and now, for just one chance, one that would last forever - but a chance nonetheless. And as Mydei stared down at him and twisted his face through so many emotions, Phainon could only pray his gamble was worth it all. 

All before he seemed to relax a little, closing his eyes before heaving out a little sigh and shaking his head leisurely, “.. Very well, since you are so earnest in your desires, I will indulge you.”

With those words fierce golden eyes blinked open again, staring down at Phainon as he seemed to be morphing into the appearance of complete seriousness. A taut line on his lips as he moved a little to cross his arms over his chest - albeit, a bit looser to avoid the gash on his arm this time around. 

“Remain on your knees, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae,” Mydei told him in such an odd voice - one he had never quite used with Phainon before, and Phainon could only assume it was his more.. Royal one. For his royal duties that no longer existed in his life, all while Mydei gingerly took that sword from Phainon’s hands.

A feeling that was foreign to Phainon; to seek out that sword so earnestly, only to give it up immediately to his king. A thing that he almost felt right in doing this time around, but still one that made his bones shake and rattle in his joints in rather incomprehensible ways, even to himself. 

Though, Phainon didn’t shy away from dropping his hands at that - bowing his head finally and closing his eyes.

Even if Mydei decided to repeat fate once more, to become a second king to try to slay him; a piece of Phainon would find peace in it.

.. He probably wouldn’t though, not really, since well.. He wouldn’t die from the wound and would have to continue as an undead that had been stabbed by the man he trusted once again. 

But, he liked to think he would be at peace dying to Mydei right now - even if he knew there would be more layers to killing him.. Probably something about removing the magical force keeping him ‘alive’, but he digresses.. 

"Perseverance is a rather rare trait to run so deeply through one’s veins, let alone as admirably as it flows through yourself. You have my respect for that.” Mydei paused at that, and Phainon was left feeling his mind struggle over those words - doing his best to understand the praise he was receiving right now. All before feeling the blade of his own sword against his shoulder - the blunt underside of it, but enough to make his thoughts stall over it. 

“Devotion runs through your entire core to a depth that I almost fail to fathom, and yet you’ve shown it to me time and time again.. I have nothing but admiration for such a feat.”

Phainon found himself sucking in air over that - a useless attempt to fill lungs that had long since ceased functioning, all to feel that blade move to the other shoulder so gently.

Tenderly, yet, his own mind was faltering when he continued to think about how that man was praising his personality; his features. Telling him what he admired about him, all while fully meaning it - it was enough to make Phainon struggle to keep a normal smile on his lips. Instead slowly raising his head as he felt that blade fully leave his shoulders.

Only to stare at that man who now was looking at the sword a bit idly, taking his time to inspect the smelting of it - the craft and dedication. And unlike the last time in this situation  with a different king in front of him and pacing around him, it felt almost impossible to feel any malice with Mydei’s actions. 

Phainon felt himself crack a smile as he stared upwards at that man; “If I knew I would be praised by you so deeply during this, I would have begged more for it sooner.”

That made Mydei raise a brow - glancing at him before moving to shake his head a little slowly, a chuckle leaving his lips as his eyes settled on that blade he still had in his hands. Holding it as if it were a fragile treasure, even to Mydei who had no idea the full meaning behind that blade.

“.. I’ve never done a knighting ceremony, I’m unsure what else I was supposed to say.” Mydei admitted, but that only made Phainon grin even more - completely at his own mercy to give into those swelling feelings of pure and utter happiness as he watched that man fiddle with his blade.

No longer seeming as if he was carefully looking at the craft, but now so blatantly trying to avoid eye contact with Phainon instead and opting to use it as an excuse. 

“You’re doing perfect,” Phainon told him as he slowly rose to his feet - intending on taking that blade from Mydei and feeling himself smile a little over what a lack of a fight he gave over  it. Allowing Phainon to simply.. Regain that blade, just as it had always belonged to him.

“I’m not saying you’re doing anything wrong, I just am reflecting on my own past actions of not trying to get your praise sooner. It’s rather addicting to hear it from you.” Phainon couldn’t help but laugh a little, watching the way that prince now had nothing to waste his gaze on. Instead flicking it to meet Phainon’s own a bit. 

“.. You have a rather sly tongue for a knight,” Mydei huffed in an extremely tired sounding tone, all before rolling his eyes the more he seemed to think on it, “Regardless, I suppose you're my knight of all things, as well now.”

“Correct, and I will do my utmost best to serve you!” Phainon chirped out as he now happily moved to sheathe that blade back up - humming all the while as he keenly watched the way Mydei still appeared antsy.

As if that ceremony was something that was embarrassing for him; but that was all the more reason why Phainon found himself treasuring it so much more. 

“Such an eager knight..”

Mydei tutted as he noted that, sure, but it wasn’t as if Mydei hadn’t known or expected it - Phainon was quite sure he had been open and honest about his eagerness so many times before. Yet now, it was merely something he was allowed to show on display for his king. 

“Should I carry you back home, as well?” Phainon offered without missing a single beat - feeling a smile grow on his lips as he slowly straightened himself out and beamed towards Mydei. Doing his best to completely ignore the way Mydei’s jaw had twitched over it. Tightening and looking strained as he clicked his tongue a bit over the offer. 

All before Mydei sighed painfully loudly; “.. My arm is barely wounded, and nothing is wrong with my legs, you mutt.”

Sure, Mydei was acting almost annoyed, but Phainon had gotten used to this; Honing his own ability to be able to tell when the man was actually amused and doing his best to keep his laughter on the topic to himself. 

.. This was one of those times, by the way. 

“Very well, Very well.. But I was simply offering.” Phainon hummed out, unable to keep himself from smiling quite widely over it - eyes looking up as he did his best to move beside that man. Already falling back into the rhythm of being at the side of Mydei, the place he felt most at home..

Phainon had to blink his eyes and jerk his head to the side as his balance was thrown off just a little. The tiniest of amounts as Mydei seemed to knock their shoulders together with a quiet little chuckle leaving his own throat, “No, my knight, I still have the ability to walk.”

“If you ever falter, I will be there to catch you. Do not forget that, that goes even for these easy walks together.”

“Sappy.”

──────────────

“Phainon,” Mydei began, turning on his heels and looking at Phainon with a tilt of his head innocently, “Do you have something you wish to say?”

The man in question had to look away at that - instead moving his eyes to look at the sparks floating through the air, the smoke rising to the night sky. It was a beautiful thing, really, even if the garden was now wilted and gone - it would have truly have been where Kephale himself would have loved to be buried.

Phainon for that reason found himself merely sitting there silently, unable to think of much as he stared at the night stars above them both. 

It was so painfully quiet now with all the undead released, a thing that Mydei had mumbled something about ‘fulfilling his oath’ in regards to that abomination when Phainon had asked where it had slinked off to. And now.. It was merely the both of them in the silent world around them, the fire’s crackles being the only thing to keep them company with the distant cicadas. 

“No.” 

Phainon didn’t look down - he feared what he would see instead of the inviting universe above them, he worried about the reality that was in front of him. The end of an era, that he had never fully come to terms with when he thought about any of it for too long. It felt as if it were a blur that had wounded his soul in too many differing ways. 

“You were his knight for many years,” Mydei argued at that, his voice as sweet as honeycakes but Phainon didn’t know if he could budge on this topic,  “Surely you would want to.. To say at least a few words?”

“No.”

That was his reply yet again, because his own mind already felt as if it were cracking and fraying the longer he even considered.. Speaking about Kephale. 

The man who was actually Kephale, not the lich who had stolen his identity and abused his body in death - the actual human who.. Phainon wasn’t even sure how to put it into words of how treasured he was by his kingdom, or to himself.

.. The thought made his hands twitch as he sat on that marble bench motionlessly staring at the sky - idly aware of the way Mydei was pacing, just the tiniest of bits. 

All before Mydei stopped moving, no longer allowing Phainon to hear the rustling of slightly overgrown weeds getting stuck on his feet and tearing when the prince moved too much. Instead, it was a new layer of silence - all before Mydei pressed out a rather quiet sigh. 

 “.. I see.”

Phainon felt his face burn with those words, moving to gnaw at his own tongue a little as his mouth felt full of cotton - he had no idea how to convince Mydei he was fine, but he had to try.

“Kephale already long since passed and had his reputation blemished beyond the need of a f-”

“All the more reason to pay your respects to him now so he may fully rest,” Mydei countered without even letting Phainon finish - leaving him to stare at the sky with an open and slack mouth, “I did not meet or know Kephale when he was living, nor while he was in full control of himself. But I do know he was a king worthy of having his last remaining knight’s favor, just one more time.”

Phainon wanted to hang his head in shame with those words - he wanted to dive into sand and not think about this anymore. He didn’t want to think of his years with Kephale, and how it all was finally over - a chapter of a book that was written and done, left to be forgotten to the tests of times as a footnote. 

He wanted to.. He wanted to just ignore it, to not think about who all he had lost - to not think of how everyone was lost but one man that was important to him now.

“.. I am your knight now.”

Those were the words Phainon pushed himself to say, those were the words that were truth as they felt like ash on his tongue. He meant them, he did, but he also knew that would never be enough. He could feel those golden eyes studying him, watching him, and he knew Mydei was probably aware of it.

Aware of the way he was trembling, shaking with his own sorrow that was clawing into his body and threatening to drown himself. A deep rooted emotion he had avoided thinking about until now, the man behind the evil that he had tried to not think too long about - a piece of him hoping that somehow..

Some way.. Even Kephale could have been saved.. A piece of him was so greedy, that he had remained hopeful, up until this very moment.. And now..

“While his body burns to ash, I can bring myself to let him borrow your loyalty one last time,” Mydei told him with a soft tone, too kind and sweet - it only worked to add to Phainon’s agony. 

“I don’t..” Phainon tried to speak, to figure out what he wanted to say all while he now had to fully come to terms that the man he knew was forever gone, “I don’t know what to say, Mydei.”

“Speak to him one last time, won’t you?” Mydei pressed onwards, and as much as Phainon felt like he was suffocating - he was thankful for it, at the very least,  “One last talk between the both of you, as if I were not even here.”

He was thankful that even without him saying it, Mydei knew that.. 

He did want to speak to Kephale one last time, he wanted to hear his voice and his laughter, he wanted to be close to him and enjoy their time together. He wanted to eat dinner with him and be told about his day, he wanted to see that man smiling at him and telling him he did a good job. He wanted him to correct the way he was holding his sword and pat him on the head again.

He wanted to speak to Kephale while he wasn’t being burnt to ashes in front of Phainon..

.. He just wanted another day with Kephale, was that.. So bad? 

“Mydei..” Phainon forced himself to speak as he drooped his head a little - his eyes finding their way to looking at Mydei, though.. That didn’t help at all.

Not with how much kindness and attention was being layered throughout his facial expression - looking so dreadfully inviting for Phainon to just cling to him and hide away. And yet, he fully knew that the prince had no intentions of letting him run, not when this was the last chance Phainon had to speak to that man.

“He was practically your father, correct? I knew rumors of the king of Aedes Elysiae adopting a child whose home was ravaged and burnt to the ground. An orphan with nothing left, and new found loyalty to the man who saved him and grew up to be his trusted personal knight..”

Ah.

So Mydei knew even that - that was enough to make Phainon close his eyes and try to breathe out a shallow little breath to stay sane in this instance. 

An orphan with no one left in his life, not even a home, yet.. Kephale had given him one and a reason to keep walking - a kingdom to grow so painfully fond of, and do his best for his adoptive father to see it flourish. Only for both of their dreams and hopes to be cut down so easily by the evil within the world, and now.. 

“That’s you, is it not?”

“.. Yes, That’s me,” Phainon admitted as he looked at that man before blinking his eyes and looking at the bonfire instead. Kephale couldn’t be seen anymore, wrapped up by Mydei and burned too much for Phainon to be able to see him through the blaze - and yet, it stung his eyes to see it all the same. 

“Then there’s no need for you to be formal with it like a knight would,” Mydei pointed out in that same delicate tone, as if he was more than a little worried for Phainon’s fraying mind now, “Speak to him like you are his son, one last time.” 

“I was not.. Formally his child, I just-”

“Phainon.” Mydei cut in, and that was enough for Phainon to bite his own tongue over it - very aware of the way he was dancing around with excuses. Running from facing it, even though.. 

This was his one chance to actually say good bye, wasn’t it? That thought felt suffocating as he pulled his lips into a small frown, blinking at the sky one last time before looking down again. 

“.. Alright,” That was all he said as he stood from his spot on that small bench - not thinking twice as he rose and immediately walked past Mydei with a heavy heart. Unable to stop himself from nervously glancing at that prince who only offered such a somber smile on his lips to him. 

Phainon had to look away at that, his feet pausing a bit away from those logs that were crackling with embers and ruby red going through the veins of them through the fire’s burn. And now.. Phainon finally had to stand there and face them himself.

“Kephale, I..” Phainon tried to figure out his thoughts, but they all felt too tangled - a string around his throat pulling him back tightly. All while he had to try his best to continue onwards,  “I told you many times how thankful I was that you gave me a chance to live in this world after.. I lost everything.”

So many times he had told Kephale that, and so many times Kephale had chuckled and ruffled Phainon’s hair a little. Laughing a little over how he would have saved him every single time, even if Phainon had no desire ever to stay by his side. Kephale was a man who had always comforted and reassured Phainon, a man who always knew what to say when he needed to..

And now Phainon.. 

What was Phainon supposed to say now?

What was he supposed to say at this man’s funeral who he had grown to love as if he were Phainon’s actual father? What could he say to fully explain away the shake in his bones and the way his heart still felt anguish as if it were alive? How could he tell his father how deeply he had denied him being dead, and instead prayed they could free him from the lich?

How could he confess all that, when his mouth could barely function? When his words could barely pass through his lips with a voice behind them and not merely a scratch of sorrowful emotions peeling through his body? 

His years of hoping for the best for them all.. And now he.. 

Phainon could only move his eyes to stare at the flickers of that fire - the smallest of smiles on his lips as he forced himself to speak; “.. I just wanted you to get a happy ending, that’s all.”

Phainon found himself merely standing there after those words - his mouth opened and closed, yet no words actually left his lips now that his quiet wish had been spoken. Not even the quietest of sounds as his eyes staring at that man who he had loved as if they were truly related - a man that had practically raised him and doted on him while allowing him to live that fantasy of being his ‘knight’. 

Of trusting his adoptive father, through and through, and now he had to watch him be used as some kind of puppet - some tool, and then burnt to nothingness.

Was he supposed to feel so.. Oddly empty? He didn’t even know, but either way his throat closed on him - allowing no other words to be said, and maybe that was fine.

The way he turned and didn’t dare look at that prince who was a mere few feet away had to be fine as well, especially as his head instead found Mydei’s shoulder without wasting a single moment. His own arms snaked around Mydei’s waist to hold him there, an action that was oddly reciprocated as Mydei moved hands to pet into Phainon’s hair.

Gentle and tender, inviting and nonjudgemental - merely a kind reassurance that Mydei was with him, and if that was the case.. Even Phainon could be vulnerable, just for this one moment, just for tonight with only his prince to see him. 

In the silence of the world around them, while the only sound to comfort them was the bonfire setting Kephale to rest; that was perhaps the first time Phainon had finally cried over his own losses.

──────────────

“What is the plan now, Mydeimos?”

Phainon asked in a light-hearted tone, though he didn’t feel very at ease. Not actually, at least.

How could he?

They had slain that man and ended his reign, sure, but he still felt horrible dread over if he truly was himself. Finding himself unable to truly rest and instead, most of his time was spent standing on guard and keenly watching Mydei. Taking care of Mydei and seeing it through that the man was taking decent care of himself.

After all, that’s what Mydei deserved, he deserved to be pampered and doted on by a knight after getting vengeance for not just one kingdom, but two.

Yet, there was something more to it all. An odd distance between them both that Phainon was finding himself more and more privy to. As if Mydei was focused on something else, and was doing his best to retract himself from Phainon; not that he minded. 

He had sworn an oath to Mydei, and he would uphold it even if Mydei became more distant. That.. Was fine, so long as they were together, Phainon could deal with those festering emotions as they came and went. 

“The answer is obvious,” Mydei mumbled out, making Phainon move a little to stand behind Mydei at his desk in that small cave they called their home - his own eyes flitting to those eerie green lanterns before focusing on what Mydei was writing, “I am the one who slaughtered Aedes Elysiae and took control of their king.”

Phainon’s eyes didn’t even get a chance to take in the odd red letting on the paper Mydei was holding - his eyes dipping to that pen in Mydei’s hand as he instead moved even closer to the side of Mydei. Close enough to finally be able to peer into those golden eyes that merely looked right back at him with a feigning of innocence surrounding them. 

He couldn’t even stop the word that came to his head over that statement from falling freely from his own lips; “.. What?”

“I’ve pondered this for days, but it is the best outcome for your people who still live,” Mydei explained as he dipped his eyes back to that paper - making Phainon copy and stare at the rather fancy lettering there, “I will continue living as an outlaw and such a decree will allow other kingdoms to finally give them the aid they deserve.”

That.. Sounded insane to Phainon’s ears as Mydei was innocent, yet he was going to.. Take the fall for it all? Was it not more simple to try to explain it, or was it too far-fetched?

.. Was Mydei’s reputation so much more tainted than he had truly ever considered, and people would not even buy into the possibility that he was innocent? Was him being the sole Kremnoan survivor its own death sentence, then? 

“Where will we go as exiles, then?” Phainon asked, and something about that made Mydei pause - just the slightest amount, the briefest time all before he cocked his head to Phainon.

“.. We?” Mydei echoed out before sighing, shaking that same blond head of hair before looking at his work in progress letter and tapping his quill on the paper idly,  “Right.. We.. We will merely roam the world, I imagine.”

Phainon didn’t like that.

Something about it felt off, as if Mydei was doing his best to avoid this topic - running from it, almost, and yet Phainon had no idea how to bring it up.. Instead, he could only grit his teeth and look at the way Mydei was lacking his gloves. 

Red ink.

No gloves.

Those things paired together were never something Phainon found himself happy to see, especially as his eyes moved over those already scarred fingers languidly. 

“What.. Are you doing now?” Phainon asked, though his eyes were already semi-scanning that parchment to read it.

A proclamation claiming to have ruined Aedes Elysiae himself, so bold and demanding, a mocking thing.. And yet it only made Phainon’s stomach curl uncomfortably when he remembered it all was a simple lie.
