A foolish thing that Mydei was saying to allow other people’s lives to become easier at the cost of his own comfort.

Forever running away from people who may recognize him, and yet.. Mydei was so self sacrificing that he appeared barely even bothered by the idea of it. 

“Writing a letter using my own blood.” Mydei answered so easily, as if it was the most logical thing in the world - only.

Phainon found himself sighing loudly over it; “.. You know I hate how you do that.”

“It’s much more imposing and demonic to send a letter written in blood, especially when they’re assuming it is not my own.” Mydei mumbled without missing a single beat of the conversation - not allowing it to lull for even the briefest of times, as if he had fully been expecting such a question.

And maybe he was, since Phainon did often bring it up - that was enough to make Phainon click his tongue before huffing loudly; “.. We should start using animal blood, I don’t like the amount of scars on your hands.”

“No one sees my hands, anyway. They’re always in my gauntlets for that very reason.” Mydei argued against that point, and that was enough to make Phainon drag a hand to the bridge of his nose and pinch it tiredly.

Trying to protect a king that was causing more harm to himself than anyone else ever could, really. 

Moreso, Phainon found himself upset at those words; “.. I see them.”

It was more than just seeing them, it was the fact that he had to live with the knowledge that Mydei was in pain. That Mydei was doing this to himself, even if he would grumble about the reasons behind it and how it didn’t hurt - wasn’t it still cruel? Or was Phainon over thinking what goes on in a necromancer’s mind..?

“Then look away from them, next time,” Mydei grumbled out, sounding less than amused as he shook his head slowly over Phainon’s chiding buzzing in his ears.  All before he looked to Phainon with the slightest tilt of his head, “Regardless, you should rest, Phainon.”

“.. My body doesn’t actually need sleep, you know that,” Phainon huffed as he looked away from that man - he knew fully well what Mydei was implying to him, but he just.. He had so much to think about, as of late.

His fear of that lich being buried in his mind was haunting him, lingering there and crawling through his thoughts constantly - but it served one purpose decently well.. It did however distract him from the hollow feeling of his father truly being gone now.

“Your mind does, however,” Mydei countered, making him flit his eyes back to that necromancer to bite into his gums a little while looking at him returning to his writing idly,  “You haven’t allowed yourself to sleep since we returned home from Kephale.”

Phainon swallowed over that; “I..” 

“It’s alright, I swore to you; did I not?” Mydei asked in a rather gentle tone of voice, “If you truly become corrupted, I will put you to rest, I promised you that.”

Phainon.. Wasn’t sure whether to laugh or to cry at the way Mydei was choosing not to bring up the funeral and how long Phainon had stayed with his head buried into Mydei’s shoulder. Instead focusing on the fact he had been freaked out over the lich’s grip and honestly.. He wasn’t wrong for it, anyway. 

“Rest, your mind needs the break from the mental anguish it’s assuredly under..” Mydei told him, moving a little to blink his amber eyes upwards at Phainon a bit innocently, “Staying up and taking vigil to watch me sleep is undoubtedly sweet, and expected of my knight; but if your mind becomes so frayed that you cannot function, what knightly duties can you even perform?”

Too innocent, even. So innocent that Phainon felt his thoughts stalling as that man sat there blinking at Phainon with heavy and dazzling golden eyelashes - looking much too sweet for a man who had done fleshcraft in his life and commanded the undead.

.. But Phainon was probably a weak willed man in general when it came to Mydei, moving a little to sigh - his head dipping to the side all while feeling the phantom ghost of his skin burning under the stare. 

“I will.. Rest for just a bit, alright?” Phainon conceded, not feeling strong enough to refuse that man right now - pursing his lips in a tiny little pout as he felt an eerie sinking sense of dread crawling into him. 

One that, really, he couldn’t comprehend why it was becoming such a pit in his soul - not when he was just going to sleep.. Did he fear the vulnerability of his mind turning off for just a short time period that he really did think if he slept the lich would claim his mind? 

“Mhm..” Mydei hummed, returning back to his work lazily - and with that, Phainon really wasn’t sure if he was going insane or not.. If Mydei wasn’t worried about it, why should Phainon be? After all, Mydei would know better than he would, and yet he was still pushing for Phainon to sleep.

He had to hang his head a little and sigh dejectedly the more he thought on it - instead turning on heel to walk away with a lazy wave over his shoulder to the man who was still watching him, studying him even. 

“Good night, Mydeimos.”

“.. Good bye, Phainon.”

Phainon paused his steps over that - tilting his head to the side just the slightest bit as he tried to understand why that sounded so odd to him. Bizarre, even. A bit.. Off, even. Even Mydei’s voice sounded like it had a twinge of sadness laced into it now - one that made Phainon crease his brows with a bite of his gums.

It felt as if he was missing something, but the most he could force himself to do was sigh heavily over it. If Mydei wanted some time alone, he would allow him just that - instead moving into their bedroom to collapse onto the soft wool of their bed with an exhale leaving his useless lungs. Rolling over a little to tug off his own shirt and sit up slightly, just enough to look at that scar that ran through his chest idly - fingers slowly tracing over the mess of flesh there. 

All before looking to his arm as well, that spot where he had taken an arrow for Mydei had never quite healed up - instead Mydei had sewn his skin together while mumbling something about needing to learn a better healing skill for those who are already dead. Something about his skin being unable to heal itself anymore, and he should be more careful lest his guts fall out of him like a stuffed animal’s stuffing. 

Though, all he could do now was curl up into their bed and finally let sleep take him - doing his best not to think about how Mydei could be attacked right now without him. He hadn’t sent that letter out yet, no one would be after him as of right now, and yet.. That familiar dread was hard to bite down as he forced his eyes closed - shakily sighing as he allowed sleep to crawl into him regardless. 

“This is my true good bye to you, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae,” Phainon felt his hand twitch at those words - yet his eyes remained closed as he felt himself slipping back into that darkness, “May you rest well now, and have a wonderful life.”

There was a soft feeling on his forehead at that - so gentle that he almost wrote the pressure off, feeling his mind mourning the lack of feeling he possessed as he gritted his teeth in his sleep. Strange, it was so very strange. 

“Thank you for being my knight, even if it was for just one mere battle. I’ll treasure the time we had together,” Those words were spoken so softly - as if the speaker didn’t want to stir Phainon from his slumber at all. As if they were trying to speak and leave without Phainon ever knowing they were truly there. 

“You deserve this second chance, and this is the most I can try to give to you.” That voice spoke to him as sweet as honey - and Phainon had to resist the urge to flip on his side and swat that voice alone. “A chance that cannot happen if I stay in your life any longer than necessary, so our path.. Splits here. You’ll be fine, I promise you that.”

All before he jolted up with a sense of dread - blinking in the dark room and scanning it quickly, focusing on that still burning lantern in the corner before tilting his head a little.

That was Mydeimos’s voice, he knew that much, but was that fake, or a dream?

He didn’t know, instead moving to yawn and rub at his head as he peered into the darkness of their shared home - swinging his feet off their bed before moving a little into their shabby living space. Staring around before huffing a little.

“Mydei? Are you.. here?” Phainon called, and it wasn’t strange to not get a reply - Mydei liked to do most of his work outside. 

Phainon paused to listen, all before sighing a little and getting dressed for his day - even though he was unable to shake those words from his mind; it was fine. He just needed to go find Mydei in the forest clearing or by the river to help him dissuade those thoughts.

That was what he told himself as he strapped his sword on to his back and tugged his boots on, a smile dancing on his lips as he moved out of that familiar place they both called home. Every step was as light as possible as he moved his eyes upwards to peer at the sky - blinking at the light that was beaming through the leaves as he breathed out a steady sigh.

The world felt so much more peaceful for him now as he walked, no longer dreading the shadow that was being cast by that lich - instead replaced by the sunshine and the pure curiosity in his heart over where Mydei and himself would head off to next.

“Mydeimos?” Phainon expectantly called out in that familiar clearing where he had found Mydei reading so many times before with undead scurrying the forest.

And yet, there was no one here. 

Phainon clicked his tongue over that, instead moving a bit quicker to the river nearby where they both bathe - steps feeling less light. Hurried, now, as if a weird feeling of dread was sinking into his body, clawing into him and becoming more and more unwilling to leave.

And that feeling only became worsened by the sight of no one there, either.

There were no traces of Mydei, no traces of that necromancer around or his undead, it was as if.. Mydei had purposefully left him.

That was a haunting thought, really, as Phainon’s feet immediately began to move to that path he and Mydei had traveled so many times before. All to pause as he reached it and stare towards the way to Aedes Elysiae.. Would Mydei head that way? He doubted it, what was left of that kingdom for either of them?

Phainon didn’t know, not really, only finding himself walking that road with a rather brisk pace - feeling that sinking pit in his stomach get even deeper as he thought on it more and more. 

The reality that those words weren’t from a dream; that Mydei himself had been saying them and leaving Phainon behind, leaving Phainon alone in this world without him and Phainon.. Really didn’t know what to do if that was the case.

He had desired to be that man’s knight for the rest of his life, to stand by his side and protect him so that Mydei could live a long full life unlike he himself had. That one of them could live and be happy; that..

He could be happy.

That Phainon could find his happiness with the only man that had made him smile in such a painfully long time, even if he was dead, he still felt happiest with Mydei. Happier than he had while alive and struggling, happier than he had in such a long time..

And now Mydei.. Was trying to leave him? 

Phainon really couldn’t wrap his mind around that - not as he hurried his steps and found himself gritting his teeth more and more as he briskly walked. Every step was in a direction that he was unsure of, a direction that could, or could not lead him right to Mydeimos. 

And yet, he had to continue walking regardless of that fact - quickly moving to try to search for the man he cherished more than anyone else now. The person that had given him a reason to continue walking and moving on in this eternal torment he called his undying life. 

He could only pray that he was lucky in his life for once; that his feet would lead him to Mydei and that he wouldn’t have to feel his sinking feeling for long. That every step he took was bringing him closer to the man who seemed to genuinely believe self-sacrificing whatever happiness he had would make Phainon happier in the long run.

.. It wouldn’t, Phainon already knew that much from how twisted his guts felt - from how desperately he wanted to bend his body in half and retch up his lunch.. And he didn’t even eat anymore. 

This felt agony - as if he was being tortured for crimes he didn’t even know which he committed, every step making him feel more and more confused. Should he go back? Would Mydei be the other way? How could he ever possibly know without going back and checking that way as well, yet then Mydei could be even further away from him?

Those were the thoughts rolling around in his head as he stayed on this path - eyes facing forward as he borderline jogged and waited to see someone else. Anyone else; if it was Mydei, he could corner him here and now, if it was someone else he could ask if they had seen that man with blazing hair that couldn’t be confused for another.

He didn’t know how long he was practically running for - nor did he think he cared considering his body didn’t need to rest. All before he finally saw someone else in the distance, someone in front of him on that dusty path that made his stopped heart beat again effortlessly. 

Phainon could barely control the jittery feeling in his body as he neared that man who seemed to almost be leisurely taking a stroll - almost. His pace was assuredly quicker than normal, all before Phainon found himself unable to keep himself silent anymore. Hands twitching at his side all before he moved closer after that blond haired man, staring at those familiar flaming locks as they both walked. 

“Mydeimos,” Phainon growled out - all to watch the way Mydei’s feet stopped at that, not turning around yet in the trade of sighing. Inaudible to Phainon, yet the obvious sink of his shoulders and a shake of his head was impossible to miss, especially as Mydei tilted his head upwards a little. Enough to make those stray blond hairs move slightly over it.

“Phainon,” Mydei breathed out, finally turning just a bit to give Phainon a rather somber looking smile - once that appeared as if he hadn’t been expecting Phainon to chase him down, “You woke up quickly.”

Phainon felt his own jaw twitch in annoyance over that - a flick in his muscles over how easily Mydei was talking to him. As if this was an outcome he almost had expected, yet had been running from.

It drove Phainon insane to try to comprehend.

All while he tried to convince himself to stay calm; to stay level as he spoke; “Where do you think you’re going?”

Mydei made a heavy sighing noise over that - his eyes flicking to the side, taking in the sight of trees that they both knew so well having had walked this path together so many times before. A path that Mydei now was attempting to break away from, to walk away from Phainon forever, instead of being each other’s solace in this world like Phainon had hoped for.

Though, Mydei only looked back to him, keeping that particularly sad smile on his lips - one that seemed to be pleading for forgiveness, all while he refused to actually show that level of vulnerability to Phainon. 

“.. Surely you can understand my perspective here, Phainon.”

“I don’t and I can’t,” Phainon supplied without missing a single moment, tossing his head into a tilted position as he kept his eyes transfixed on Mydei, “I’m just a loyal knight who loves to serve, explain it to me in a way I can understand.”

Mydei was silent over that - a long period of time that seemed to stretch for minutes in Phainon’s mind as he rolled his wrists a little. Feeling more and more antsy towards this man who seemed to be doing his best to avoid this. 

All for some second chance at life for Phainon, one that Mydei seemed to have deemed impossible if he remained in his life. 

.. But there was no true second chance at life for Phainon, not in his world if Mydei wasn’t in that life; Not in his world if he couldn’t spend his time with the man who had made him happy, even while dead. This was the life he wanted, one with Mydei, and he wasn’t ready to let go of that at all, nor did he think he ever would be.

“.. You’re not a fool. I’m not sure why you desire that.” Mydei grumbled out after a few more heavy seconds of Phainon balling his hands into fists and twitching them. 

Not out of annoyance towards the man, no. He was as patient towards Mydei as possible, however patient Mydei needed him to be. The emotion causing him to act so oddly was undoubtedly his own anxiety, making him antsy and jerky in his movements as he tried to figure out what to do here. 

“Explain it to me regardless. I want to hear it from your own mouth, Mydei.” Phainon mumbled as he forced the shake in his hands to cease - gritting his teeth a little as he did his best to control himself.

To control his urges that yelled at him to cross the distance and hold onto that man, to grip him and never let go; a desire that he knew was impossible to truly act out on, though.. Maybe he could allow himself to indulge that desire, just the tiniest of bits, metaphorically. 

“This is the best outcome possible,” Mydei reasoned before moving to cross his arms over his chest with a shake of his head; all movements that Phainon had grown so painfully used to seeing, “I will leave, and you can begin your new life.”

Phainon couldn’t even stop the scoff that left his throat over that, threatening to choke him as he came fully to terms that the dream he had. Those words Mydei had spoken to him were all so dreadfully real - a lucid nightmare becoming his horrible nightmare now. 

“.. Leave?” Phainon echoed out, barely able to stop the disbelief from leaking into his words as he strained himself to utter them. Doing his best to force himself to stay sane in this conversation - all while  feeling himself rapidly unraveling at the seams the more he considered actually losing this man that was standing before him. 

“Disappear,” Mydei answered rather flippantly, as if it didn’t matter at all and this wasn’t the worst idea Phainon had ever heard  of.

Ever. 

And he had been a knight for many years, he had heard of some really bad plans from other guards and such in his free time.

“I’m not very fond of this outcome, Mydei.” Phainon confessed with a cold chuckle leaving his chest as he shook his head a little - all before moving to drag a hand through his hair with a shaky exhale leaving his chest. One that left him feeling more than a little hollow as he didn’t dare to look away from Mydei, almost scared that the man would try to bolt away.

Yet, Mydei only remained standing there, even moving one hand to wave at him rather dismissively. 

“Your life was cut off short, and with that man dead, you can still go out and live whatever life you desire.” Mydei told him in such a stern voice - lacking any and all humor, all before he added a little chuckle to it; “My life ended months ago.”

Phainon wanted to comment on that, to try to comfort the man; but he knew fully well what Mydei was implying here.

His life had ended when Kremnos fell. 

“.. That’s cruel of you to say, Mydei.” Was all Phainon could manage to say, knitting his brows together as he instead tried to focus on anything but the agony Mydei must still feel, “The life I desire is by your side, always near you, and you just want to.. Disappear?”

Even if Mydei had nothing; Even if there was nothing for him to return to.. Phainon couldn’t let him leave him behind, because who else could understand Mydei better than the man who also had nothing left?

They were supposed to be each other’s solace and support in this lonely world, Phainon fully understood that now, but how.. How was he supposed to convince Mydei of that? 

This entire situation was enough to make Phainon’s blood boil (if only he had any). As much as he understood where Mydei was coming from, what he couldn’t stomach was the idea of himself failing. If he actually failed here, if Mydei did cut him off and leave his side forever.

.. Would Phainon really be able to move on with his life, or would he find himself chasing after Mydei’s shadow for the rest of his existence? 

“Don’t you dare act as if it’s for my own good, either. I won’t allow it.” Phainon found himself growling out, unable to stop the venom leaking into his words as he continued to consider his own insanity if this man truly slipped away from him.

Only, there was an easy answer to all of this - wasn’t there? A simple one, as simple as the sword sheathed on his back, one that made his hand move to its hilt in a smooth and quickened movement as he pulled it free. Exhaling a shaky breath that was hollow as he kept his eyes trained on that man who tilted his head to the side. Golden eyes watching Phainon’s blade with rather blatant curiosity seeping through his expression now.

A blade that Phainon wasn’t afraid to use against Mydeimos, just like old times, and just once more; “Draw your blade, Mydeimos.”

Mydei only seemed to straighten himself out a little, standing taller - slightly more on edge as his eyes took in the sight of that familiar blade all before looking back to Phainon, “.. Phainon.”

His name in that accent from Mydei was something he had never truly gotten used to, always liking the sound of Mydei saying his name just a little bit more than anyone else due to it and he wasn’t sure if he was right in his mind for that or not.

But it was his emotion for this man, and his alone; that made it such a precious thing to himself.. 

Either way, he only remained there with his sword in hand, all before extending the blade towards Mydei - narrowing his eyes and convincing himself to take this as seriously as he could.

“I demand a duel with the prince of Kremnos,” Phainon explained in a gruff and haughty tone, “A duel for his hand in marriage, and to bind our lives together for the rest of eternity.”

All of his words made himself feel more and more anxious - nervous as he stared and waited for Mydei to draw his own sword and begin the duel. Yet, Mydei instead gave Phainon a stare as if he had grown a second head, eyes going wide with his now blatant shock over those words. 

“.. Have you gone mad?” That question was asked by Mydeimos in such an incredulous tone that Phainon couldn’t help but huff a little laugh at it. A grin breaking onto his lips as he tried to steady the slight shake in his hand that still was holding his blade towards the man he loved the most. 

“Would the great prince of Kremnos truly be so cowardly as to refuse a royal duel? Have you no honor?” Phainon asked in a mocking tone, fully aware that his own words were hollow - though they seemed to do enough to make Mydei’s jaw clench rather visibly.

Always the defender of his pride and honor as a Kremnoan, even now, and Phainon understood him better than anyone else in this world; of course he knew what buttons to press on that man to anger him. 

“Draw your blade,” Phainon found himself growling out again, making demands to the man he considered his king, and more so the owner of his heart felt devious - but he was beyond desperate here, “I will show you how deep my devotion to you goes, how deep my desire for you is buried into my soul.”

Mydei didn’t budge over that - still appearing a bit perturbed, but still having his lingering shock on his expression. As if he didn’t quite understand the situation and how it was truly unfolding before the both of them now.

“Draw your blade, and allow me to show you my love for you runs through my veins in every swing of my sword I may take in your name,” Phainon hissed out every word, unable to stop the odd venom in his voice that was burning against his tongue, “Duel me, and become my king forever, Mydeimos.”

He loved Mydeimos.

He loved that king of Castrum Kremnos that had lost everything, just like Phainon. He loved the way the corner of his eyes wrinkled the tiniest of bits when Mydei laughed. He loved the way that man idly would grab at his own braid and undo it, just to rebraid it when he was nervous. He loved the way Mydei faced things head on, even if he was uncomfortable.

.. So why was Mydei doing his best to run from Phainon, this one last time? 

Mydei only huffed over that, shaking his head a bit from side to side in disapproval as his arms rested over each other - staring daggers into Phainon’s own mind silently; “And what if you are to lose, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae?”

“I won’t lose,” Phainon told him with a little laugh, feeling a smile creeping onto his lips over the question, “Because you, too, want me to stay by your side.”

That did enough to make Mydei’s frown flinch just a tiny bit - barely even noticeable as he moved a little - enough to withdraw his own sword with a heavy chuckle leaving his own lips after a moment. 

“You’re foolish to assume I would go easy on you in a formal duel for such a petty reason,” Mydei pointed out in a tone that almost sounded like he was offended - but only almost. Nothing more, his volume instead dropping in a way that made Phainon quite sure he had gotten his guess correct.

“No,” Phainon growled out, feeling his hands tighten on his sword he knew so well,  “I have assumed no such thing, in fact, I crave you to fight me with your full strength and put me in my place. After all; I am also your most loyal knight, begging for your attention.”

His eyes moved down to the blade of his own sword - a sword that had been tainted and given a new purpose at Mydei’s side, and now.. Now he had to raise it against Mydeimos to make him fully understand the depths of his love for him, and a piece of him thought that was perfectly fine.

They had met through fighting and trying to kill each other, Phainon could confess his love through fighting and doing his best to make Mydei lose that battle. Anything, if it meant they would stay together - even if it was raising his sword against the man he would protect by giving as many lives as he could for him.

“Show me the strength of my king, Mydeimos. So that I can know how much more I need to revere you,” Phainon was practically panting out his words - unable to stop how excited he already felt by Mydei having his blade in hand. 

A showing that he was going to accept this duel, and whatever came after it..

“Very well,” Mydei said in a rather grandeur tone - moving a little to pop his neck to the side before lowering himself in that pose of battle he knew was signature to Mydei and Mydei alone, “I accept your duel, Phainon, do not disappoint me.”

“My entire life is yours, Mydeimos, I would never do anything to allow you to falter let alone have myself fall short of your expectations,” Phainon retorted in his voice that he knew was as if he was taking a vow once more.

He didn’t mind - he would do anything for Mydei, even if it was to fight that man down and make sure he finally understood just how much he meant to Phainon.. He would do it.

“.. You’re already dead.” Mydei reminded him with a rather egregious look, one that seemed wholly unimpressed and Phainon.. Phainon found himself whimpering a little over that. 

His head hanging dejectedly as he gripped at his sword, “Can you let me have a moment here?”

“Sorry.”

Phainon shook his head over that - resisting the urge to laugh it over because this.. Was a deeply serious matter to Phainon. This was nothing he could laugh at, not when Mydei was so desperate to escape him for whatever reason he was assuming in his head. Not when Mydei was undervaluing just how much he meant to Phainon.

This was a battle of Phainon’s love and devotion for the man who was now stanced up just as much as he was. Just as ready for a battle that he had not seen coming, but Phainon..

Phainon just wanted Mydei to know how dearly loved he truly was. 

“Are you ready, Mydeimos?” Phainon calmly asked, even though his bones felt anything but calm - they felt as if they were shaking beneath his undead flesh. Trembling as he stayed there fully prepared to fight this necromancer just like they once had, all while the goal was completely different..

“Of course,” Mydei smoothly replied, “You may strike when you’re ready.”

Mydei spoke those words, and Phainon found himself unable to do anything but stand there taking in the sight of that man - always finding his posture the most bizarre fighting stance. And yet, he knew it now to be so painfully Mydei - strong and respectable, forceful and powerful in all of his movements.

Precise, a keen hunter and warrior as he cocked his head to the side with a rather coy expression on his lips - waiting for Phainon to strike at him, wholly unaware that he had easily struck first at the undead man with his own beauty. Phainon couldn’t even bring himself to look away from that man, feeling a bit dazed over how bulky he truly was.

Even if Phainon had seen him display his prowess many times before, for some reason, now it felt different. More relaxed, calm, as if he had been preparing himself for this fight with Phainon and was more than a little willing to engage him in combat. Though, they had fought many times before; this was still so painfully different.

Of course, Phainon knew it was different for himself for so many different reasons.

The most important and obvious reason on his mind was easy to digest; He was hopelessly in love with the man named Mydeimos who stood a mere few feet away from him, holding Phainon’s entire future and only chance at a happy ending in the palm of his hand. 

That was reason enough for Phainon’s own grip on the hilt of his blade to steady - to become as firm as possible as he lowered his eyes to his familiar sword. The weapon he had reclaimed and felt at peace with again, now being raised against the man who he had loved more than anyone else. 

Yet that was fine, after all, to Mydei; this was a form of love as well? A way for Phainon to proclaim his love for him and do his best to prove how deep and carnal his love went for Mydei.. 

Phainon found himself moving at those thoughts, unable to even think twice as he instead lunged at that king that he treasured so much. All to put his emotions into his blade that was last used by himself all those months ago to fight Mydeimos all the same - a clash of heavy steel and metal against another.

.. And it only made Phainon feel so painfully alive to hear metal clinking and scratching so loudly together as Mydei didn’t miss a single beat - easily parrying him and retaliating with his own attack without missing a beat, his sword barely missing Phainon by a hair. So close that Phainon could hear the swing of metal pass him by with a small laugh leaving his throat.

He shouldn’t laugh, he shouldn’t enjoy it, and yet - he was beaming. Staring at his beloved’s face who was only smiling right back at him, a toothy grin that reminded Phainon just of who he was actually fighting.

Even if their swords were clashing in such a harsh way that it rattled Phainon’s bones - it only seemed to make Mydei come all the more to life. Fiery and beautiful in the heat of battle to where Phainon felt so jittery, thrilled that he could be the cause of Mydei’s joy in such an unbridled way.

“You fight like your life is on the line!” Mydei said in a voice that was much too airy - too light-hearted and playful for the way his blade was lashing out to match Phainon’s, actions that didn’t match up with his words and only served to make Phainon feel even fuzzier in his head over how deep his admiration for this man went. 

“It is, Mydeimos,” Phainon tried to rival his words back, feeling as if it were nigh impossible to resist smiling along with that king who now was attacking him so freely, “You are the only thing I have left.. I won’t let you leave me behind!”

He meant his words - even if they were unhealthy or codependent, he meant them as deeply as he could. Doing his best to study Mydei so closely now, his posture in fights had always been strange - more feral and unrestrained than someone who had formal sword fighting teachings, but maybe that was on purpose.

A prince who had his own style of fighting on the battlefield was much more terrifying than those who strove to remain rigid and uptight in their movements. 

“My devotion to you is laced in every swing, every attempt to knock you down,” Phainon growled out - for once feeling so very thankful that he didn’t need air as he watched the way he could see Mydei’s chest rising so harshly.

If anything, he almost feared that their blades matched in combat and that it would be some stick competition of stamina.. Especially as Mydei seemed to perfectly match him in their dance of movements, effortlessly keeping up even as Phainon desperately wanted that man to mess up - somehow.. 

Phainon couldn’t hold himself back from talking even more between inching forward to try to break the man’s defensives, “You said you respected and admired both my perseverance and devotion, so I can only do my best to put them on display more for my king to hear that praise again.”

Mydei’s expression didn’t falter, clearly more entertained by the ongoing battle than allowing Phainon to get into his mind and make him stumble with his words. Instead, Mydei only seemed to grin a bit more wickedly at him - as if he was becoming more and more amused by it all. 

“You are th-” Phainon nearly bit into his tongue as he watched Mydei throw his sword to the side - his head watching it skid across the dirt before tilting his head a little, unable to understand it,  “.. Huh?”

He almost thought it was.. Mydei forfeiting, for the briefest of moments Phainon’s mind was spiraling to comprehend why he would do such a thing. That wasn’t the victory Phainon sought - yet.. Instead, Phainon found himself choking a little, side stepping to avoid the way that man.. Was trying to punch him instead. Completely abandoning his sword in favor of his clawed gauntlets he had always kept on himself.

That was even more insane to Phainon as he felt himself move his sword out of sheer instincts to slash at the man - feeling his mind race over how Mydei couldn’t defend himself.

Only for Mydei to grab the damn blade with that crazed tooth grin on his lips.

.. Phainon was assuredly in love with this man, he knew that much as he felt how tight those hands were on his sword, struggling a little to yank it free from the man who moved instantly towards him to try to throw a punch as Phainon moved to keep his stance corrected over his sword being stuck for a moment. 

Even as Phainon worked to dance and parry those new insane frenzied attacks - Phainon had no real idea what to make of this duel.

He knew it was an important one, but he surely hadn’t expected Mydei to just be.. Trying to punch him shitless?! Were Kremnoan duels really with just whatever weapons they desired?!

Furthermore, why did Phainon keep feeling his teeth chattering when that man’s fist met with his blade - as if the shock and strength of his fists ran through his entire body and up to his jaw? Every single hit felt like if Phainon was still alive, his body would have been grounded into a fine dust with the weight of Mydei’s strength - even if he had an inkling they were actually well matched he.. He couldn’t help but to admire it. 

Admiring the way Mydei moved was one thing - he was as agile as a feline striking to kill their prey in one foul attack. Admiring the way Mydei was so quickly able to dip and dodge away from Phainon’s blade, or parry it with a force that made Phainon feel the air leave his lungs.. And he didn’t even need air in them to begin with. 

Everything about this man was perfect, from the way he fought, to the smile on his lips while his hair seemed to burn and blaze a path behind him. He was utterly stunning and Phainon.. Really should focus more on those clawed hands - just barely dancing away from another outreached claw that felt like it could easily rip his skin from his bones. 

“Mydeimos,” Phainon breathed out as he blocked another rampaging fist, feeling the way his body wanted to surrender, and yet.. His mind only had one thought every single time he saw Mydei lunge for him with such power and ferocity, “I love you.”

Those words seemed to be enough to make Mydei’s eyes widen - for his claws to stall their attack just a little, and Phainon felt almost cruel for it. Cruel for the way he took that opening without waiting for a single second, instead full body tackling that man - his whole weight slamming into Mydei’s chest to topple that fist-fighting necromancer. 

It was too precious of a moment for Phainon to give up, too rare that he had to abuse to win that fight and slam Mydei to the ground - he would feel more guilty later. But for now, he had to take whatever victory he could with that man. 

Mydei chest rose and fell so quickly now that he was stunned and lying there. Beneath Phainon on the floor, all with Phainon’s blade near his neck - claiming his victory and hesitating there as a silent threat for the prince if he dared to try to consider fighting. Though, it wasn’t as if Phainon had been fighting to claim Mydei’s life.. Well..

Not in the way Mydei would normally expect, at least. 

“This is my win, Mydeimos.” Phainon breathed those words out, moving his knees in the dirt and grass just a tiny bit. Enough to trap that man beneath him even more as he watched Mydei pant and blink upwards at him.

His face was rather muted, absolved of any true emotions as he remained laying there in defeat. Clearly waiting for whatever Phainon had decided to do with his win as he breathed out a quiet chuckling sound. 

“..Due to your cruel tricks.. But, It would seem so.”

Cruel.

Cruel tricks? There was no true trick there, he did love Mydei.. But.. He had to remain silent as he gave a quiet huff over Mydei conceding that he had won this battle. 

Phainon didn’t waste a single moment before moving to throw his sword to the side - watching the way Mydei’s eyes flicked to the side to watch it go. Blinking a little before turning his head to focus on Phainon above him all while Phainon was already digging into his own pockets. Seeking out something he had picked up while in town one day with Mydei.

It was a mindless thing, a movement that he had done without a second thought, really. All because he felt himself yearning for it as he looked at them. 

Phainon moved swiftly to grab at Mydei’s right hand, navigating his own fingers to remove Mydei’s gauntlet without sparring a single moment as he slid that small little golden ring around the man’s ring finger. Basking in the way it seemed to be a perfect fit, and the way Mydei had gone stiff under him - appearing frozen by the action. 

“What is.. That?” Mydei asked in a hushed tone, as if he was completely baffled over what he was feeling - but Phainon knew fully well that man knew what it was.

After all, his eyes were locked on where their hands both were, staring at his own fingers and that band of glimmering metal that was now safely around his ring finger. 

Phainon found himself unable to stop a smile from growing on his lips fondly over that shocked reaction from him; “A ring.”

“A ring?”

“A marriage ring, to be more precise. But yes, a ring,” Phainon purred out as he slowly threaded their fingers together - all before bringing Mydei’s hand to his lips to kiss that ring that was now sitting beautifully on his hand, forevermore; “You have one now to match my own, isn’t that romantic?”

Phainon couldn’t help himself but chuckle just a tiny bit quietly - feeling it bubble out of himself as he kept their hands together, lowering them slowly. All to drag his free hand to Mydei’s face, tenderly rubbing at the man’s cheekbone and savoring the way Mydei didn’t even wince from it. His eye didn’t close at all, instead, he appeared completely trusting in the gesture as Phainon lowered himself even more. 

“This was a fight for your hand in marriage, after all, Mydei. So you’re mine now since I’ve won this duel.” Phainon was barely whispering his words out, smiling all the while and staring into those golden flaked eyes that seemed to shine and glimmer in the light. Practically glowing, all while Phainon moved his face just a little bit closer to Mydei’s own on the ground. 

Mydei remained quiet for a moment, just the briefest of time before he flashed a small grin to Phainon and barked out a laugh over it - and Phainon almost felt like a fool if not for the way Mydei seemed to be squeezing their hands together now tightly; “.. Have you gone truly mad?”

“No, I think I fell in love with you quite a while ago, even if I didn’t know the name for those feelings.” Phainon admitted with a little laugh, rubbing his fingers over the spot where Mydei once had a wound on his face - finding himself a little thankful that it had healed to be barely even existent, “But now, I can’t possibly say good bye to you like this, Mydei..”

Phainon felt achingly nervous as he spoke those words - feeling his own hand tighten on Mydei’s to try to ground himself. Praying that those soft golden eyes were welcoming towards him; sweet and endearing.

Instead, Mydei only leisurely blinked his eyes upwards at Phainon, letting him study the way those lashes glimmered in the sunlight, dazzling and almost nonexistent. All while Mydei looked a little confused, “Are you going to kiss me then? Usually a marriage is forged formally through a kiss.”

Phainon felt himself choke a little over that - doing his best to keep his mind on track as he studied the way that man was smiling, just a tiny bit, but that was enough to make Phainon’s heartbeat pound in his own ears.. And his heart didn’t even beat to begin with.

“You would let me?” Phainon asked, unable to help the way his voice sounded as if it wasn’t even meant for Mydei’s own ears. 

“You silly knight..” Mydei’s voice was equally as quiet - so much so that Phainon couldn’t help but blink wide confused eyes at him, “I would have let you kiss me ages ago, if you had desired.”

Phainon found himself grinning over that, immediately dipping his head down to press his own lips to Mydei - drinking in the way Mydei had immediately closed his eyes over it. So instantly allowing himself to enjoy their first kiss that Phainon almost felt off-balance, struggling for breath he didn’t even need as his hand tightened against Mydei’s own. 

He couldn’t help himself from gripping onto Mydei’s face a tiny bit harder as well, desperate to deeper than kiss - even if he couldn’t exactly feel it, that didn’t matter to  him. All he needed to know was the way Mydei was more than a little willing, eager, even to be kissing Phainon back. Sweetly pressing their lips together and happily accepting Phainon as his husband, and Phainon.. Couldn’t be any more gleeful than how he felt in this moment.

He was powerless to stop the smile on his lips as he tried to deepen that kiss, desperate to feel the warmth of that man - desperate to feel any piece of him as he gripped at Mydei’s skin. All before pulling away from him, just a breath away, but far away enough to put their foreheads together with a rather shaky breath from Mydei.

One that Phainon wished he could copy, yet, instead he could merely stare that man in the eyes and bask in the way those fierce burning eyes looked so much softer. Dull, dazed even as they stared right back into Phainon’s. 

“I’ll serve you until my bones become utter nothingness, Mydei. Dust in the wind, and my heart will still be yours.” Phainon spoke those words as sternly as possible - meaning every single word he was uttering as he tried his best to let that man know how deep his devotion truly went.

Only, Mydei gave a quiet little scoffing sound over that - a coy smile on his lips. 

“That’s quite the oath,” Mydei commented with a little hum in his throat, “Are you sure you can keep such a hefty promise to me, my knight?”

Hefty?

Phainon didn’t think it was hefty at all, if anything, this oath was the most freeing thing he could ever promise to this man. 

“Perhaps not as your knight, but as your husband I won’t fail you, beloved.” Phainon tried his best to reassure that man, all while still trying his best to mean every single word. Since well.. He did. 

Only, Mydei cocked his head to the side a little - the tiniest of bits considering Phainon still had their heads together and was straddling him to lock him onto the ground, “Will you get off of me and allow me to stand, then?”

“.. Ah..” 

To be honest, Phainon didn’t quite want to - and rather liked how beautiful Mydei was on the ground with his hair forming a rather fiery halo around him. Practically glowing in the sun and sparkling in a way that Phainon found himself so painfully fond of every time he looked at that necromancer. 

Still, Phainon practically scrambled to his feet over that - laughing a little as he moved to yank Mydei up as that man grabbed his discarded gauntlet  as well, doing his best to never let go of that man’s hand with a fond smile on his lips over the way.. Mydei seemed to be doing that as well. Keeping their hands connected all while slowly rising to his feet with a rather heavy sigh leaving his chest, a sigh that sounded exhausted, and yet.. Phainon found himself beaming to see such a small smile on Mydei’s lips as well. 

“Where are we going, anyway?” Phainon asked as he moved a little to cling to Mydei’s hand a bit more, savoring the way this man truly was his husband now; and kicking himself a little over the way Mydei seemed to have fallen for him, first. 

“.. I don’t know, I was planning on living a life of solitude, but..” Phainon didn’t miss the way Mydei seemed to take a moment, lifting their hands that were combined together a little before hearing that prince scoff quietly - as if he was amused by the fact they were still hand holding, “I believe the solitude has just been removed from the circumstance.”

“Mm,” Phainon hummed as he swung their hands a little, tightening his grip on Mydei’s but never tight enough to harm that man,“We should go see the world. Someone once told me there’s plenty of wonderful sights to see if you go out looking for them.”

“Did they? They sound rather wise,” Mydei replied a bit playfully, making Phainon bark out a little laugh over this man calling himself wise. Shaking his head a little over how they had practically uprooted their entire lives again. 

Mydei certainly wasn’t carrying anything - so it made Phainon a bit curious what his plans actually were, but it didn’t matter.. Not when he would be beside Mydei for all of it now, anyway. 

“Oh, I’m sure..” Phainon huffed out quietly, all before humming a little at his thoughts - head tilting a little to blink at the sky now that he was free to relax a little. A peace of mind that Mydei was beside him with that ring matching Phainon’s own..

“Now that we’re married, we should discuss how many children you want to start repopulating Castrum Kremnos!”

That was enough to make Mydei seem to stumble a little, as if he was about to trip but Phainon found himself laughing over that and immediately moving a little to catch the man if needed. Though, he was skilled enough to catch himself - and Phainon found himself enjoying the tightness on his own hand from Mydei gripping him for more support. 

“Phainon.. You’re dead, and we’re both males.” Mydei pointed out as he righted himself, straightening himself out with a heavy sigh - making Phainon give up on his own attempts to fight down his own smile. Instead moving to knock their shoulders together with another bubble of laughter.

Phainon couldn’t find himself at all bothered by those two points, because, after all..

“I’m dead and still able to marry the man of my dreams, so I would like to assume the children are still possible too.”

“Let’s stop talking for a while.”
